scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Replantation
question: How much is the unit cost for Arabica and Robusta under this scheme?
answer: The unit cost for Arabica is ₹2,75,000 per hectare, and for Robusta, it is ₹2,00,000 per hectare.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Replantation
question: What percentage of subsidy is provided to coffee growers under this scheme?
answer: Coffee growers are eligible for a 40% subsidy of the unit cost.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Replantation
question: Are there any special provisions for SC/ST community coffee growers?
answer: Yes, SC/ST community coffee growers with holdings up to 4.00 hectares are eligible for an additional 10% support of the unit cost.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Replantation
question: How is the subsidy released for clean replanting?
answer: For clean replanting, the first instalment is 70% of the applicable unit cost, and the second instalment is 30% of the applicable unit cost.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Replantation
question: What is the subsidy release process for replantation by interlining method?
answer: In the case of replantation by interlining, the first instalment is 30% of the applicable unit cost, and the second instalment is 70% of the applicable unit cost.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Replantation
question: What are the age criteria for coffee plants that can be replanted under this scheme?
answer: Arabica plants aged 25 years, Robusta plants aged 40 years, and Arabica dwarfs aged 15 years can be replanted.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Replantation
question: Is there a specific requirement for the removal of old plants in the case of interlining?
answer: Old and unproductive plants should preferably be removed after one harvest but not beyond two harvests to ensure vigorous growth of the newly interlined plants.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Replantation
question: Does the choice of coffee variety depend on the elevation of the plantation?
answer: Yes, in Arabica zones with an elevation of 1000 meters above MSL, only disease-tolerant, high-yielding Arabica varieties should be replanted. In other areas, both Arabica and Robusta can be replanted.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Replantation
question: What is the subsidy calculation for coffee grown with intercrops like pepper and banana?
answer: The subsidy is based on the actual extent of the area replanted with coffee or the maximum extent mentioned in the land documents, including other intercrops, whichever is less.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Replantation
question: Are there any recommendations for planting designs?
answer: Growers are encouraged to adopt planting designs suitable for mechanization. Modified planting designs amenable to mechanization can be considered for the entire area of replanting.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Replantation
question: Are there any exclusions for those who have previously received subsidies?
answer: A grower who has availed subsidy for one activity/component cannot avail subsidy for the same activity/component during the MTF period until new beneficiaries are covered.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Replantation
question: What is the exclusion related to Arabica replaced with Robusta?
answer: Arabica replaced with Robusta at a higher elevation of more than 1000 meters is not eligible for support.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Replantation
question: When can a grower claim the first instalment of the subsidy?
answer: The first instalment can be claimed during the same financial year of replanting as far as possible.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Replantation
question: What documents are required for claiming the first instalment of the subsidy?
answer: The required documents include a claim statement, a sketch of the replanted area, and an expenditure statement.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: Can a grower who has availed subsidy under one activity/component claim subsidy for the same activity/component again during the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) period?
answer: No, a grower who has availed subsidy under one activity/component is not eligible to claim subsidy for the same activity/component during the MIDH period unless new beneficiaries are covered.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: What additional documents are required for coffee exported directly?
answer: For coffee exported directly, additional documents include an export permit with Customs endorsement, ICO certificate of origin with customs endorsement, and the Bill of Lading (BL).

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: What additional documents are necessary for coffee marketing through auction platforms or commodity exchanges?
answer: For coffee marketed through auction platforms or commodity exchanges, additional documents include a registration certificate as a member of ICTA or other recognized marketing auction platform, and proof of coffee sold, attested by the auctioneers.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: What are the mandatory documents required for claiming the subsidy?
answer: The required documents include the application in the prescribed format, certificate of incorporation/registration, complete member details, member-wise coffee sales details, and certificates indicating membership in the Growers' Collective/SHG/Cooperative and VAT registration certificate from the state Government commercial tax department where applicable.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: When is the subsidy disbursed to the individual members of small growers' collectives/SHGs/Cooperatives?
answer: The subsidy is disbursed only after the sale of coffee is completed by small growers' collectives/SHGs/Cooperatives, and it is released directly to the individual members' bank accounts through National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) in cases where the application is complete in all respects.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: What is the procedure for claiming subsidy under this scheme?
answer: Small growers' collectives/SHGs/Cooperatives should furnish their claim for reimbursement along with supporting documents after marketing their coffee. The application for subsidy should be submitted to the concerned Deputy Director (Extension) during the same financial year of completing the activity.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: How much subsidy is provided per kilogram of clean coffee under this scheme?
answer: The subsidy is ₹4.00 per kilogram of clean coffee.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: What are the acceptable methods of marketing coffee under this scheme?
answer: Coffee marketing should be carried out either through recognized public auction platforms like the Indian Coffee Trade Association (ICTA), direct export by the organization, or through recognized Commodity Exchanges with physical delivery of coffee.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: Who is eligible to benefit from the "Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing" scheme?
answer: All Small Growers' Collectives, Self Help Groups (SHGs), and Cooperatives in traditional coffee-growing states are eligible.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: What is the objective of the scheme "Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing"?
answer: The scheme aims to support small and tiny coffee growers in forming collectives, Self Help Groups (SHGs), or cooperatives, thus encouraging them to engage in the marketing of coffee produced through a community-based approach, with financial incentives to improve coffee quality and enhance its value.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: Are there any special provisions for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe (SC/ST) community growers?
answer: Yes, SC/ST community growers with smaller holdings can receive additional support during the MIDH period.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: What is the role of the Coffee Board in implementing this scheme?
answer: The Coffee Board oversees the approval and disbursement of subsidies to eligible growers.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: How can a small grower ensure eligibility for this scheme?
answer: Small growers should market coffee in the name of their collectives/SHGs/Cooperatives through recognized channels.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: Can you explain the importance of recognized public auction platforms?
answer: Recognized auction platforms provide a transparent and efficient way to sell coffee and realize better prices.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: Can individuals benefit from this scheme, or does it require collective action?
answer: Both individual small growers and collectives/SHGs/Cooperatives can benefit from this scheme.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: Is this scheme applicable to non-traditional coffee-growing areas?
answer: This scheme is primarily aimed at traditional coffee-growing states.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: What is the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) period?
answer: The MIDH period is the timeframe during which the subsidy cannot be availed again for the same activity/component by growers who have already received it.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: How can small growers realize better value for their coffee through this scheme?
answer: They can achieve better value by marketing coffee on a community-based approach and through financial incentives.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: What is the significance of forming collectives or SHGs for coffee marketing?
answer: Forming collectives or SHGs helps small growers improve coffee quality and realize better prices through collective bargaining.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
question: What documents are required if coffee is exported directly?
answer: For direct export, documents such as an export permit, ICO certificate of origin, and Bill of Lading are needed.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: What is the minimum depth recommended for an open well/ring well with or without a pump?
answer: The recommended depth is 30 feet.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: What is the unit cost for open well/ring well activities?
answer: The unit cost for open well/ring well activities is ₹75,000 per unit.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: Can growers choose to execute water storage structures of any dimension?
answer: Yes, growers can execute structures of any dimension based on their requirements, and the subsidy will be applicable based on unit cost or actual cost, whichever is less.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: What is the unit cost for sprinkler/drip irrigation equipment for different holding sizes?

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: How is the subsidy amount released to the beneficiaries?
answer: The Deputy Director (Extn) releases the subsidy amount directly to the bank account of the applicant through Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT), RTGS, or NEFT.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: Is there additional support for the Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe (SC/ST) community?
answer: Yes, SC/ST community growers with coffee holdings up to 4 hectares are eligible for an extra 10% subsidy, with a ceiling of ₹2,50,000.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: What is the scale of subsidy for water storage tanks for different holding sizes?
answer: Subsidies range from 40% of the unit cost up to ₹2,50,000 for different holding sizes.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: What documents are required to obtain a Feasibility Report?
answer: Documents include a filled and signed application, Aadhaar card, proof of land ownership, rough sketch of the estate, quotation for machinery/equipment, and more.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: What is the procedure for claiming the subsidy?
answer: Applicants should submit the subsidy claim to the jurisdictional Coffee Board office, which involves document scrutiny, field inspection, and approval by the Deputy Director (Extn).

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: What should growers ensure before commencing any activities related to the scheme?
answer: Growers should obtain the Technical Feasibility Report (TFR) before starting any activities related to the scheme.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: Are non-tribal coffee growers in Non-Traditional Areas eligible for this subsidy?
answer: Yes, non-tribal coffee growers in Non-Traditional Areas with coffee holdings of up to 10 hectares are also eligible for this subsidy.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: Where should water augmentation infrastructure be created?
answer: It should be created either within the coffee estate or in its vicinity, depending on the water source. The land for this purpose should be in the name of the grower or their family members.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: When do growers become eligible for the same water augmentation activity again if they have previously benefited from the subsidy?
answer: Growers become eligible for the same activity from the 11th year onwards after benefiting from the subsidy.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: Is it possible to combine subsidies for different water augmentation activities?
answer: Subsidy may be availed for any one of the water harvesting structures combined with any one of the irrigation equipment during the MTF period.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: Can a grower avail the subsidy for the same activity more than once during the Multi-Year Thrust Plan (MTF) period?
answer: No, a grower who has availed the subsidy for a specific activity/component cannot avail it again during the MTF period unless new beneficiaries are included.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: What specific purposes is the subsidy applicable for?
answer: The subsidy is applicable for water harvesting structures (e.g., water storage tanks, open wells, or ring wells) and procurement of irrigation equipment, including sprinkler or drip systems.

scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
question: Who is eligible to apply for this subsidy?
answer: Individual growers, joint ownerships, or family members applying jointly (limited to mother, father, wife, and children) with coffee holdings of up to 10 hectares are eligible.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: What Is Meant By "Aadhaar Seeding"?
answer: The fellowship is directly paid to the research scholars in their bank accounts. For this, the bank account numbers of the scholars are required to be Aadhaar linked and verified. This process is called "Aadhaar Seeding". As per the instructions of the Government of India, the Aadhaar has been made mandatory for the disbursement of all Government subsidies/Scholarships/Fellowships which are disbursed directly into the beneficiary's account. Accordingly, Aadhaar will be used as an Identifier for the release of grants under these schemes.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: Does Only The Submission Of An Application Form Guarantee The Award Of A Fellowship And Research Grant?
answer: No, mere submission of an application form does not guarantee the award of a Fellowship and Research Grant.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: Who Shall Be Held Responsible If The Applicant Furnishes Incorrect/Incomplete Information That Results In The Cancellation Of His/Her Candidature?
answer: It is the responsibility of the applicant to provide correct information, failing which he/she will be solely responsible for the cancellation for his/her candidature.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: Can I Apply Offline For The Research Grant?
answer: No. You need to visit the official website to apply.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: Is There Any Application Fee?
answer: No. The entire application process is completely free of cost.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: How Do I Know If A Field In The Application Form Is Mandatory?
answer: The mandatory fields have a red asterisk (*) mark at the end.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: How Many Slots Are There In This Fellowship Scheme?
answer: There are 900 slots, allocated as per Govt. of India reservation policy. 30% of slots will be reserved for women candidates.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: What Are The Objectives Of Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship?
answer: The objective of these fellowships is to provide an opportunity to carry out advanced studies and research in Sciences, Engineering, and Technology, Humanities & Social Sciences including languages in Indian Universities/Institutions. The tenure of the fellowship is 3 years with no provision for further extension.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: Is Reader Assitance Available For A Person With Disability?
answer: Yes, there is Escorts/Reader Assistance @Rs.3000/-p.m.(fixed) in cases of PWD (Person with Disability).

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: What Is The Amount Of Contingency Allowance In This Scheme?
answer: Contingency @ Rs. 50,000/- p.a.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: Are The Candidates From NAAC-Accredited Universities Also Eligible To Apply To This Scheme?
answer: Yes, candidates from Universities (including constituent and affiliated institutions) included under section 2(f) of the UGC Act, 1956, and having valid accreditation from NAAC, are also eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: Are There Any Norms For Utilizing The Contingency Grant?
answer: The Contingency grant may be utilized for minor equipment useful for research such as laboratory equipment or laptop costing less than 50,000/-, chemicals, and other research-specific items within the ceiling of Rs.1.00 Lakh p.a. with the approval of the host university/institution. The items purchased from the contingency grant are assets of the university/institution and at the end of the fellowship are to be handed over to the host university/institution. The contingency grant cannot be used for international travel and the purchase of furniture.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: What Is The Provision If The Scholar Wishes To Draw HRA?
answer: In case, the scholar wishes to draw HRA, he/she is required to submit a certificate, in the prescribed format, to his institution.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: Is Medical Assistance A Part Of The Scheme Benefits?
answer: No separate/fixed medical assistance is provided. However, the scholars may avail the medical facilities available in their Institutions concerned.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: Is The Fellow Eligible To Receive Maternity Leave?
answer: Maternity/paternity leave as per the Govt. of India norms issued from time to time shall be available for scholars at full rates of the fellowship once during the tenure of the fellowship.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: What Is Meant By An 'Intermittent Break'?
answer: An 'Intermittent Break' for a maximum total period of 1 year shall be permissible to the women scholars. The break can be availed a maximum of 3 times during the entire period of the fellowship. However, the total duration of the break shall not exceed one year. No fellowship shall be available for the period of such break(s). This period of intermittent breaks shall not be counted towards the tenure of the fellowship, and thus effectively the total period of fellowship shall remain the same.

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: Where Can I View The Notification Released Regarding The Scheme?
answer: Short notification is uploaded to the UGC website i.e. www.ugc.ac.in

scheme_name: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship
question: For How Long Is The 'Academic Leave' Permissible?
answer: 'Academic leave' shall be permissible only for one year throughout the tenure for any kind of academic/teaching assignment/foreign visit in connection with research work. However, during the period of academic leave no fellowship, contingency, etc will be paid by the UGC. The period of academic leave will be counted towards the tenure. Expenditure on foreign visits in connection to research work cannot be claimed from UGC.

scheme_name: AICTE-INAE Distinguished Visiting Professorship Scheme
question: What is AICTE-INAE Distinguished Visiting Professorship Scheme?
answer: AICTE and INAE distinguished visiting Professor scheme envisages promotion of industry-institute interaction.

scheme_name: AICTE-INAE Distinguished Visiting Professorship Scheme
question: Who manages this scheme?
answer: The Indian National Academy of Engineering (INAE) and All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) jointly manage this scheme.

scheme_name: AICTE-INAE Distinguished Visiting Professorship Scheme
question: When this scheme was launched?
answer: This scheme was launched in 1999.

scheme_name: AICTE-INAE Distinguished Visiting Professorship Scheme
question: What should be the minimum educational qualification of the industry expert?
answer: The Industry Experts should have a minimum graduate degree in engineering or an equivalent qualification.

scheme_name: AICTE-INAE Distinguished Visiting Professorship Scheme
question: What should be the age criteria of a Distinguished Visiting Professor?
answer: The Age of a Distinguished Visiting Professor shall be in the range of 40 to 75 years.

scheme_name: AICTE-INAE Distinguished Visiting Professorship Scheme
question: How many years of industry experienced is required for an applicant?
answer: The applicant must have minimum TEN years' experience in Industry.

scheme_name: AICTE-INAE Distinguished Visiting Professorship Scheme
question: Whether a retired INAE fellow can apply under this Scheme?
answer: Yes. Since the year 2018, the scheme has also been made applicable to all retired INAE Fellows.

scheme_name: AICTE-INAE Distinguished Visiting Professorship Scheme
question: Maximum how many colleges a DVP can visit in his/her tenure?
answer: A DVP can visit up to two AICTE approved engineering colleges in his/her tenure.

scheme_name: AICTE-INAE Distinguished Visiting Professorship Scheme
question: What is the tenure of the Distinguished Visiting Professor?
answer: Tenure will be initially for a period of one year, which is further extendable up to a maximum of five years.

scheme_name: AICTE-INAE Distinguished Visiting Professorship Scheme
question: How the application can be made?
answer: Through offline mode.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Market
question: What is the purpose of this online trading platform for agricultural markets?
answer: It is designed to integrate existing markets across the country into a single online system, enabling unified trading for agricultural commodities and promoting "One Nation One Market."

scheme_name: National Agriculture Market
question: How does this platform improve price discovery for farmers?
answer: It enables real-time price discovery through e-auctions and e-trading based on demand and supply, helping farmers secure better prices.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Market
question: How does the system ensure transparency in agricultural trade?
answer: It offers clear, online auction processes, quality testing results, and direct electronic payments, reducing the scope for manipulation or hidden charges.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Market
question: What services are provided to farmers through this platform?
answer: Farmers get single-window services including commodity arrival details, quality assaying, e-bidding for price discovery, and direct e-payment to their bank accounts.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Market
question: How does quality testing work on this platform?
answer: Free assaying (quality testing) is offered at markets to help ensure standardized pricing based on the quality of produce.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Market
question: What advantages does wider buyer participation offer to farmers?
answer: It increases competition among buyers, which helps farmers get better prices for their commodities.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Market
question: What role do assaying labs and electronic weighbridges play?
answer: They help standardize and verify quality and quantity, making trading more reliable for both farmers and buyers.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Market
question: How are market committees or boards supported for integration?
answer: They receive infrastructure support like e-auction halls, assaying labs, electronic weighbridges, internet, and training facilities to enable online trading.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Market
question: Is software support provided to markets joining the platform?
answer: Yes, free software with state-level customization and support staff is provided to help markets manage online trading.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Market
question: How does this system reduce information gaps for farmers?
answer: By showing arrival data, auction prices, and quality testing results online, farmers can make more informed selling decisions.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s E-YUVA Fellows (for under graduate students)
question: What is the "E-YUVA Scheme"?
answer: The scheme "Empowering Youth for Undertaking Value Added Innovative Translational Research (E-YUVA)" was started by the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) to promote a culture of applied research and need-oriented (societal or industry) entrepreneurial innovation among young students and researchers. The scheme provides funding support (through fellowship and research grant), technical and business mentoring, exposure to bio incubation model, orientation to an entrepreneurial culture, etc. to students at various levels including undergraduates, post-graduates, and post-doctoral.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s E-YUVA Fellows (for under graduate students)
question: What is the "E-YUVA Centers (EYCs)"?
answer: E-Yuva Centers are housed within the University/Institute set-up. It acts as an anchor and extends requisite support and mentoring to students. Each EYC has a BIRAC-supported pre-incubation space which offers infrastructure and equipment for basic research and experimentation by selected students.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s E-YUVA Fellows (for under graduate students)
question: Which is the implementing agency of this scheme?
answer: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC)

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s E-YUVA Fellows (for under graduate students)
question: What is the "BIRAC's E-YUVA Fellowship"?
answer: The "BIRAC's E-YUVA Fellowship" is the scheme a category under E-YUVA Scheme. Under the scheme, a team of students who are pursuing under graduation in any domain can apply to pursue their research work at their College/University labs and will also be allowed access to facilities at EYC and EYC Knowledge Partners as and when required. It will be mandatory for all the fellows to spend 3-4 weeks at EYC/EYC Knowledge Partner during their fellowship period.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s E-YUVA Fellows (for under graduate students)
question: What are the areas covered under this fellowship category?
answer: BIRAC encourages interdisciplinary proposals from any stream that can help conversion of innovative ideas into biotech products and technologies in any of the above fields.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s E-YUVA Fellows (for under graduate students)
question: What is the nature of proposals?
answer: Proposal should be original. | Proposal should apply interdisciplinary knowledge. | - The Proposal should aim at the development of innovative Biotech products/technologies with societal/commercial potential.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s E-YUVA Fellows (for under graduate students)
question: How many fellows can be at Each EYC?
answer: Each EYC will support up to 5 teams with upto 5 students each every year.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s E-YUVA Fellows (for under graduate students)
question: What is the duration of fellowship?
answer: Fellowship is provided for a period of 12 months.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s E-YUVA Fellows (for under graduate students)
question: Who is eligible to apply under the scheme?
answer: Indian students from Indian Institutes/colleges who are pursuing under graduation in any domain should apply as a team.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s E-YUVA Fellows (for under graduate students)
question: What is the maximum number of students who can be in a team?
answer: A team should comprise a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 5 Indian students from Indian Institutes/colleges pursuing under graduation in any domain.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s E-YUVA Fellows (for under graduate students)
question: What is nature of support provided to fellows under the scheme?
answer: BIRAC's E-YUVA Fellows will receive a quarterly stipend and annual research grant as mentioned below: | Quarterly Stipend: INR 7,500/- per quarter per student of the team | Annual research grant: INR 2,50,000/- per team

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s E-YUVA Fellows (for under graduate students)
question: Are the students received stipend monthly?
answer: No, the stipend is released quarterly to the student's account, subject to the Mentor's approval.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s E-YUVA Fellows (for under graduate students)
question: How will research grant release?
answer: The annual research grant is released in two installments (1st installment: 75%; 2nd installment: 25%) to the Institute's account and is managed by the mentor/guide.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s E-YUVA Fellows (for under graduate students)
question: How can an applicant submit the proposals under the scheme?
answer: Any one team member can create a user account on BIRAC's website on behalf of the team followed by filling up of online application form. (https://birac.nic.in/)

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s Innovation Fellows (for post graduates and above)

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s Innovation Fellows (for post graduates and above)

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s Innovation Fellows (for post graduates and above)

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s Innovation Fellows (for post graduates and above)
question: How many Innovation Fellows can be at Each EYC?
answer: Each EYC can have 3 Innovation Fellows at any given time.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s Innovation Fellows (for post graduates and above)
question: What is the duration of fellowship?

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s Innovation Fellows (for post graduates and above)
question: Who is eligible to apply under the scheme?
answer: An Indian Student who has completed Masters/ Ph.D in any discipline is eligible to apply for this fellowship.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s Innovation Fellows (for post graduates and above)

question: What is nature of support provided to fellows under the scheme?

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: BIRAC’s Innovation Fellows (for post graduates and above)
question: How can an applicant submit the proposals under the scheme?

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: E-YUVA Centers
question: What are the roles and responsibilities of EYCs?
answer: Roles and Responsibilities of EYCs: | View and process online applications received for fellowship | Screen applications for eligibility and suitability for the scheme | Carry out online Technical Review of eligible applications through Subject Experts (Reviewers) | Shortlist proposals for interview(F2F/skype/telephonic) by an Expert Panel | Communicate decision to applicants at each step of selection | Seek BIRAC approval on the final selection of fellows or their eligibility | Issue fellowship award letters to the selected candidates on behalf of BIRAC | Release fellowship and research grant received from BIRAC | Provide mentorship, handholding, and access to facilities at EYC and EYC Knowledge Partner for BIRAC's Innovation and E-YUVA Fellows | Monitor the targeted milestones | Organize periodic review meetings | Provide mentorship and handholding for domain expertise, entrepreneurship, and activities including but not limited to IP management, mobilizing resources, and other business development-related activities | Provide platforms/opportunities for interaction with experts | Provide periodic updates and reports on the progress of Fellows to BIRAC | Conduct entrepreneurial workshops | Any other activity required for effective implementation of fellowships on mutual consent with BIRAC.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: E-YUVA Centers
question: What is the tenure of EY Centres?
answer: EYCs will be engaged for an initial duration of 3 years, extendable further based on performance review.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: E-YUVA Centers
question: Who is E-Yuva Knowledge Partner?
answer: BIRAC will assign engagement with BioNEST-supported Bio-incubators for the mentoring of Innovation Fellows and for providing overall guidance to EYCs,. Each EYC will be formally associated with a BioNEST-supported bio incubator, which shall provide necessary handholding and mentoring to EYCs and Innovation Fellows. The knowledge partner will engage with the fellows throughout the award period and provide overall guidance.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: E-YUVA Centers
question: Who is eligible to apply under the scheme?
answer: University/Institution established as a legal entity under the relevant Law of India having at least 51% Indian stakeholders (owners/partners/trustees/members/associates etc.) from Tier II/III cities is eligible to apply.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: E-YUVA Centers
question: What are the other mandatory conditions to apply under the scheme?
answer: Other mandatory conditions are as follows: | Applicant University/Institution should have a Department in the Life Sciences stream (Biotechnology/ Biosciences/ Agriculture /Horticulture/ Food technology etc.) for technical support. | Age of the applicant University/Institution should be at least 3 years or more. | Presence of an Innovation supporting formal body, such as E-Cell/ Institutional Innovation Councils/ IP Cells/ TTOs / Incubation centres, etc. is a must. | Offer dedicated space of approx. 3,000 sq. ft. & relevant infrastructure ready for use.

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: E-YUVA Centers
question: What is nature of support provided to beneficiaries under the scheme?
answer: Under the scheme, financial Support is provided to each EYC in the form of Recurring Head & Non-recurring Head (Creating pre-incubation space).

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: E-YUVA Centers
question: What is the mode of Proposal submission?

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: E-YUVA Centers
question: How can an applicant submit the proposals under the scheme?

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: E-YUVA Centers

The Institute should be willing to support EYC fellows to facilitate networking through individuals/groups. | Connects with bio incubators and other organizations actively promoting Entrepreneurship

scheme_name: E-YUVA Scheme: E-YUVA Centers

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme
question: What is the objective of the scheme?
answer: The main objective of the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) is to make India self-reliant (Atmanirbhar) in the electronics supply chain by building a strong domestic component manufacturing ecosystem.

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme
question: Who can apply for ECMS?
answer: Only a Company or LLP investing in the manufacturing of target segment electronics products is eligible. Both greenfield and brownfield projects are allowed.

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme
question: What is the official portal to apply?
answer: Applications are submitted online at https://ecms.meity.gov.in/register.

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme
question: What are the Target Segments under ECMS?
answer: There are 5 segments - A (Sub-assemblies), B (Bare Components), C (Selected Bare Components), D (Supply Chain & Capital Equipment), and E (Telecom Sub-assembly)

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme
question: What incentives are available?
answer: Three types - Turnover-linked, Capex-linked, and Hybrid (combination of both)

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme
question: What is the total budget of the scheme?
answer: The scheme has a total budgeted outlay of ₹22,919 crores

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme
question: How long does the scheme run?
answer: The scheme runs for 6 years from FY 2025-26 with a 1-year gestation period for Segments A, B & C

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme
question: Can one company submit multiple applications?
answer: Yes, but only one application per product is allowed. Separate applications are required for each product under the target segment

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme
question: Is the application fee refundable?
answer: No, the application fee is non-refundable.

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme
question: What is the minimum investment required?
answer: It varies by product - minimum ₹10 Cr for Segment D (Supply Chain & Capital Equipment) and up to ₹1,000 Cr for HDI/MSAP/Flexible PCB

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme
question: How long does PMA take to acknowledge the application?
answer: PMA issues acknowledgement within 15 working days of application submission.

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme
question: Who gives the final approval?
answer: Secretary MeitY approves incentives up to ₹100 Cr and Minister of Electronics & IT approves incentives above ₹100 Cr.

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme
question: How are incentives disbursed?
answer: Incentives are disbursed on a first-come, first-served basis after submission of certified annual claims, capped at 50% of the eligible incremental investment.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
question: Who can apply for this scheme?
answer: Individuals, Self Help Groups (SHGs), Farmers Producer Organizations (FPOs), Farmers Cooperatives (FCOs), Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), and Section 8 companies can apply.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
question: How is the subsidy disbursed?
answer: For bank-financed projects, the subsidy is released in two installments-first after the loan disbursement and confirmation, and second after project completion and verification.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
question: Is the scheme available for self-financed projects?
answer: Yes, self-financed projects are eligible, but applicants must provide a bank guarantee valid for three years for the remaining project cost beyond the subsidy amount.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
question: What kind of poultry can be reared under this scheme?
answer: Only Low Input Technology Birds or those that can be sustained in a free-range management system are permitted.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
question: What are the essential project components covered under this scheme?
answer: Parent Farms, Rural Hatcheries, and Brooder cum Mother Units with a minimum of 1,000 parent layers are covered.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
question: How long does it take for the second installment of the subsidy to be released?
answer: The second instalment is released after project completion and verification by the State Implementing Agency.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
question: Who verifies the project for subsidy disbursement?
answer: The State Implementing Agency verifies the project and confirms eligibility for the second instalment of the subsidy.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
question: Can private organizations supply birds for the scheme?
answer: Yes, private organizations with certificates of guaranteed production, along with designated research institutions, can supply birds.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
question: What documents are required for application?
answer: Applicants must provide identity proof, address proof, business entity registration, a detailed project report, bank loan approval (if applicable), a bank guarantee (for self-financing), and a declaration form.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
question: Can an applicant avail of this subsidy multiple times?
answer: The guidelines do not specify multiple availments; applicants should check with the State Implementing Agency for clarification.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
question: Where can one apply for this scheme?
answer: Applications must be submitted through the designated online portal or the relevant State Implementing Agency.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
question: What expenses are not covered under the subsidy?
answer: The subsidy does not cover working capital, personal vehicles, land purchase, rent, or lease costs.

scheme_name: Establishment of Entrepreneur for Breed Development in Small Ruminant Sector (Sheep and Goat Farming)
question: What is the objective of this scheme?
answer: The primary objective is to develop entrepreneurs in the small ruminant sector, create sustainable business models for sheep and goat farming, and promote the transition from an unorganized to an organized sector through entrepreneurship and investment.

scheme_name: Establishment of Entrepreneur for Breed Development in Small Ruminant Sector (Sheep and Goat Farming)
question: Who are the eligible beneficiaries under this scheme?
answer: Eligible beneficiaries include Individuals, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Farmer Cooperatives (FCOs), Self Help Groups (SHGs), Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), and Section 8 companies.

scheme_name: Establishment of Entrepreneur for Breed Development in Small Ruminant Sector (Sheep and Goat Farming)
question: What is the financial assistance provided under this scheme?
answer: The scheme provides up to 50% back-ended subsidy for the capital cost of the project, with a maximum subsidy of ₹ 50 lakh per unit. Subsidy is provided in two equal instalments.

scheme_name: Establishment of Entrepreneur for Breed Development in Small Ruminant Sector (Sheep and Goat Farming)
question: What are the essential documents required to apply for the scheme?
answer: Essential documents include the application form, project proposal, identity proof, address proof, entity registration documents (if applicable), bank account details, loan sanction letter (if applicable), bank guarantee (for self-financing projects), declaration form, technical specifications, proof of expenditure, and land ownership/lease documents.

scheme_name: Establishment of Entrepreneur for Breed Development in Small Ruminant Sector (Sheep and Goat Farming)
question: How is the subsidy disbursed?
answer: Subsidy is disbursed in two instalments: | First Instalment: Released upfront to the scheduled bank or financial institution after confirmation of the first instalment of the loan by the State Implementing Agency. | Second Instalment: Released after completion of the project and its verification by the State Implementing Agency.

scheme_name: Establishment of Entrepreneur for Breed Development in Small Ruminant Sector (Sheep and Goat Farming)
question: Can urban residents apply for this scheme?
answer: While the scheme primarily focuses on rural development, urban residents may apply if their projects align with the rural development objectives of the scheme. It is advisable to consult with the State Implementing Agency for specific eligibility criteria.

scheme_name: Establishment of Entrepreneur for Breed Development in Small Ruminant Sector (Sheep and Goat Farming)

scheme_name: Electronic Manufacturing Clusters (EMC) Scheme: Common Facility Centres/ Brownfield Electronics Manufacturing Clusters

scheme_name: Electronic Manufacturing Clusters (EMC) Scheme: Common Facility Centres/ Brownfield Electronics Manufacturing Clusters
question: What is the objective of the Brownfield EMC component?

scheme_name: Electronic Manufacturing Clusters (EMC) Scheme: Common Facility Centres/ Brownfield Electronics Manufacturing Clusters

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: What does EPCG stand for and what is the benefit of an EPCG authorisation?
answer: EPCG stands for Export Promotion Capital Goods. The objective of this scheme is to facilitate the import of capital goods to produce quality goods and services to enhance India's export competitiveness. EPCG scheme allows import of capital goods for pre-production, production, and post-production at zero customs duty.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: Who can benefit from the EPCG Scheme?
answer: Manufacturer exporters with or without supporting manufacturer(s), merchant exporters tied to supporting manufacturer(s) and service provider(s), and service providers. Refer to FTP and HBP for the latest details.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: If my IEC is in DEL/cancelled/suspended, am I eligible to apply for the EPCG authorisation?
answer: If your IEC is in DEL, you shall be allowed to proceed with the submission of your request for issuance of an EPCG authorisation; however, your application shall only be actioned upon once your IEC is removed from DEL. | If your IEC is cancelled/suspended, you shall not be allowed to proceed with the submission of your request for the issuance of an EPCG authorisation.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: How is my export obligation period divided into blocks?
answer: Your export obligation period is defined for six years from the date of issuance of the authorisation. These six years are divided into two blocks, namely, the first block and the second block. The first block period is for the first four years from the date of issuance of the authorisation. Whereas, the following two years are known to be the second block period of your authorisation.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: Is there a time period for amendment of an issued authorisation?
answer: An authorisation may only be allowed for amendment until its import validity period. No authorisations shall be permitted for amendment post the validity period of the authorisation.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: What is the significance of initial and revised value of my authorisation validity dates?
answer: The initial and the revised values of the authorisation validity dates show the import and export validity dates as per the issued authorisations and amended validity dates (if any). If no extensions have been granted against the selected authorisation, the initial and the revised values shall be the same.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: What is the application fee for amendment?
answer: One per thousand for differential duty saved amount to be enhanced in addition to a flat fee of INR 200/- for amendment to the issued authorisation. No additional fee is required if the maximum prescribed fee has been paid initially.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: Why can't I decrease my import quantity of an item?
answer: You can only decrease the quantities of imported items if the bill of entries of these items already exists in the Shipping Bill Repository, i.e., post importing the item, you shall not be allowed to decrease the quantity of the item.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: What are the benefits of domestic sourcing?
answer: You may be allowed a benefit of 25% in your specific Export Obligation for domestic sourcing.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: What is an installation certificate?
answer: An installation certificate is proof of the installation of capital goods at the said factory/premises of the authorisation holder or the supporting manufacturer of the authorisation holder. This certificate may be obtained from the jurisdictional customs authority or an independent chartered engineer.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Council Membership Reimbursement Scheme for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe

scheme_name: Export Promotion Council Membership Reimbursement Scheme for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe

scheme_name: Export Promotion Council Membership Reimbursement Scheme for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe

scheme_name: Export Promotion Council Membership Reimbursement Scheme for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe

scheme_name: Export Promotion Council Membership Reimbursement Scheme for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: What are the minimum years of service required to be eligible for pension benefits under this scheme?
answer: The applicant must have completed a minimum of 10 years of contributory service under the Employees' Provident Fund to qualify for pension benefits.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: How is the monthly member's pension calculated under this scheme?
answer: The pension amount is calculated using the formula: (Pensionable Salary × Pensionable Service) / 70. The result determines the monthly payout.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: What is the minimum pension amount guaranteed under this scheme?
answer: The minimum pension provided is ₹1,000 per month, subject to deductions for commutation or early pension adjustments.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: Who is eligible to receive a family pension after the member's death?
answer: The deceased member's spouse is eligible for 50% of the pension, while children receive 25% each, up to a maximum of two children.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: What happens if a member exits the scheme before completing 10 years of service?
answer: Members who exit before 10 years receive a withdrawal benefit, calculated as per Table D of the scheme's provisions.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: At what age does the superannuation pension become payable under this scheme?
answer: The superannuation pension is payable once the member attains 58 years of age, provided they have at least 10 years of service.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: Can a member claim an early pension before reaching 58 years of age?
answer: Yes, early pension can be claimed between 50 and 58 years, but it is reduced by 4% for each year below 58.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: What documents are required to apply for a family pension after a member's death?
answer: The applicant must submit the member's death certificate along with proof of relationship, such as a marriage or birth certificate.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: How is the pension amount adjusted if a member delays claiming it beyond 58 years?
answer: For each year deferred beyond 58, the pension increases by 4%, up to a maximum of 60 years of age.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: What is the orphan pension, and who is eligible to receive it?
answer: Orphan pension is 75% of the widow's pension, payable if there is no surviving spouse and only dependent children.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: What is the pension benefit for a member who becomes permanently disabled during service?
answer: A minimum of ₹250 per month is provided as a permanent total disablement pension if disability occurs during employment.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: How can a member track the status of their pension application online?
answer: The status can be checked on the EPFO portal using the UAN and acknowledgement number or via the SMS service.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: What is the process for activating the Universal Account Number (UAN) for online services?
answer: Visit the EPFO Unified Portal, enter UAN and mobile details, validate OTP, and set a password to activate the UAN.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: What are the password requirements for accessing the EPFO member portal?
answer: The password must be 8-12 characters long, with at least 1 uppercase letter, 1 number, and 1 special character.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: What is the maximum file size allowed for document uploads during online application?
answer: Scanned documents must be in PDF, JPEG, or PNG format, with a maximum size of 2 MB per file.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: What should an applicant do if their pension claim is delayed beyond the expected timeline?
answer: Delays beyond 20 working days incur a 12% penal interest, and grievances can be raised via EPFiGMS or helpline.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: What is the validity period of the OTP used during the online application process?
answer: The OTP sent for verification remains valid for 10 minutes before expiring.

scheme_name: Employees' Pension Scheme
question: Is there a helpline available for assistance regarding pension-related queries?
answer: Yes, the EPFO helpline (1800-118-005) operates from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM for support and grievance redressal.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
question: What is the purpose of the Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab scheme?
answer: The scheme aims to increase per-animal productivity, reduce inbreeding, and prevent sexually transmitted diseases in pigs by providing high-quality boar semen for artificial insemination.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
question: Who is responsible for implementing this scheme?
answer: The scheme is implemented by the State Implementing Agencies of the State Animal Husbandry Department and the State Animal Husbandry Departments.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
question: What type of semen is used for artificial insemination under this scheme?
answer: Since frozen semen technology is not effective for pigs, artificial insemination is carried out using liquid boar semen, which remains viable for a longer duration when processed scientifically.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
question: What assistance is provided under this scheme?
answer: Financial assistance is provided to establish semen processing laboratories at government pig farms to produce high-quality liquid boar semen for artificial insemination.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
question: How much financial support is provided for setting up a semen processing lab?
answer: A one-time grant-in-aid of up to ₹1.5 crore is provided for constructing the lab and maintaining breeding boars. An additional ₹30 lakh is provided for the first-time procurement of consumables, medicines, and chemicals.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
question: What is the funding pattern for the scheme?
answer: For most states, the funding is shared in a 60:40 ratio between the Central and State Governments. However, for the North Eastern Region (NER) and Himalayan states, the ratio is 90:10.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
answer: The scheme is open to State Livestock Agencies and the Animal Husbandry Departments of State Governments.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
question: Can private farms or organizations apply for assistance under this scheme?
answer: No, only State Livestock Agencies and the State Animal Husbandry Departments are eligible to receive assistance.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
question: How does the scheme help in reducing inbreeding among pigs?
answer: By providing access to high genetic merit boar semen for artificial insemination, the scheme reduces the chances of inbreeding, which improves the overall genetic quality of pig populations.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
question: Why is liquid boar semen preferred over frozen semen for pigs?
answer: Unlike large ruminants, frozen semen technology does not work well for pigs. Liquid semen, when processed hygienically, has a success rate of 60% in artificial insemination.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
question: What kind of expenses are covered under the ₹30 lakh grant?
answer: The ₹30 lakh grant is meant for the procurement of consumables, medicines, chemicals, and other essential items required for the initial processing of boar semen.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
question: Is the financial assistance provided on a recurring basis?
answer: No, the assistance is provided as a one-time grant to help set up the semen processing lab and procure initial supplies.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
question: Where will the semen processing labs be set up?
answer: The labs will be established at government pig farms to ensure the production and availability of high-quality liquid boar semen.

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
question: Whom should an interested agency contact for more details?
answer: Agencies should reach out to their respective State Animal Husbandry Department for detailed guidelines, application procedures, and support.

scheme_name: Establishment of Regional Semen Production Laboratory and Semen Bank for sheep and goat
question: What is the objective of this scheme?
answer: The objective is to genetically improve indigenous sheep/goat breeds through selective breeding, upgrade non-descript breeds by cross-breeding with high genetic rams or bucks, and reduce negative selection and inbreeding by propagating superior male germplasm through artificial insemination and other reproductive technologies.

scheme_name: Establishment of Regional Semen Production Laboratory and Semen Bank for sheep and goat
question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
answer: State Livestock Agencies are eligible to apply for this scheme.

scheme_name: Establishment of Regional Semen Production Laboratory and Semen Bank for sheep and goat
question: What financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
answer: The scheme provides a funding pattern of 60:40 for most states, 90:10 for North Eastern Region (NER) and Himalayan States, and 100% for Union Territories (UTs). It includes a one-time grants-in-aid up to ₹ 400 lakh for the establishment of the laboratory and ₹ 30 lakh for the initial procurement of consumables, medicines, and chemicals.

scheme_name: Establishment of Regional Semen Production Laboratory and Semen Bank for sheep and goat
question: What are the key components of the project?
answer: Key components include the establishment of a Frozen Semen production laboratory for goats, a liquid semen production laboratory for sheep, and adherence to Minimum Standards for Sheep and Goat Semen Processing (MSP) guidelines.

scheme_name: Establishment of Regional Semen Production Laboratory and Semen Bank for sheep and goat
question: What is the funding pattern for this scheme?
answer: The funding pattern is 60:40 for all states except for NER & Himalayan States where it is 90:10, and 100% for UTs.

scheme_name: Establishment of Regional Semen Production Laboratory and Semen Bank for sheep and goat

scheme_name: Establishment of Regional Semen Production Laboratory and Semen Bank for sheep and goat

scheme_name: Establishment of Regional Semen Production Laboratory and Semen Bank for sheep and goat
question: Is recurring expenditure covered under this scheme?

scheme_name: Establishment of Regional Semen Production Laboratory and Semen Bank for sheep and goat
question: What are the responsibilities of the State Implementing Agency?
answer: The State Implementing Agency is responsible for verifying the submitted documents, assessing project feasibility, disbursing funds, and conducting follow-up verification after project completion.

scheme_name: Establishment of Regional Semen Production Laboratory and Semen Bank for sheep and goat
question: Where can I get more information about the scheme?
answer: For more information, contact the State Implementing Agency or the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry, and Dairying (MoFAHD), Government of India.

scheme_name: Establishment of Regional Semen Production Laboratory and Semen Bank for sheep and goat

question: What is APEDA ?
answer: The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) was | established by the Government of India under the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority Act, 1985. The primary objective of APEDA is to undertake the development and promotion of the export of the following products. | i. Fruits, vegetables and their products, | ii. Meat and meat products, | iii. Poultry and poultry products, | iv. Dairy products, | v. Confectionary, biscuits, and bakery products, | vi. Honey, jaggery and sugar products, | vii. Cocoa and its products, chocolates of all kinds, | viii. Alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, | ix. Cereals and Cereal products, | x. Groundnuts, peanuts and walnuts, | xi. Pickles, chutneys and papads, | xii. Guar Gum | xiii. Floriculture and floriculture products, | xiv. Herbal and medicinal plants. | xv. Cashew kernels, cashew nut shell liquid, cardanol | The following specific objectives have been laid down in Section 10(2) of the APEDA Act: | i. The development of industries relating to the Scheduled products for export by way of providing financial assistance or otherwise for undertaking surveys and feasibility studies, | participation in the equity capital through joint ventures and other reliefs and subsidy | schemes; | ii. the registration of persons as exporters of the Scheduled products on payment of such fees as may be prescribed; | iii. The fixing of standards and specifications for the Scheduled products for the purposes of | export; | iv. the carrying out of inspection of meat and meat products in any slaughterhouse, processing, | plant, storage premises, conveyances, or other places where such products are kept or handled for the purpose of ensuring the quality of such products; | v. the improving of packaging of the Scheduled products; | vi. the improving of the marketing of the Scheduled products outside India; | vii. the promotion of export-oriented production and development of the Scheduled products; | viii. the collection of statistics from the owners of factories or establishments engaged in the | production, processing, packaging, marketing, or export of the Scheduled products or from | such other persons as may be prescribed on any matter relating to the Scheduled products; | and the publication of the statistics so collected, or of any portions thereof or extracts there | from; | ix. the training in various aspects of the industries connected with the Scheduled products; | x. such other matters as may be prescribed. | In addition to the above, APEDA has also been entrusted with the task of registration and protection of Intellectual Property rights in respect of 'Special Products' in India or Outside India. At present, the only 'Special Product', as listed in the Second Schedule to the APEDA Act, is Basmati Rice. After protracted efforts, APEDA was able to obtain GI registration for Basmati Rice in February 2016. APEDA is also the Secretariat for the National Programme for Organic Production, specifying the accreditation and certification programs for organic production. The organic certification programme covers all agricultural commodities including non-APEDA scheduled products. More than 10 lakh farmers are registered under the programme and the certification is a mandatory requirement for organic products exports. | For more information please visit: https://apeda.gov.in/apedawebsite/

scheme_name: Agriculture And Processed Foods Export Promotion Scheme Of APEDA For The 15th Finance Commission Cycle (2021-22 To 2025-26)
question: What are the Scheme Components ?
answer: The Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS) is an export promotion scheme run by APEDA. The | scheme aims to facilitate the export of agri-products by providing assistance to exporters. It | achieves its objective through the following: | - Understanding the several challenges faced by agri-exporters. | - Acknowledging the need for assistance to successfully navigate through these challenges and achieve the objectives of APEDA. | Financial assistance is provided in three broad areas, namely: Development of Export Infrastructure, Quality Development, and Market Development. | (i) Development of Export Infrastructure: APEDA recognizes the importance of infrastructure for the growth of agro-industries and the export of agricultural products in the value chain. The scheme component covers both fresh produce and processed food products. The objective of the scheme is to reduce losses caused due to spoilage and to ensure quality production of agro products. To achieve this, it seeks to set up post-harvest handling facilities. Under this component, assistance is provided for the following: | a) Infrastructure such as packhouse facilities with packing/grading lines Pre- cooling units with cold storage and refrigerated transportation, etc. | b) Cable system for handling crops like banana | c) Common infrastructure facilities | d) Pre-shipment treatment facilities such as irradiation, Vapour Heat Treatment (VHT), and Hot Water Dip Treatment (HWDT) for compliance with the Phyto-Sanitary requirements of importing countries Infrastructure for processing facilities (process food sector) for addressing missing gaps which may include equipment like X-ray, Screening, Sortex, filth/metal detector, sensors, vibrators or any new equipment or technology for food safety and quality requirements | (ii) Quality Development: To participate/engage in international trade, it is necessary to comply with the Food Safety requirements of different countries. Several importing countries demand adherence to stringent Maximum Residue Levels (MRLs). Some of the developed importing countries have set up MRLs at a very low level. For this, high-precision equipment is required to be installed by the food testing labs. Under this component, assistance is provided to comply with the prescribed standards of importing countries. Assistance under this component covers the following: | a) Installation of quality management systems, | b) Laboratory testing equipment, | c) Hand-held devices for capturing farm-level peripheral coordinates for traceability systems and testing of samples etc. | d) Testing of water, soil, residues or pesticides, veterinary drugs, hormones, toxins, heavy | metal, contaminants, etc. | (iii) Market Development: | This component helps exporters achieve market access in new markets and helps sustain their | presence in the existing markets. It covers structured marketing strategies for the export of food products, market intelligence for making informed decisions, international exposure, skill | development, capacity building, and high-quality packaging. The assistance under this | component covers the following: | a) Participation in International trade fairs | b) Exchange of trade delegations | c) Organizing buyer-seller meets | d) Developing packaging standards for new products and upgrading the existing standards

scheme_name: Agriculture And Processed Foods Export Promotion Scheme Of APEDA For The 15th Finance Commission Cycle (2021-22 To 2025-26)
question: What are the general requirements and conditions (across all components)?
answer: - Assistance will be applicable for all APEDA scheduled products. | - The date of submission of the online application in APEDA shall be considered as the date of receipt of an application for grant of principal approval. scheme_name: GEN-NEXT Support for Innovative Startups (GENESIS)
question: What does GENESIS stand for, and which ministry has launched it?
answer: GENESIS stands for "Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups." It has been launched by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, and is implemented by the MeitY Startup Hub (MSH).

scheme_name: GEN-NEXT Support for Innovative Startups (GENESIS)
question: What is the total budget and duration of the GENESIS scheme?
answer: The total budgetary outlay for the GENESIS scheme is ₹4,90,00,00,000/- (₹490 Crore). The scheme is operational for a duration of 5 years.

scheme_name: GEN-NEXT Support for Innovative Startups (GENESIS)
question: Which cities or regions does the GENESIS scheme primarily target?
answer: The GENESIS scheme primarily targets Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities and towns across India. The scheme aims to discover, support, grow, and accelerate successful startups in these cities, ensuring an inclusive startup ecosystem beyond metropolitan areas.

scheme_name: GEN-NEXT Support for Innovative Startups (GENESIS)
question: How many startups does the GENESIS scheme aim to impact?
answer: The GENESIS scheme envisages impacting and consolidating 10,000+ (more than ten thousand) tech startups over the course of its 5-year duration.

scheme_name: GEN-NEXT Support for Innovative Startups (GENESIS)
question: What are the 4 funding/support components available under the GENESIS scheme?
answer: The 4 components under the GENESIS scheme are: | - Ideation Support (Entrepreneur in Residence - EiR): Funding up to ₹10,00,000/- (₹10 Lakhs) for early-stage startups; no matching fund required. | - Pilot (Proof-of-Concept) Support: Average funding of ₹40,00,000/- (₹40 Lakhs), up to ₹50,00,000/- (₹50 Lakhs); no matching fund required. | - Investment Support: Average funding of ₹40,00,000/- (₹40 Lakhs), up to ₹50,00,000/- (₹50 Lakhs); requires 1:1 private sector matching fund. | - Deep-tech Startup Support: Funding up to ₹1,00,00,000/- (₹1 Crore) per startup; no matching fund required.

scheme_name: GEN-NEXT Support for Innovative Startups (GENESIS)
question: Which funding component requires a matching contribution from the private sector?
answer: Only the Investment Support component requires a private sector matching fund in the ratio of 1:1. This means that for every rupee provided by the government under this component, the startup (or its investors) must arrange an equal amount from private sector sources. The Pilot (Proof-of-Concept) Support, Ideation Support (EiR), and Deep-tech Startup Support components do not require any matching fund.

scheme_name: GEN-NEXT Support for Innovative Startups (GENESIS)
question: Who are the eligible Implementing Agencies (IAs) under the GENESIS scheme?
answer: An Implementing Agency must be a legal entity and must fall under one of the following categories: | • Entity registered under Section 8 of the Companies Act. | • Society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860. | • Trust registered under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882. | • Statutory body created through an Act of the legislature. | • Incubator, Accelerator, or Educational Institute recognised by the University Grants Commission (UGC) / All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), or formed under a Central/State Act. | • Any other startup ecosystem entity engaged in supporting startups.

scheme_name: GEN-NEXT Support for Innovative Startups (GENESIS)
question: What are the eligibility conditions for a startup to apply under GENESIS?
answer: A startup must meet all of the following conditions to be eligible: | • Should be a beneficiary of a MeitY scheme or registered with MeitY Startup Hub (MSH). | • Should be registered with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT). | • Indian promoters must hold at least 51% shareholding in the startup at the time of application, as per the Companies Act, 2013. | • Must have a full-time Chief Executive Officer (CEO). | • Must have market-ready products and be seeking funds for business development and commercialisation (applicable in certain categories).

scheme_name: GEN-NEXT Support for Innovative Startups (GENESIS)
question: Who are the target beneficiaries of the GENESIS scheme?
answer: The GENESIS scheme targets all stakeholders engaged in the creation, promotion, and acceleration of the startup ecosystem in India. This includes: | • Students, faculty, and academic institutions. | • Budding entrepreneurs. | • Startup companies and their employees. | • Incubators, Centres of Excellence (CoEs), and accelerators. | • Mentors and investors. | • Corporates engaged in innovation-based growth.

scheme_name: GEN-NEXT Support for Innovative Startups (GENESIS)
question: How can one apply or get more information about the GENESIS scheme?
answer: Applicants can visit the official MeitY Startup Hub portal at https://msh.meity.gov.in/ for scheme details, eligibility, notifications, and the application process. For further queries, contact MeitY Startup Hub at: | • Email: meity-sthub@gov.in | • Phone: 011-24301244 | • Office: MeitY Startup Hub, 2044, Electronics Niketan, 6, CGO Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi - 110003.
