answer: The disbursement of the assistance will be in two installments: | a) 1st Installment: 75% of the sanctioned amount will be released as an advance. | b) 2nd Installment: 25% of the sanctioned amount will be in the form of reimbursement.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Research & Development Scheme
question: What Percentage Of The Financial Assistance Be Disbursed In The First Installments?
answer: In the 1st Installment: 75% of the sanctioned amount will be released as an advance.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Research & Development Scheme
question: What Percentage Of The Financial Assistance Be Disbursed In The Second Installments?
answer: In the 2nd Installment: 25% of the sanctioned amount will be in the form of reimbursement.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: What is the 'Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme'?
answer: The 'Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme' is a component of the National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) launched by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India to make available the credit to handloom weavers at concessional interest rates.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: What is the aim of the Scheme?
answer: The scheme aims to provide adequate and timely assistance from the banks to the handloom sector to meet their credit requirements for term loan & working capital in a flexible and cost effective manner across the country.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: Which banks are eligible to participate in the 'Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme'?
answer: All Scheduled Commercial Banks, Regional Rural Banks, State Cooperative Banks, District Central Co-operative Banks and any financial institution with the approval of Competent Authority of Ministry of Textiles, GoI.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: What are the key benefits of the scheme?
answer: The Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme offers various benefits, including Margin Money Assistance, Interest Subvention, and Credit Guarantee.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: What is the rate of Margin Money Assistance for Individual Handloom Weaver/Weaver Entrepreneur?
answer: Individual Handloom Weaver/Weaver Entrepreneur - Margin Money assistance @20% of loan amount, subject to maximum of ₹25,000/-.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: What is the rate of Margin Money Assistance for Handloom organization?
answer: Handloom organization - Margin money assistance @20% of loan amount, subject to maximum of ₹20.00 lakh (margin money @₹2.00 lakhs for every 100 weaver/worker). Additional margin money requirement, if any as per banking norms will be borne by the beneficiary Agency.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: What is the maximum Margin Money Assistance provided to Primary Handloom Weavers' Co-operative Societies/Apex Handloom Weavers' Co-operative Societies/State Handloom Corporations?
answer: Margin money assistance to Primary Handloom Weavers' Co-operative Societies/Apex Handloom Weavers' Co-operative Societies/State Handloom Corporations will be provided on the recommendation of State Director of Handlooms.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: Who is eligible for Interest Subvention under the 'Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme'?
answer: Subsidized loans at concessional interest rate of 6% for a period of three years will be available to eligible handloom organizations only. However, this is subject to interest subvention cap only upto 7% by the Government of India.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: How long is the Interest Subvention applicable after the first disbursal of the loan?
answer: Interest subvention as applicable will be provided maximum for 3 years from the date of first disbursal.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: Which handloom organizations are eligible for Credit Guarantee under the 'Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme'?
answer: The eligible handloom organizations will be guaranteed by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC)/Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro & Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), as per decision of the Bank/Financial Institution concerned. Guarantee cover will be effective from the date of disbursement of loan for 3 years.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: Where is the Margin Money Assistance transferred for Handloom Organizations?
answer: Margin money assistance will be transferred directly to loan account of Handloom Organization.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: What is the method of fund transfer for Interest Subsidy and Credit Guarantee Fee under the scheme?
answer: The interest subsidy and credit guarantee fee will be transferred to the concerned bank.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: Who are eligible to avail loans under the 'Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme'?
answer: Following agencies are eligible to avail loan from the Banks/Financial Institutions: | - Handloom Weavers involved in weaving activity, | - Weaver Entrepreneur, | - Self Help Groups, | - Joint Liability Groups, | - Handloom organizations, including Primary Handloom Weavers' Co-operative Societies, | - Apex Handloom Weavers' Co-operative Societies, State Handloom Corporations and | - Producers' Companies/Consortia promoted by handloom weavers including those promoted under Cluster/Mega Cluster/Handloom Parks under SITP or other schemes of the Ministry of Textiles

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: What is the eligibility criterion for individuals who have already availed Margin Money Assistance?
answer: Individual weaver who have already availed margin money assistance will not be eligible for financial assistance in terms of margin money assistance, interest subvention and credit guarantee fee under the strength of Handloom Organization, SHGs etc.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: What is the eligibility criterion for Fresh loan?
answer: Fresh loan may be sanctioned after one year of re-payment of previous mudra loan to the handloom beneficiaries who availed loan in the past and have re-paid. Margin money will be available to all the beneficiaries, while interest subsidy and credit guarantee fee will be available to only Handloom Organizations.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme: Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme
question: How can apply for loan under the scheme?
answer: Eligible beneficiaries are required to approach Participating Bank concerned along with required documents etc. for availing loan benefits under the scheme.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP): Scholarship Component
question: Is there an age limit for the children of handloom weavers who can apply for this scholarship?
answer: The scheme does not mention an age limit for the children of handloom weavers who can apply.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP): Scholarship Component
question: Can you explain the role of the District Collector (DC) (Handlooms)?
answer: The DC (Handlooms) is responsible for sanctioning and releasing funds to the concerned zonal office for onward transfer to the bank account of the handloom weaver/worker or their children.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP): Scholarship Component
question: How is the proposal submitted by the concerned WSC processed at the Zonal Office?
answer: The Zonal Office scrutinizes the proposal and sends the requirement of funds, along with relevant details, to the head office for sanction/release of funds by the District Collector (DC) (Handlooms).

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP): Scholarship Component
question: What is the role of the concerned Weavers' Service Center (WSC) in the application process?
answer: The WSC plays a crucial role in verifying and attesting the documents provided by handloom weavers/workers and forwarding the complete proposal to the Zonal Office.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP): Scholarship Component
question: What are the submission requirements for subsequent years' scholarships?
answer: Subsequent years' scholarships are paid upon submission of the proposal, along with a copy of the mark sheet for the annual exam and admission proof for the next academic session from the relevant institution.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP): Scholarship Component
question: How is the first-year scholarship disbursed?
answer: The first-year scholarship is paid after the admission of the ward of handloom weavers/workers.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP): Scholarship Component
question: Is there an additional stipend provided to scholarship recipients?
answer: Yes, in addition to academic fees, eligible candidates receive a monthly stipend of ₹5,000, subject to a maximum of ₹2,00,000 per child per annum or actuals, whichever is less.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP): Scholarship Component
question: What expenses are covered by the scholarship?
answer: The scholarship covers tuition fees, admission fees, examination fees, and other annual fees/charges required by the academic institution.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP): Scholarship Component
question: How is the scholarship amount disbursed?
answer: The scholarship amount is disbursed through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly to the bank account of the concerned handloom weaver/worker or their children.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP): Scholarship Component
question: What educational institutions are eligible for this scholarship?
answer: Central and State government-recognised and funded Textile Institutions are eligible for this scholarship.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP): Scholarship Component
question: Can you clarify the need-based approach mentioned in the scheme?
answer: The need-based approach means that the scholarship is provided based on the financial needs of the handloom weavers' children, ensuring that those who require it the most receive support.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP): Scholarship Component
question: What is the financial support offered under this scholarship?
answer: The scholarship provides a maximum of ₹2,00,000 per annum for up to 2 children of handloom weavers/workers for pursuing diploma, undergraduate, or postgraduate courses at recognized government-funded textile institutions.

scheme_name: National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP): Scholarship Component
question: How long is the NHDP Scholarship Component intended to be implemented?
answer: The scheme is designed to be implemented from the financial year 2021-22 to 2025-26.

scheme_name: Niramaya Health Insurance Scheme
question: What is Niramaya scheme?
answer: Niramaya Health Insurance Scheme ,launched by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, aims to provide affordable health insurance to the Persons with Disabilities (PwDs).

scheme_name: Niramaya Health Insurance Scheme
question: What are the benefits under the scheme?
answer: - Health insurance coverage. | - Outpatient department (OPD) treatment. | - Regular medical checkups. | - Dental care. | - Surgery. | - Non-surgical/hospitalization. | - Ongoing therapies. | - Alternative medicine. | - Transportation costs

scheme_name: Niramaya Health Insurance Scheme
question: What is the health insurance maximum coverage amount?
answer: This scheme provides affordable health insurance cover of up to ₹1,00,000/-.

scheme_name: Niramaya Health Insurance Scheme
question: Is there any limitation of hospitals to avail this scheme benfits?

scheme_name: Niramaya Health Insurance Scheme
question: Is this is a health insurence scheme?
answer: Yes

scheme_name: Niramaya Health Insurance Scheme
question: Who will be covered under this scheme?
answer: All PwDs who have at least one of the disabilities under the National Trust Act, 1999 with valid disability certificate are eligible to apply for the scheme.

scheme_name: Niramaya Health Insurance Scheme
question: What is the enrolment process?
answer: Parents/guardian of the PwD will visit the nearest RO for Niramaya enrolment with required documents.

scheme_name: Niramaya Health Insurance Scheme
question: How to find the nearest for Niramaya enrolment ?

scheme_name: Niramaya Health Insurance Scheme

scheme_name: Niramaya Health Insurance Scheme
question: How the reimbursement can be avail under this scheme?
answer: All claims for settlement under Niramaya have to be submitted to the centres of the insurance provider | in the prescribed Claim Form along with relevant vouchers / bills, etc. (preferably within 30 days of treatment) or discharge from hospital.

scheme_name: NIELIT Internship Programme
question: What Shall Be The Amount Of Stipend Paid To The Interns?
answer: For S&T section/wing interns: ₹ 5,000/- per month. | For non-S&T section/wing interns: ₹ 3,000/- per month.

scheme_name: NIELIT Internship Programme
question: To Which Divisions Will The Interns Be Attached?
answer: Every batch of interns or individual interns, as the case may be, will have a Scientific/Technical Project Supervisor/Mentor to be appointed by the Wing/Section Head of NIELIT Haridwar.

scheme_name: NIELIT Internship Programme
question: Students From Which Education Streams Can Apply For This Internship?
answer: Students from all streams may undertake this internship.

scheme_name: NIELIT Internship Programme
question: What Shall Be The Deliverables On The Part Of The Interns?
answer: At the end of the Internship Programme, all the interns will be required to submit a report on the work undertaken.

scheme_name: NIELIT Internship Programme
question: Can School Students Also Apply For This Internship?
answer: The applicant should be an Indian student from a recognized university in India/abroad who has secured at least 60% marks in the last held degree or certificate examination and: | a) Who has completed or pursuing a Diploma. | OR | b) Who has completed or pursuing Graduation/Bachelor's education/Engineering/ etc. | OR | c) Who has completed or pursuing an Integrated or Dual Degree/Master/Post Graduate degree/ etc.

scheme_name: NIELIT Internship Programme
question: How Many Interns Are Taken In A Month?
answer: A maximum of five (05) interns shall be engaged for the S&T section at NIELIT Haridwar in a financial year. | A maximum of five (05) interns shall be engaged for non - the S&T section at NIELIT Haridwar in a financial year.

scheme_name: NIELIT Internship Programme
question: What Shall Be The Duration Of The Internship?
answer: The minimum duration of the internship shall be as defined or prescribed in the curriculum and endorsed by the Sponsoring institution. | Duration can be a maximum of 6 months and shall not be extendable beyond 6 months in any case.

scheme_name: NIELIT Internship Programme
question: Does This Internship Guarantee Placement In NIELIT?
answer: This internship is neither an employment nor an assurance of employment.

scheme_name: NIELIT Internship Programme
question: What Is The Attendance Criteria For This Internship Scheme?
answer: A minimum of 80% attendance is required to be maintained in a month, failing which a Stipend and certificate of Internship shall not be given to the Intern.

scheme_name: NIELIT Internship Programme
question: What Shall Be The Mode Of Disbursal Of The Amount Of The Stipend?
answer: The stipend shall be paid in non-cash mode only via Cheque/NEFT/RTGS etc.

scheme_name: NIELIT Internship Programme
question: When Shall The Certificate Of Completion Be Provided To The Intern?
answer: Certificates will be issued by NIELIT Haridwar to the interns on completion of the Internship and submission of the Report duly countersigned by the supervisor/mentor and accepted by the Wing/Section Head.

scheme_name: AICTE-National Initiative for Training of Technical Teachers (for Inductee Teachers) Scheme

scheme_name: AICTE-National Initiative for Training of Technical Teachers (for Inductee Teachers) Scheme
question: Through which platform the training would be provided?
answer: On SWAYAM platform through the NITTT portal.

scheme_name: AICTE-National Initiative for Training of Technical Teachers (for Inductee Teachers) Scheme
question: How many modules are there in the training ?
answer: Eight modules.

scheme_name: AICTE-National Initiative for Training of Technical Teachers (for Inductee Teachers) Scheme
question: What is the main purpose of the scheme?
answer: The purpose of this scheme is to provide a framework for training of Inductee Teachers in AICTE approved institutions.

scheme_name: AICTE-National Initiative for Training of Technical Teachers (for Inductee Teachers) Scheme
question: When was this scheme launched?
answer: The scheme was launched in 2020.

scheme_name: AICTE-National Initiative for Training of Technical Teachers (for Inductee Teachers) Scheme
question: What is the duration of the program?
answer: Three(3) years.

scheme_name: AICTE-National Initiative for Training of Technical Teachers (for Inductee Teachers) Scheme
question: In which portal the teachers need to register?

scheme_name: AICTE-National Initiative for Training of Technical Teachers (for Inductee Teachers) Scheme
question: Is there any certificate provided?
answer: Yes, Only after successful completion of all the three phases, a final training completion certificate shall be issued to the Inductee Teacher.

scheme_name: AICTE-National Initiative for Training of Technical Teachers (for Inductee Teachers) Scheme
question: How many phases are there in this training program?
answer: Three phases.

scheme_name: AICTE-National Initiative for Training of Technical Teachers (for Inductee Teachers) Scheme
question: Is there any registration fee?
answer: One-time registration fee as notified from time to time (currently, it is ₹ 2,000/-) is to be paid to the Coordinating Institute.

scheme_name: AICTE-National Initiative for Training of Technical Teachers (for Inductee Teachers) Scheme
question: Is there any certification fee?
answer: The module based certification fee as notified from time to time (currently ₹ 1,000/- per module) is required to be paid to the Coordinating Institute for each module.

scheme_name: AICTE-National Initiative for Training of Technical Teachers (for Inductee Teachers) Scheme
question: Who is eligible for this scheme?
answer: All the teachers working in technical institutions/universities imparting technical education.

scheme_name: Nikshay Poshan Yojana
question: Who is eligible to receive the DBT benefit under the Nikshay Poshan Yojana?
answer: Any TB patient notified in the Nikshay portal on or after 1st April 2018, whether treated in the public or private sector, is eligible. Pediatric patients are also eligible.

scheme_name: Nikshay Poshan Yojana
question: What benefit will I receive under the scheme?
answer: ₹1,000 under this scheme.

scheme_name: Nikshay Poshan Yojana
question: What documents are required to receive the benefit?
answer: - A copy of your bank passbook, canceled cheque, or bank statement | - Aadhaar card (if available, but not mandatory) | - If using a family member's bank account, a written consent form is required.

scheme_name: Nikshay Poshan Yojana
question: Can I receive the benefit if I don't have a bank account?
answer: Yes, but you must open a savings bank account, preferably Aadhaar-linked. Health workers can help you open an account under schemes like Jan Dhan Yojana.

scheme_name: Nikshay Poshan Yojana
question: How will I receive the payment?
answer: Once your bank account is validated by PFMS (Public Financial Management System), the amount is directly credited to your account. You'll also get an SMS confirmation.

scheme_name: Nikshay Poshan Yojana
question: How can I check if my bank details are validated?
answer: Your health provider or treatment supporter can check the validation status in Nikshay. If your account is rejected, they will assist you in correcting it.

scheme_name: Nikshay Poshan Yojana
question: What happens if I move to another district during treatment?
answer: Your benefits will be transferred to the new district. The current district TB unit will continue processing your payments based on your updated location in Nikshay.

scheme_name: Nikshay Poshan Yojana
question: Can I opt out of receiving the benefit?
answer: Yes. If you do not wish to receive the DBT benefit, you must submit a written declaration. Your record in Nikshay will be marked as "Forego Benefits."

scheme_name: Nikshay Poshan Yojana
question: What should I do if I haven't received the payment?
answer: - Contact your healthcare provider or treatment supporter | - Call the national helpline: 1800-11-6666 | - Check if your bank details are validated and benefit status is approved in Nikshay

scheme_name: NITI Internship Scheme
question: - Will I get a stipend for this internship?
answer: No, it is an unpaid internship.

scheme_name: NITI Internship Scheme
question: - What is the minimum and maximum duration of the internship?
answer: The minimum duration for the internship is 6 weeks and the maximum duration is 6 months.

scheme_name: NITI Internship Scheme
question: - Can I apply offline for the internship?

scheme_name: NITI Internship Scheme

scheme_name: NITI Internship Scheme

scheme_name: NITI Internship Scheme
question: - Who can I contact if I face web-related problems during the application?
answer: For any web-related issues while filling out the application, you can contact nic-niti@gov.in

scheme_name: NITI Internship Scheme

scheme_name: NITI Internship Scheme
question: - Will I be informed if my application is rejected?
answer: No. Only those who are selected will be contacted for further process.

scheme_name: NITI Internship Scheme
question: - When can I apply again for the internship if my application gets rejected once?
answer: You can re-apply for the internship when you have met all the requirements as mentioned in the eligibility criteria.

scheme_name: NITI Internship Scheme

answer: Yes, you can, if it is not in the same financial year as your previous internship. You are allowed to do the internship only once in a financial year (01st April of a year to 31st March of the next is called the financial year).

scheme_name: National Mission on Edible Oils- Oil Palm
question: What is the fund flow mechanism for the scheme?
answer: Release of Central and States' share for this scheme will be through PFMS system. Both the GoI and State share of funds shall be transferred through defined mechanism of PFMS.

scheme_name: National Mission on Edible Oils- Oil Palm
question: Is there a role of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) under the scheme?
answer: The State Governments may develop a sound mechanism for involvement of PRIs in the formulation, prioritization of activities & identification of beneficiaries at grass root level and ensure involvement of NGOs, Self Help Groups and Private companies for selection of beneficiary, identification and mapping of priority areas, liaising with processors, state officials and SAUs, etc.

scheme_name: National Mission on Edible Oils- Oil Palm
question: What is the role of processors in the Mission?
answer: The processors are eligible for setting up of seed gardens and nurseries, distribution of planting material etc. The processors will submit their oil palm area expansion target and component wise Annual Action Plan (AAP) to the State for its implementation in the state.

scheme_name: National Mission on Edible Oils- Oil Palm
question: Is there any age criteria for availing scheme benefits?
answer: Any farmer who owns the land can avail benefits under the scheme.

scheme_name: National Mission on Edible Oils- Oil Palm
question: Is there a preference for certain gender /caste of farmers?
answer: All farmers are to be considered under the scheme, however, the resources for Schedule Caste (17%) and Schedule Tribe (8%) will be earmarked for utilization under all the components of NMEO.

scheme_name: National Mission on Edible Oils- Oil Palm
question: Is there an area restriction?
answer: No area restriction is applicable for individual farmers for availing subsidy/ intervention.

scheme_name: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme
question: What is the objective of the scheme?
answer: The primary objective is to support talented students from low-income families so that financial constraints do not force them to discontinue education after Class VIII.

scheme_name: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme
question: How many scholarships are awarded under scheme each year?
answer: Approximately 1 lakh fresh scholarships are awarded every year to selected students of Class IX.

scheme_name: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme
question: What is the scholarship amount under scheme?
answer: Each selected student receives ₹12,000 per annum (₹1,000 per month).

scheme_name: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme

question: Q1. What Is The Primary Objective Of The National Productivity Council (NPC)?

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q2. What Services Does NPC Offer To Improve Productivity And Competitiveness?
answer: A2. NPC offers a range of services, including consultancy, training for capacity building, action research, and evaluation studies, customized to suit the client's needs for improving productivity and competitiveness.

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q3. What Is The Code Of Conduct Expected From Interns During Their Internship At NPC?
answer: A3. Interns are expected to demonstrate sincerity, punctuality, courtesy, cooperative attitude, willingness to learn, proper etiquette, and appropriate attire. They must also maintain workplace decorum throughout their internship period.

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q4. What Are The Responsibilities Of Interns During Their Internship At NPC?
answer: A4. Interns are expected to perform the assigned tasks and duties with due care and diligence as per the instructions provided to them. They must also submit a project/assignment report/paper at the end of their internship to the concerned Head(s) regarding their learning experience.

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q5. How Does NPC Ensure Confidentiality During The Internship Period?
answer: A5. Interns are required not to disclose any proprietary or confidential information relating to the services, contract, or business operations of NPC or its clients during or after the internship period without seeking prior written consent from NPC.

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q6. What Happens If An Intern Violates The Non-Disclosure Agreement?
answer: A6. If an intern violates the non-disclosure agreement, NPC may take necessary action to safeguard its interests and the interests of the Council.

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q7. Can NPC Terminate An Intern's Engagement Or Program During The Internship?
answer: A7. Yes, NPC has the authority to terminate an intern's engagement or program at any time, especially in cases of misconduct or discipline, without providing any reason. NPC's decision in this regard is considered final.

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q8. Can Interns Voluntarily Leave The Internship Program?

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q9. Does The Internship Program Guarantee Employment With NPC?

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q10. What Happens If NPC Discovers Any Material Error In An Intern's Application?

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q11. Are Interns Allowed To Take Any Information About NPC's Software, Hardware, And Policies Outside The Organization?

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q12. Who Retains The Copyright Of The Software/Applications Developed By Interns During The Internship?

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q13. What Rights Does NPC Have Over The Work Assigned To Interns During Their Internship?

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: Who can apply to this scheme?
answer: Any retail trader, shopkeepers and self-employed person with annual turn-over not exceeding Rs.1.5 crore, in the age group of 18-40 year can subscribe this Scheme. They should not be an income tax payer or a member of National Pension Scheme (NPS - GOVT FUNDED), Employees' State Insurance Corporation scheme (ESIC) and Employees' Provident Fund Organization (EPFO) and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan.

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: How much pension would be received through this scheme and at what age?
answer: Under the Scheme, a minimum monthly assured pension of Rs. 3000/- will commence after the beneficiary attains the age of 60 years.

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: How can I enrol for this scheme?
answer: Under the scheme, the beneficiary may visit the nearest Common Service Centre and get enrolled in the scheme using her/his Aadhar number and savings bank account/Jan-Dhan account number on self-certification basis. Nearest Common Service Centres (CSCs) can be located at locator.csccloud.in/.

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: Is the Proof of Age/DOB a required document?
answer: No, Self-Certification and age as in Aadhaar card will be the basis for enrollment. However, any change of date of birth will not be allowed later.

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: What are the exit provisions?
answer: Exit provisions are as under: | in case an eligible beneficiary exits this Scheme within a period of less than ten years from the date of joining the Scheme by him, then his share of contribution only will be returned to him with savings bank rate of interest payable thereon. | if an eligible beneficiary exits after completion of a period of ten years or more from the date of joining the Scheme by him but before his age of sixty years, then his share of contribution only shall be returned to him along with accumulated interest thereon as actually earned by the Pension Fund or the interest at the savings bank interest rate thereon, whichever is higher | if an eligible beneficiary has given regular contributions and died due to any cause, her/his spouse shall be entitled to continue with the Scheme subsequently by payment of regular contribution as applicable or exit by receiving the share of contribution paid by such beneficiary along with accumulated interest, as actually earned thereon by the Pension Fund or at the savings bank interest rate thereon, whichever is higher | in case of exit on account of clauses (i), (ii) and (iii) above, the accumulated share of Government's contribution shall be credited back to the Pension Fund | any other exit provision, including nomination, as may be decided by the Central Government by issuing instructions from time to time. | after death of beneficiary and his or her spouse, the corpus shall be credited back to the fund;

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: What would be the role of LIC?
answer: The scheme is being implemented through LIC and CSCs. LIC is the pension fund manager and also responsible for pension pay out.

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: Is auto-debit facility available?
answer: Yes. Monthly subscription shall be automatically debited on a fixed date of every month from her/his linked savings account. Only, first subscription will be paid in cash for which receipt will be provided by concerned CSCs/VLEs.

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: Is there a fee for enrollment in this scheme?
answer: There is no administrative cost to the beneficiary as it is a Social Security Scheme of the Government of India. The enrollment under the Scheme is free for beneficiaries.

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: Is there a provision for family pension?
answer: Yes, there is a provision for family pension under the scheme. It is applicable only to the spouse of the beneficiary. If the beneficiary dies, after the pension has commenced, the spouse of the beneficiary shall be entitled to receive 50 % of the pension.

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: If the payment of the subscription is stopped, can the beneficiary re-join / revive the application again?
answer: If the payment of subscription has been stopped or delayed, the beneficiary can revive the scheme after paying the outstanding subscription with a nominal interest as decided by the Government.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What is NPS Vatsalya?
answer: NPS Vatsalya is a contributory pension system under the National Pension System (NPS). Its objective is to create a pension society and encourage the empowerment of children by inculcating the habit of saving for retirement from an early age.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: Who can subscribe to NPS Vatsalya?
answer: NPS Vatsalya is open to all citizens of India who are under the age of eighteen years. The account will be opened and operated by the guardian on behalf of the minor.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What are the benefits of opening a NPS Vatsalya account?
answer: Opening an NPS Vatsalya account provides the child with a head start on saving for retirement and offers valuable financial lessons from an early age. It instils the importance of financial planning and discipline, which can benefit the child throughout their life.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: How is the NPS Vatsalya account operated?
answer: The account is opened by the natural or legal guardian in the name of the minor. | The minor is the sole beneficiary of the account. | A unique Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) is issued in the minor's name. | The account is operated by the guardian for the exclusive benefit of the minor until they reach the age of majority (18 years).

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What is the procedure for opening a NPS Vatsalya account?
answer: The NPS Vatsalya account can be opened through: | Points of Presence (POPs) registered with PFRDA (Major banks, India Post and Pension Funds etc), either online or in physical mode, directly or through Retirement Advisors/Pension Agents. | The online platform (eNPS) of NPS Trust.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What are the KYC requirements for opening a NPS Vatsalya account?
answer: The KYC norms applicable to the guardian must be in accordance with the standards stipulated by PFRDA. | In the case of a court-appointed legal guardian, a copy of the court order regarding the appointment of the Legal Guardian must be submitted along with the KYC documents.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What documents of the minor are required for opening a NPS Vatsalya account?
answer: For the minor, proof of date of birth is required. Acceptable documents include: | Birth certificate of the minor School leaving certificate / Matriculations issued by Higher Secondary Board of respective states, ICSE, CBSE, etc. | Passport of the minor | PAN

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: Is a bank account required for opening a NPS Vatsalya account?
answer: The bank account details of the minor or a joint account with the minor are not mandatory for opening the account for Indian residents but will be required at the time of partial withdrawal or exit before the age of 18. | For non-residents, details of NRE or NRO account are mandatory.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What happens when the minor attains the age of 18 years?
answer: The account will continue to be operational and will be seamlessly transitioned into a NPS -Tier 1 Account under the All Citizen Model. | Upon transitioning, the features, benefits, and exit norms of the NPS-Tier I for All Citizen Model will apply. | A fresh KYC of the subscriber must be carried out within three months of reaching majority. | Contributions to the NPS Tier1 Account will be allowed after the submission of fresh KYC.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: Can an NRI or OCI open a NPS Vatsalya account?
answer: The minor must be a citizen of India. | The guardian can be a Non-Resident Indian (NRI) or Overseas Citizen of India (OCI). | A separate form is applicable for guardians who are NRIs or OCIs. | A bank account (NRE or NRO) is mandatory when the guardian is an NRI or OCI.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: Is it required to furnish a nomination while joining the scheme?
answer: No, the guardian becomes the nominee under the scheme.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: How many NPS Vatsalya accounts can I open?
answer: The guardian can open a single account (per child) for the minor.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: Can a guardian who is a NPS subscriber open a NPS Vatsalya account for a minor?
answer: Yes, a guardian who is an NPS subscriber can open an NPS Vatsalya account in the name of the minor.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What are the minimum and maximum contributions for Accumulation Phase under the NPS Vatsalya account?
answer: The minimum contribution is ₹ 1000 per annum, with no upper limit on the maximum contribution. | The initial contribution required for enrollment under the scheme is ₹ 1000.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What are the modes of contribution available for Accumulation Phase under NPS Vatsalya?
answer: A subscriber can contribute through any of the following modes: | Physical mode: By visiting any registered service provider (PoP) and depositing a cheque/cash along with the NPS contribution slip. | Online mode: | o Online facility provided by PoPs. | o eNPS platform of NPS Trust.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What choices do I need to exercise for Accumulation Phase under NPS Vatsalya?
answer: All choices available under the NPS All Citizen model are also available for NPS Vatsalya, including: | Choice of CRA (Central Recordkeeping Agency): From the registered CRAs with PFRDA. | Choice of Pension Fund (PF): From the registered PFs with PFRDA. | Choice of Allocation of Funds: | o Auto Choice: | Conservative Life Cycle Fund (LC25) | Moderate Life Cycle Fund (LC50) - Default | Aggressive Life Cycle Fund (LC75) | o Active Choice: | Equity (E) - Maximum 75% | Corporate Bonds (C) - Up to 100% | Government Securities (G) - Up to 100% | Alternate Assets (A) - Maximum 5%

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: How are the contributions for Accumulation Phase invested in NPS Vatsalya?
answer: The contributions made by the subscriber are invested according to the choices (Pension Fund and Asset allocation) exercised and recorded with CRA, in line with the investment guidelines prescribed by PFRDA for each asset class: | Asset Class E - Equity shares of Top 200 companies under NSE/BSE in terms of market capitalisation. | Asset Class C - Corporate Bonds/Debentures that are listed and rated not below A. | Asset Class G - Government securities and State Development Loans. | Asset Class A - Alternate Assets. For detailed investment guidelines, refer to the Circulars Section of the PFRDA website.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: How do I know about the performance of my NPS investments under Accumulation Phase?
answer: The performance of your NPS investments is available in the Statement of Transactions, which can be accessed online through the subscriber web login or mobile app. Periodic statements are sent by the CRA to the registered email ID of the subscriber, and a physical statement for the financial year is sent to the correspondence address of the subscriber.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What happens if I don't make the minimum contribution under Accumulation Phase? Will my account be closed?
answer: If the minimum contribution is not received, the account is categorized as 'frozen' and will be activated upon contributing to the account. The NPS account will be closed only when a subscriber submits a request (physical or online) for exit from NPS to a service provider (PoP).

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: How do I access my NPS account under Accumulation Phase?
answer: Subscribers can access their Pension Account through: | Physical mode: By visiting their service provider (PoP). | Online mode: Using the login credentials provided by CRA in the Account Opening Kit.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: Can I partially withdraw money from the NPS Vatsalya account before 18 years?
answer: Partial withdrawals from your NPS Vatsalya account are allowed to address contingency situations. | The reasons/conditions for partial withdrawal include: | o Education of the minor subscriber | o Treatment of specified illnesses of the minor subscriber | o Disability of more than 75% of the minor subscriber | A maximum amount of up to 25% of contributions (excluding returns) can be partially withdrawn. | This facility is available on a declaration basis after a minimum of 3 years from the date of account opening. | The Partial withdrawal can be made a maximum of three times till the subscriber attains 18 years of age.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What are the exit options under the scheme?
answer: The subscriber can exit on attainment of the age of 18 years. | On such exit, at least eighty percentage of the accumulated corpus available in the account must be utilized for the purchase of an annuity and the remaining balance shall be paid in a lump sum. | In case, the accumulated pension wealth available in the account is equal to or less than two lakh fifty thousand, or the purchase of annuity is not available from empanelled Annuity Service Providers ('ASPs'), the subscriber shall have the option to withdraw the entire accumulated pension wealth.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What happens in case of death before 18 years?
answer: In the event of the minor subscriber's death, the entire accumulated corpus is to be paid to the guardian. | If the guardian registered under the account dies during the account's subsistence, another guardian must be registered on behalf of the minor subscriber by submitting the KYC documents as specified by the PFRDA from time to time. | In case of the death of both parents, the legally appointed guardian can continue the account with or without making contributions to the account, and upon attainment of 18 years of age, the subscriber can exit from the scheme.

answer: -For resolving subscriber grievances, the Authority has notified the PFRDA (Redressal of Subscriber Grievance) Regulations, 2015 and an online platform 'Central Grievance Management System (CGMS)' has been hosted for subscribers to lodge grievances online by logging into his/her NPS account. | - A complaint/grievance has to be resolved by the intermediary concerned as early as possible within a maximum period of 30 days of the receipt of the complaint. | - If a subscriber is not satisfied with the resolution provided, he/she can escalate his grievance to the next higher level for resolution and the escalation matrix is as under:

scheme_name: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
question: What Does NSAP Stand For And When Was It Launched?
answer: NSAP stands for National Social Assistance Programme. NSAP was launched on 15th August 1995.

scheme_name: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
question: What Is The Objective Of NSAP?
answer: In providing social assistance benefits to poor households in the case of old age, death of the breadwinner, and maternity, the NSAP aims at ensuring minimum national standards, in addition to the benefits that the States are currently providing or might provide in future. It also aims at ensuring that social protection to the beneficiaries everywhere in the country is uniformly available without interruption.

scheme_name: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
question: What Are The Components Of NSAP?
answer: The NSAP at its inception in 1995 had three components namely (1) National Old Age Pension Scheme (NOAPS, (2) National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS), and (3) National Maternity Benefit Scheme (NMBS). The National Maternity Benefit Scheme (NMBS) was subsequently transferred on 1st April, 2001 from the Ministry of Rural development to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. | On 1st April 2000 a new Scheme known as Annapurna Scheme was launched. This scheme aimed at providing food security to meet the requirement of those senior citizens who, though eligible, have remained uncovered under the NOAPS. | In February 2009, two new Schemes known as Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) and Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) were introduced. | Presently NSAP comprises of five schemes, namely - (1) Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), (2) Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS), (3) Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS), (4) National Family Benefit Scheme NFBS) and (5) Annapurna.

scheme_name: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
question: Who Implements NSAP?
answer: The NSAP is implemented in the States/UTs in accordance with the general conditions applicable to all components of the NSAP as well as specific conditions applicable to each component. The NSAP Schemes are mainly implemented by the Social Welfare Departments in the States. But NSAP is implemented by Rural Development Department in the States of Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Goa, Meghalaya and West Bengal; by the Department of Women & Child Development in Orissa and Puducherry; by the Revenue Department in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu and by the Department of Labour Employment & Training in Jharkhand. The NSAP extends to both the rural as well as urban areas

scheme_name: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
question: What Is The Basic Eligibility Criterion Under NSAP?
answer: For getting benefits under NSAP the applicant must belong to a Below Poverty Line (BPL) family according to the criteria prescribed by the Govt. of India.

scheme_name: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
question: How Are The Beneficiaries Identified In Rural Areas?
answer: As per the revised eligibility criteria, new beneficiaries will be identified from the BPL list prepared by the States/UTs as per guidelines issued by the Ministry of Rural Development (MORD) for the BPL Census 2002.

scheme_name: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme

answer: They will continue to get the pension as at present without any interruption notwithstanding the fact that their names are not borne on the BPL list, provided they were eligible as per the old criteria.

scheme_name: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
question: How Is IGNOAPS Different From The Earlier National Old Age Pension Scheme (NOAPS)?
answer: Under NOAPS, old age pensions were granted to a person who is 65 years old or higher and who is destitute in the sense of having little or no means of regular income. Pension under IGNOAPS is now granted to a person who is 60 years or above and belongs to a household below the poverty line instead of only to destitute.

scheme_name: National Science Chair- Scientific Excellence
question: How/When can the individual start his NSC Award?
answer: A letter is sent by the SERB to the nominee as well as to the host Institute informing the award of NSC. After receiving the same the nominee has to join the chair within six months of the date of offer letter and to send his / her Acceptance Letter to the Host Institute, indicating the tentative Date / Month when the nominee wants to start the award. Then the Institute will forward his Acceptance / Joining Letter to Science & Engineering Research Board along with the updated details of the bank for transfer of fund through RTGS (in the prescribed format). Based on this letter, SERB will process the file for getting administrative and financial approvals and then a Sanction Order is issued to the Host Institute. The start date, as per joining letter date of the nominee, of the award will be mentioned in the Sanction Order.

scheme_name: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh / Direct Benefits Transfer For LPG
question: What Will Have To Be Done By The LPG Consumer Who Had Already Joined The Scheme Earlier?

answer: Option I (Primary): LPG consumers who have an Aadhaar number must provide their Aadhaar number to LPG distributor using Form 2 and to Bank using Form 1. This is the preferred mode of joining the scheme. | Option II (Secondary): If the LPG consumer does not have an Aadhaar number, he/she can do one of the following: | a. Give Bank details to the LPG distributor in Form 4 | OR | b. Give a 17-digit LPG ID to the Bank using Form 3.

scheme_name: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh / Direct Benefits Transfer For LPG
question: When Can An LPG Consumer Visit The Distributorship For Submitting Aadhaar And Bank Details Seeding Forms To Join PAHAL (DBTL) Scheme?
answer: The LPG consumers can visit their LPG distributorship on any weekday during office hours for submitting the forms. For the convenience of LPG consumers, all distributorships will also remain open on their weekly off day for exclusively receiving Aadhaar & Bank detail seeding forms of the PAHAL (DBTL) scheme till the end of the grace period.

scheme_name: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh / Direct Benefits Transfer For LPG
question: How Does An LPG Consumer Check His/Her PAHAL (DBTL) Joining Status?
answer: To check PAHAL (DBTL) joining status, consumers can log on to the transparency portal of their LPG Company (IOC, BPC, HPC) through www.myLPG.in and follow instructions. On each of the OMC's transparency portals, a call out with the name 'Check DBTL (CTC) Status' has been provided. Consumers can click on this and see the status both for ATC as well as BTC methods.

scheme_name: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh / Direct Benefits Transfer For LPG
question: What Happens Where Transactions Sent To The Bank Fail And How Are They Dealt With?
answer: A) In case some transfers cannot be processed by the banks, they are termed as failures, and the failure cases if any along with the amount is received back from the Sponsor Bank by the OMCs. A report on such failure cases has been provided by the OMC on their portal which is accessible to the distributors as well | as Call Centre. | b) Payments returned will be re-processed twice in a span of 15 days each and if it is still not transferred, the amount will be kept for payment as and when the bank-related issues are resolved. | c) If the amount towards the subsequent cylinder delivered is successfully transferred then the pending amount also will be transferred thereafter. | d) The time period up to which such payments will be kept pending will be 3 months or the end of the current financial year whichever is later.

scheme_name: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh / Direct Benefits Transfer For LPG
question: How Is The Quota Of Subsidized Cylinders Worked Out For New Consumers?
answer: A) The eligibility for the quota of subsidized cylinders for all new connections released is on a pro-rata basis. This is also applicable to CTC consumers. | b) For new connections, CTC consumers will receive both the advance amount (after the booking of the first cylinder) and the subsidy amount (after the delivery of the first cylinder). | c) Thereafter, they will receive a subsidy amount with every cylinder delivery upto the capped subsidized quota of cylinders.

scheme_name: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh / Direct Benefits Transfer For LPG
question: How To Deal With Advance Amounts Given To Consumers When They Are On Transfer?
answer: A) CTC consumers, who are transferred, have to return the advance amount to the parent distributor. In other words, when the Termination Voucher is made the net amount of the Security Deposit of equipment minus the Permanent Advance amount will be refunded to consumers. | b) If such consumers are transferred to another district where PAHAL (DBTL) has been launched, they will be given an advance once they become a consumer at the new location and are handed over the Subscription Voucher. | c) OMC Software has the provision to capture Security deposits and advance amounts separately and account for them in the ERP accounting system. | d) For CTC consumers located in the same city on transfer without any surrendering of equipment and refund of deposit (TTV/CTA), Permanent Advance amount will not be refunded.

scheme_name: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh / Direct Benefits Transfer For LPG

answer: Visibility has been provided to the consumers through the Transparency portal of OMCs (via www.mylpg.in). A call center with a dashboard on all transactions is available for suitable consumer grievance redressal.

scheme_name: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh / Direct Benefits Transfer For LPG

answer: A) For getting any information, providing feedback, and registering any complaint OMCs have a call center which is accessible at Toll-Free No 18002333555. | b) Consumers can also visit http://petroleum.nic.in/dbt/index.htm or visit the transparency portal of their LPG Company (IOC, BPC, HPC) through www.myLPG.in.

scheme_name: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh / Direct Benefits Transfer For LPG

answer: This scheme is managed by All India Council for Technical Education(AICTE).

scheme_name: AICTE-PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT SCHEME
question: Mention one of the main benefits of the scheme.
answer: Under this scheme, Financial grant will be disbursed on reimbursement basis.

scheme_name: AICTE-PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT SCHEME
question: What should be the criteria of the institution?
answer: Institutions should be AICTE approved.

scheme_name: AICTE-PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT SCHEME
question: What is the main objective of the scheme?
answer: The main objective of the scheme is to To enable the meritorious faculties and officers of AICTE to interact at international level to update themselves to the global changes in the concerned field of specializations through paper presentation in conference abroad & within India.

scheme_name: AICTE-PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT SCHEME
question: How many proposal can be submitted at a time by the applicant?
answer: Applicant should submit only one proposal at a time

scheme_name: AICTE-PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT SCHEME
question: When the application should be submitted?
answer: Application should be submitted three months in advance.

scheme_name: AICTE-PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT SCHEME
question: Who are eligible to apply?
answer: Full time regular faculty from the AICTE approved Institute/AICTE approved University Department (with at least 5 years of existence) and the officers of Assistant Director and above on regular and deputation basis in AICTE are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Welfare Fund For Sportspersons
question: Are the financial assistance provided as a lump sum amount?
answer: Yes, a lumpsum ex-gratia financial assistance is provided to the beneficiary.

scheme_name: Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Welfare Fund For Sportspersons
question: Are the sportspersons injured during training covered under this scheme?
answer: Yes, injured sportspersons are eligible for a lump sum ex-gratia financial assistance subject to a maximum of Rs. 10 LPA.

scheme_name: Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Welfare Fund For Sportspersons
question: What are benefits provided to the dependents of a deceased sportsperson?
answer: To such dependents, a lumpsum ex- gratia financial assistance, not exceeding Rs. 5.00 lakh in each case, may be provided to the families of deceased outstanding sportspersons living in indigent circumstances.

scheme_name: Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Welfare Fund For Sportspersons
question: I am a hockey player who has represented India at national level tournaments. I am disabled as a result of a sports injury. Am I eligible to apply?
