scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme
question: Is there any upper limit of loan for claiming the interest subsidy?
answer: A) Interest subsidy is provided for a maximum loan amount of ₹10.00 Lakhs (Loans more than ₹10.00 lakhs will be eligible for interest subsidy up to ₹10 lakhs only). | b) No collateral security or 3rd party guarantee is required for Education Loans sanctioned up to ₹7.50 lakhs. The Loaner Bank (registered under CGFSEL Scheme of NCGTC) is to ensure that the loans less than or equal to ₹7.50 Lacs should be covered under CGFSEL for covering the accounts under CSIS. | c) Financial institutes which are not registered under the CGFSEL Scheme of NCGTC will cover their accounts under CSIS, 2022 (Education Loan Sanctioned as per IBA Model Education Loan Scheme) for the interest charged on loans sanctioned without collateral & 3rd party guarantee and for the maximum amount of ₹7.50 lakhs irrespective of CGFSEL coverage.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme
question: Who is the income certificate issuing authority?
answer: Appropriate authority designated by the respective State/UT Governments.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme
question: Whether it is necessary to submit the income certificate every financial year?
answer: • Income Certificate (covering annual income of entire family of the borrower) is to be submitted at the time of loan sanction/ disbursement of first instalment, as decided by loan disbursing bank. | • Borrowers need not submit income certificate every year.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme
question: How Borrower can claim the subsidy to Government of India?
answer: • Borrower cannot claim the subsidy directly from Gol. | • lt is the prime responsibility of the financing Bank/Branch to claim the subsidy on behalf of the borrower. | • If any lending Bank fails to claim interest subsidy for the current year, backlog/pending claims of interest Subsidy will not be entertained. | • The Ministry of Education shall not be liable for any back-payments due to the failure of the bank to claim of the interest subsidy before the closure of the loan account of the student.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme
question: What is the procedure to check the CSIS subsidy claimed amount of individual education loan accounts?
answer: Canara Bank has created a dedicated web portal for this purpose: https://www.canarabankesis.in/SubsidyEnquiry/SubsidyEnquirV.aspx.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme
question: What is the Payment Process of CSIS?
answer: - The subsidy amount will be credited to PM VIDYALAXMI DIGITAL RUPEE APP (CBDC WALLET) of the beneficiary and on redemption on the app by the beneficiary, the amount will be transferred to the beneficiary loan account. | - It is the sole responsibility of the Loaner Bank to submit the correct Account details of the Beneficiaries for the purpose of crediting the subsidy amount through DBT mode. | - Students to contact the Financing Bank in case of any delay in receiving of the subsidy amount.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme
question: Whom should I have to contact for subsidy amount disbursed by the government?
answer: • The details of the amount credited may be obtained from the concerned financing bank Branch. | • The head office of the concerned Bank may be contacted if the Branch reply is not satisfactory. | • If any lending Bank fails to claim interest subsidy for the current year, backlog/pending claims of interest Subsidy will not be entertained. | • The Ministry of Education shall not be liable for any back-payments due to the failure of the bank to claim of the interest subsidy before the closure of the loan account of the student.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme
question: What is the role of Canara Bank as a Nodal bank?
answer: • Canara Bank has been nominated as Nodal Bank, for the purpose of administering the Interest Subsidy introduced by the Government of India, New Delhi. | • The role of Canara Bank as a Nodal Bank is for the purpose of consolidate the subsidy claims of Member Banks and forward the same to the Concerned Ministry and pass on the subsidy to the Member Banks as and when it is received from the Ministry.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme
question: What is PM VIDYALAXMI DIGITAL RUPEE APP?
answer: - PM VIDYALAXMI DIGITAL RUPEE App is a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) based dedicated mobile application for receiving education loan interest subvention benefits from Dept. Of Higher Education Ministry of Education GoI. | - The application is available for download at Play store for android based mobiles and App store for i-phones | - Mobile number of beneficiaries updated in PM-Vidyalaxmi portal by the financing Bank, against beneficiary claim should be used for downloading the application. | - Beneficiaries can activate their PM VIDYALAXMI DIGITAL Rupee App through AADHAAR based authentication process via OTP received in their AADHAAR registered Mobile number. | - PM VIDYALAXMI DIGITAL Rupee App is applicable for both PM VIDYALAXMI and CSIS interest subvention schemes of Dept. Of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, GoI.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
question: What are the components supported under the scheme?
answer: i. Skilling and Training (Non-traditional and traditional) | ii. Women Leadership and Entrepreneurship | iii. Education (through National Institute of Open Schooling) | iv. Infrastructure Development (through Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram)

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
question: What are the skills taught under the scheme?
answer: Any of the skills approved by the NSQC and registered under the National Qualification Register (NQR) are eligible to be provided under the scheme.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
question: Is there any stipend provided under the scheme?
answer: Yes. | Rs.3000/- per month for beneficiaries undertaking traditional skilling, | Rs. 2000/- per month for beneficiaries undertaking non-traditional (modern) skilling in non residential mode, | Rs. 1000/- per month for beneficiaries undertaking non-traditional (modern) skilling in residential mode (Max 12 months) | Rs. 1000/- for beneficiaries enrolled under education component (Max 6 months), | Rs. 200/- per day for beneficiaries under women leadership and entrepreneurship component

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
question: Does the scheme involves linking trained and certified candidates in modern skilling with placement opportunities?
answer: Placement of minimum 75% of beneficiaries trained under modern skilling are to be ensured by the implementing agency post completion of training program, with at least 50% of them in organised as categorized in the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF)/ Common Cost Norms (CCN) of Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
question: Who are eligible for benefiting under the scheme?
answer: Six notified communities under the NCM Act, i.e., Buddhists, Christian, Jains, Muslims, Parsis and Sikhs are eligible for applying under the scheme. However, up to 25% of seats may be earmarked under traditional skilling and up to 15% under other components for non minority EWS category.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
question: What is the educational qualification required under the scheme?
answer: The educational qualification for Skilling and Training component would be as per National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF) norms and Education component would be as per National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) norms. Candidates with aptitude and leadership qualities will be selected for Women Leadership and Entrepreneurship component.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
question: Are there any seats earmarked for women candidates?
answer: 33% in Skilling and Training component, 50% in Education component and 100% in Women Leadership and Entrepreneurship component are reserved for women candidates.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
question: Are there any seats earmarked for PwD candidates?
answer: 3% of the scheme benefits are earmarked for PwD candidates.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
question: Is there any income criteria?
answer: Up to 25% of seats may be earmarked under traditional skilling and up to 15% under other components for non minority EWS category.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
question: How to register for PM VIKAS scheme?
answer: Visit the SIDH Portal (https://www.skillindiadigital.gov.in/), register as a Learner/Participant (Candidate) or log in if already registered, and complete e-KYC using your personal details

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
question: How to apply for scheme/courses?
answer: Access your dashboard on SIDH portal to find PM VIKAS scheme and job roles. Use filters such as scheme, mode, and sector to find suitable courses or batches.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
question: How to apply for a training batch?
answer: Choose a batch for your preferred job role and submit your interest or application. You may select up to five batches, which will be reviewed by the training partner /training centre.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
question: How to finalize enrolment?
answer: After approval from the training partner / training centre, accept the invitation through your portal to confirm enrolment. Track your application status under the 'Applications' section.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Who launched PM-YASASVI?
answer: PM-YASASVI was launched by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What is the objective of the scheme?
answer: The objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to the OBC, EBC and DNT students studying at post-matriculation or post-secondary stage to enable them to complete their education.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What is the scope of scheme?
answer: These scholarships shall be available for studies in India only and will be awarded by the Government of State/Union Territory to which the applicant actually belongs, i.e. permanently settled.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Who can apply for the scholarships?
answer: Indian nationals belonging to Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Economically Backward Classes (EBCs), and Denotified Nomadic Tribes (DNTs) as notified by the Central Govt./State Govt./UT Admin are eligible.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What does 'Group 1' mean?
answer: "Group 1: Degree and Post Graduate level professional courses" shall mean all Professional courses in Medicine, Engineering, Technology, Planning, Architecture, Design, Fashion Technology, Agriculture, Veterinary & Allied Sciences, Management, Business Finance /Administration, Computer Science/ Applications (ii) Post Graduate Diploma courses in various branches of Management & Medicine(iii) C.A./I.C.W.A./C.S./1.C.F.A. etc. (iv) M.Phil., Ph.D. and Post-Doctoral Programmes (D.Lit., D.Sc. etc.) of Group I, Group II and Group Ill courses. (v) L.L.B, Integrated LL B, L.L.M (vi) Commercial Pilot License Courses from GoI institutes (including helicopter pilot and multiengine) (maximum 20 slots per annum)

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What does 'Group 2' mean?
answer: "Group 2: Other Professional Courses leading to Degree, Diploma, Certificate" shall mean all Professional Courses leading to Degree, M Ed. / M. Pharma., Diploma, Certificate in areas like Pharmacy (B Pharma.), Nursing(B Nursing), BFS, other para-medical branches like rehabilitation, diagnostics etc., Mass Communication, Hotel Management & Catering, Travel/Tourism/Hospitality Management, Interior Decoration, Nutrition& Dietetics, Commercial Art, Financial Services (e.g. Banking, Insurance, Taxation etc.) for which entrance qualification is minimum Sr. Secondary (10+2) and Vocational stream, ITI courses and Polytechnic where entrance qualification is Class XII or above.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What does 'Group 3' mean?
answer: "Group 3: Graduate and Post Graduate course" shall mean: courses not covered under Group 1& Group 2 e.g. BA / B.Sc. / B.Com etc. M.A/ M. Sc./ M.Com etc.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What does 'Group 4' mean?
answer: "Group 4: All post-matriculation (Post Class X level) non-degree courses" shall mean All post-matriculation level non-degree courses for which entrance qualification is High School (Class X), e.g. Senior secondary certificate (class XI and XII ); both general and vocational stream, ITI courses, 3-year diploma courses in Polytechnics, etc.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What does 'Freeship Card' mean?
answer: "Freeship Card" shall mean a card issued by the State Govt./UT Administration that entitles a student eligible for a scholarship under this Scheme, to take admission in an institution, without pre-payment of tuition fee and hostel fee.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: How will the scholarship amount be disbursed?
answer: The entire scholarship amount, including tuition fees, academic allowance, and any other admissible allowance, will be paid directly into the students' bank accounts ONLY through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), preferably through an Aadhaar Based Payment System (Aadhaar Payment Bridge).

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: How are students pursuing professional courses like CA/ICWA/CS/ICFA treated for academic allowance?
answer: Students pursuing CA/ICWA/CS/ICFA shall be treated as day scholars for the purpose of academic allowance.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Are students studying through correspondence/online courses eligible for academic allowance?
answer: No, students studying through correspondence/online courses shall not be eligible for academic allowance.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Will tuition fees be paid to online/correspondence students?
answer: Yes, tuition fees shall be paid to online/correspondence students.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What courses are covered under the scholarship?
answer: The scholarships are available for all recognized post-matriculation or post-secondary courses pursued in recognized institutions.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What educational qualifications are required for eligibility?
answer: Eligible candidates must have passed the Matriculation or higher secondary or any higher examination from a recognized University or Board of Secondary Education.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Are post-graduate medical students eligible for the scholarship?
answer: Yes, but only if they are not allowed to practice during the period of their course.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Is there a limit on the number of scholarships per family?
answer: Yes, only two boys of the same parents/guardian will be entitled to receive scholarships. However, this restriction does not apply to girls.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Can scholarship holders hold other scholarships simultaneously?
answer: No, scholarship holders cannot hold any other scholarship/stipend. They can, however, accept free lodging, grants, or ad-hoc monetary help for specific purposes.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What is the income eligibility criterion for employed and unemployed students?
answer: Employed students whose income combined with their parents/guardians does not exceed ₹2.50 lakh per annum, and unemployed students whose parents/guardians' income does not exceed ₹2.50 lakh per annum are eligible.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Who is not eligible for the scholarship?
answer: Candidates studying in the same stage of education in different subjects after passing one stage, such as pursuing B.Sc. after B.A. or B.Com. after B.A., will not be eligible.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Can a scholarship be cancelled if a scholar changes their course of study or institution without prior approval?
answer: Yes.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Is a scholar liable to refund the scholarship amount if their studies are discontinued during the year?
answer: Yes, a scholar may be liable to refund the scholarship amount at the discretion of the State Government if their studies for which the scholarship has been awarded are discontinued during the year.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: How long is the scholarship payable?
answer: The scholarship once awarded will be payable up to the completion of the course subject to satisfactory academic performance and attendance of 75% in every academic year.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Can the scholarship be renewed if a scholar is unable to appear in the annual examination due to illness?
answer: Yes, the scholarship may be renewed subject to the production of a medical certificate from a prescribed authority and acceptance of the same by the institution/college.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Is there a provision for renewal if a scholar fails in Group I course examination?
answer: Yes, If a scholar is pursuing Group I course fails in the examination for the first time, the award may be renewed. For second and subsequent failures in any class the student shall bear his/her own expenses until he/she secures promotion to the next higher class.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Is Aadhaar authentication compulsory for renewals?
answer: Yes, Aadhaar authentication is compulsory at the time of renewals if not provided earlier at the time of admission.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: How to apply for the scholarship?
answer: The applicant can apply through the specified online portal of the State/UT and National Scholarship Portal.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What is the objective of the scheme?
answer: The objective of the scheme is to recognize and promote quality education amongst Students belonging to OBC, EBC and DNT categories by providing full financial support. The Scheme will cover OBC/EBC/DNT students for pursuing studies beyond Class XII.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What is the scope and coverage of the scheme?
answer: The Scheme will operate in all the institutions notified by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for every financial year 2021-22 onwards. | The scholarship, once awarded, will continue till the completion of the course, subject to satisfactory performance of the student. The students are required to apply for scholarships every year even in case of renewal also.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: How is the scheme funded?
answer: The scheme is fully funded by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, on a 100% basis.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What is covered under the scholarship for OBC/EBC/DNT students in notified institutions?
answer: The scholarship covers various expenses including full tuition fee and non-refundable charges, living expenses, books and stationery, and provision for a computer/laptop.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: How much financial assistance is provided for tuition fees?
answer: For private sector institutions, the ceiling is ₹2.00 lakh per annum per student. For private sector flying clubs for Commercial Pilot Training and Type Rating Courses, it's ₹3.72 lakhs per annum per student.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What living expenses are covered under the scholarship?
answer: Beneficiaries receive ₹3,000 per month per student to cover living expenses.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Are there provisions for books and stationery?
answer: Yes, students receive ₹5,000 per annum per student for books and stationery.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Is there assistance provided for acquiring a computer/laptop?
answer: Yes, students are entitled to a latest computer/laptop of a reputed brand with accessories like UPS and printer, limited to ₹45,000 per student as one-time assistance during the course.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: When does the scholarship become payable?
answer: The scholarship becomes payable immediately after a student secures admission and starts attending classes.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: How are living expenses, books, stationery, and computer/laptop with accessories provided?
answer: These expenses are directly transferred to the student by the Central Government through Direct Benefit Transfer mode.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Who is eligible for the scholarship under this Scheme?
answer: The Scheme covers OBC/EBC/DNT students pursuing studies beyond Class XII.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What are the income criteria for eligibility?
answer: Students with a total annual family income from all sources up to ₹2.50 lakhs are eligible.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Is there a limitation on the number of siblings eligible for the scholarship?
answer: Yes, the benefit of the Scheme will not be provided to more than 2 siblings in a family.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Are there any provisions for girls students?
answer: Yes, 30% of slots allotted to the institution are reserved for eligible girl students based on their inter-se merit.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What happens if a student fails to get promoted to the next semester/class?
answer: The scholarship will be terminated in such cases.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: How are 'Top Class' institutions identified for inclusion in the Scheme?
answer: Institutions such as IIMs, IITs, NITs, etc., are eligible, subject to their application or recommendation by the Selection Committee. Other criteria include NAAC A++ and A+ accreditation, NIRF ranking, or Institutions of National Importance as per Ministry of Education lists.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: How to apply under the scheme?
answer: The students will submit their application on National Scholarship Portal (NSP). https://scholarships.gov.in/

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What is the objective of the scheme?
answer: The objective of the scheme is to provide premium education to the meritorious students belonging to the OBC, EBC and DNT categories by funding their education from Class 9 onwards till they complete Class 12.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: How is the scheme implemented?
answer: This scheme is a central sector component under a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, in collaboration with State Governments and the National Scholarship Portal.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Who is eligible for this scheme?
answer: All the OBC, EBC and DNT students studying in the Top Class Schools identified as per the modalities of the scheme with household annual income of less than ₹2.5 lakhs will be eligible for the scheme.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: How are slots allocated for each state under the scheme?
answer: The number of slots for each state is determined based on the OBC population data. This ensures equitable distribution of scholarships across different regions.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: How are Top Class Schools identified under the scheme?
answer: Top Class Schools (TCSs) are selected by a committee chaired by the Joint Secretary (BC), with representation from the Department of School Education and NITI Aayog. These schools must consistently achieve 100% pass rates in Classes 10th and 12th.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: What expenses does the scholarship cover?
answer: The scholarship provides grants for tuition fees, hostel fees, and other charges required by the school, up to a maximum of ₹75,000/- per annum per student for Classes 9 and 10, and ₹1,25,000/- per annum per student for Classes 11 and 12.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Are there any conditions of eligibility for students?
answer: Yes, besides belonging to eligible categories and studying in designated Top Class Schools, students must have a household income below ₹2.5 lakhs. Additionally, they must maintain a bank account and provide all necessary details while applying for the scheme.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: Is there any reservation for girls under the scheme?
answer: Yes, at least 30% of the scholarships are reserved for girls, ensuring gender inclusivity in the distribution of benefits.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: How are scholarship funds disbursed?
answer: Funds are directly transferred into the beneficiaries' bank accounts through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode. Payments are made in installments and are released before the 15th of August each year.

scheme_name: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
question: How to apply under the scheme?
answer: The OBC/EBC/DNT students already studying in the Top Class Schools (TCSs) can apply on the National Scholarship Portal for the scheme along with the marks they have obtained in the final exam of the previous class. https://scholarships.gov.in/

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Award for Yoga
question: What is the Prime Minister's Award for Yoga?
answer: It is an award to recognize individuals and organizations for their significant contribution to the promotion and development of Yoga.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Award for Yoga
question: Which ministry administers this award?
answer: The award is administered by the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Award for Yoga
question: Who is eligible to apply for this award?
answer: Individuals and organizations with significant experience and contribution in Yoga are eligible.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Award for Yoga
question: What is the minimum age required for individuals?
answer: The applicant must be at least 30 years old.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Award for Yoga
question: Can organizations apply for the award?
answer: Yes, both individuals and institutions can apply under separate categories.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Award for Yoga
question: Can an applicant apply for multiple categories?
answer: No, an applicant can apply for only one category (Individual or Institutional) in a year.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Award for Yoga
question: What does the award include?
answer: The award includes a trophy, certificate, and a cash prize of ₹ 25 lakh.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Award for Yoga
question: How many awards are given each year?
answer: A total of 4 awards are given-2 for individuals and 2 for institutions.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Award for Yoga
question: Are international applicants eligible?
answer: Yes, both national and international applicants can be considered.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Award for Yoga
question: What happens after screening?
answer: The Selection Committee evaluates shortlisted candidates and makes final decisions.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Award for Yoga
question: Does the award consider social impact?
answer: Yes, impact on society and promotion of ethical and spiritual values are key factors.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: What is the objective of the Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAGY)?
answer: The main objective of PMAGY is the integrated development of Scheduled Caste (SC) majority villages through the convergent implementation of existing schemes and additional support using gap-filling funds for unmet needs.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: When was the PMAGY launched and in which states was it initially implemented?
answer: PMAGY was launched in 2009-10 on a pilot basis in 1,000 villages across five states: Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, and Assam.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: What is the eligibility criteria for a village to be selected under PMAGY?
answer: Villages must: | - Have more than 50% SC population.- Have a total population greater than 500. Selection is done in descending order based on the percentage of SC population.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: What is the vision of an 'Adarsh Gram'?
answer: An Adarsh Gram is a model village where all residents have access to basic services like housing, sanitation, health, education, employment, and no caste-based discrimination, enabling them to live a life of dignity.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: What kind of financial support is provided under PMAGY?
answer: Each selected village receives ₹20 lakh as Central Assistance under PMAGY for gap-filling activities not covered by existing schemes. The balance amount of ₹1 lakh per village would be for administrative and other expenses

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: What are the key focus areas of development under PMAGY?
answer: Development under PMAGY focuses on: | - Physical infrastructure (roads, electricity, water) | - Sanitation & environment | - Social infrastructure and human development | - Livelihood and skill development | - Social harmony and dignity

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: Are only Central Government schemes used for development under PMAGY?
answer: No. PMAGY emphasizes convergent implementation of both Central and State/UT Government schemes, along with gap-filling funds to cover uncovered areas.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: What is meant by 'gap-filling' under PMAGY?
answer: 'Gap-filling' refers to activities and needs of the village that are not covered under existing schemes. PMAGY provides funds specifically to fulfill these unmet needs.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: What are the benefits to residents of a PMAGY village?
answer: Residents benefit from: | - All-weather roads, safe drinking water, electricity | - Sanitary living conditions and solid waste management | - Functional schools, Anganwadi centers, health centers | - Skill training, employment opportunities, and social equality

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: How does PMAGY promote social harmony and inclusion?
answer: The scheme works to eliminate untouchability, caste-based discrimination, and promotes dignity, equal rights, and active community participation through institutions like Gram Sabha, Mahila Mandals, and Youth Clubs.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
question: What is the minimum Scheduled Caste population percentage required for a village to be considered eligible under this developmental scheme?
answer: Villages must have more than 40% Scheduled Caste population as per the latest available Census data to qualify for selection. Additionally, the total population should be ≥ 500 persons for eligibility consideration.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
question: How much financial assistance is provided to newly selected villages for infrastructure development and what additional support is available for administrative activities?
answer: Newly selected villages receive ₹20,00,000/- for Gap-filling infrastructure development activities that cannot be covered through convergence with other schemes. An additional ₹1,00,000/- per village is allocated for administrative expenses including technical resource support, capacity building, awareness generation, and Management Information System maintenance.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
question: What happens to villages that have already completed the initial development phase and wish to continue further improvement after five years?
answer: Villages that successfully implement their Village Development Plan and complete the five-year monitoring period can receive an additional round of funding. This includes ₹9,50,000/- for Gap-filling component and ₹50,000/- for administrative expenses to support continuous development initiatives.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
question: Which online portal must be used for need assessment data entry and Village Development Plan preparation throughout the implementation process?
answer: All activities including need assessment, data collection, gap analysis, and Village Development Plan preparation must be conducted through the centralized web portal https://pmagy.gov.in. This portal provides all necessary formats and auto-generates the comprehensive Village Development Plan.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
question: What is the time limit for utilizing the Gap-filling funds received by selected villages and what happens during the extended monitoring period?
answer: Gap-filling funds must be utilized within 2 years from the date of release for all infrastructure development activities. However, convergent implementation continues for an additional 3 years to ensure maintenance of basic developmental milestones and stabilization of socio-economic indicators.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
question: Who heads the Village Level Convergence Committee and what are the mandatory membership requirements for effective scheme implementation?
answer: The Village Level Convergence Committee is headed by the Sarpanch or Pradhan of the village and must include all Scheduled Caste members of the Gram Panchayat, Anganwadi Workers, ASHA workers, and other concerned line officials. One Scheduled Caste member serves as Member Secretary.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
question: How many socio-economic developmental indicators must be monitored and across how many different domains are these indicators distributed?
answer: Villages must monitor 50 socio-economic developmental monitorable indicators distributed across 10 domains including drinking water and sanitation, education, health and nutrition, social security, rural roads and housing, electricity and clean fuel, agricultural practices, financial inclusion, digitization, and livelihood and skill development.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
question: What minimum score must a village achieve on the monitorable indicators to qualify for declaration as an Adarsh Gram?
answer: Villages must achieve a score of 70 or above on the monitorable indicators and be declared as Open Defecation Free to qualify for Adarsh Gram declaration. Each indicator can achieve a maximum score of 2, making the total possible score 100.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
question: What is the expected convergence ratio that State Governments must ensure with other schemes to maximize development impact?
answer: State Governments and Union Territory Administrations are expected to ensure convergence of at least 3 to 4 times of Gap-filling funds from existing Central and State Schemes or matching grants to achieve comprehensive village saturation with basic infrastructure.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
question: How frequently must the Gram Sabha conduct social audit of the scheme implementation and what is the purpose of this requirement?
answer: The Gram Sabha must undertake social audit of the scheme at least once a year to ensure greater transparency and better utilization of resources, following the same methodology required under Section 17 of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
question: What are the different formats required for capturing village level data and how do these formats contribute to the overall Village Development Plan?
answer: The need assessment requires Format I for village level data, Format II for village level infrastructural needs, Format III-A for family and individual needs, and Format III-B for consolidation. The final Village Development Plan consists of Formats I, IV, V and VI.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
question: Which committee at the district level is responsible for appraising and approving the Village Development Plans prepared by villages?
answer: The District Level Project Appraisal cum Convergence Committee headed by the District Collector is responsible for appraising Village Development Plans. This committee ensures robust planning with adequate convergence and potential for desired improvements in monitorable indicators.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
question: What specific activities are funded exclusively through Gap-filling component and what types of activities require convergence with other schemes?
answer: Gap-filling funds cover only non-recurring infrastructure developmental requirements for community purposes that cannot be met under existing Central or State Government schemes. All other developmental activities must be implemented through convergence with relevant existing schemes.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
question: How are the administrative expenses of ₹1,00,000/- per village distributed among different levels of implementation and what is the allocation ratio?
answer: The administrative expenses are distributed among Centre, State, District and Village in a ratio of 1:1:1:2. This covers technical resource support, training and capacity building, awareness generation, publicity, and Management Information System development and maintenance at all levels.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin
question: What assistance in convergence with MGNREGA is provided under PMAY-G?
answer: In convergence with MGNREGA, the beneficiaries get employment for 95 days. The beneficiaries are paid ₹ 90.95 per day for unskilled labor.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin
question: What assistance in convergence with SBM-G is provided under PMAY-G?
answer: In convergence with SBM-G, the beneficiaries get assistance for the construction of toilets of up to ₹ 12,000.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin
question: How are the beneficiaries for PMAY-G identified?
answer: The beneficiaries are identified using parameters from the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) and verified by the Gram Sabhas.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin
question: How the amount of loan or financial assistance provided to the beneficiary?
answer: The amount is transferred directly to the Aadhaar-Linked Bank Account / Post-Office Account of the beneficiary.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin
question: What is the amount and the purpose of loan provided under PMAY-G?
answer: A loan up to ₹ 70,000/- is provided at 3% lower interest rates) to the beneficiary to build a permanent dwelling.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin
question: Who is the Implementing Agency of PMAY-G?
answer: PMAY-G s being implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA).

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
question: Is the entire mission implemented as Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS)?
answer: Except for the component of Credit Linked Subsidy which is implemented as a Central Sector Scheme, the rest of the mission is implemented as Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS).

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
question: I need to know the technical specifications, construction standards of the houses/slums that will be built under this scheme?
answer: The houses must conform to the standards provided in National Building Code (NBC) and Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). For a detailed description of the houses/slums, please refer Section-2 of the scheme guidelines: https://pmay-urban.gov.in/uploads/guidelines/60180813309f2-Updated%20guidelines%20of%20PMAY-U.pdf

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
question: Are there any sections that would be given preference while providing the benefits?
answer: Preference will be given to differently-abled persons, senior citizens, SCs, STs, OBCs, Minority, single women, transgender and other weaker & vulnerable sections of the society.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
question: Will I still be eligible to apply for government's ongoing or upcoming schemes if I apply for PMAY-U?
answer: The benefits of all existing and future rural schemes will not be denied to a beneficiary solely on the grounds that she/he has availed a house under PMAY(U).

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
question: I am a beneficiary of PMAY (G) but I am in the permanent waitlist. What are my options?
answer: The beneficiaries in the permanent wait list of PMAY (G) will have the flexibility for opting for a house under PMAY(G) or PMAY(U).

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
question: How do I know if my town is covered under the scheme?
answer: You can visit https://pmay-urban.gov.in/pmayprogress to check the same. Alternatively, you can visit https://pmay-urban.gov.in/ and head to "City Wise Progress".

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
question: For how am I required to be residing in an urban area to become a beneficiary under this scheme?
answer: The States/UTs, at their discretion, may decide a cut-off date on which beneficiaries need to be a resident of that urban area for being eligible to take benefits under the scheme.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
question: Will central assistance be provided for rehabilitation of dwellers from slums built on private land?
answer: No, slums built on private land are not covered under central assistance.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
question: Is there a private entity authorised by MoHUA to collect fee from the beneficiary under PMAY-U?
answer: No private entity/persons have been authorised by MoHUA to collect this fee from any beneficiary under this scheme.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
question: How do I know if a field in the application form is mandatory?
answer: The mandatory fields have a red asterisk (*) mark at the end.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
question: How do I check my application status?
answer: There are two ways in which the applicant can check his/her application status: | Method-1: Using Assessment ID. | Step 1: Log on to the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana website: http://pmaymis.gov.in/Track_Application_Status.aspx or go to the 'Citizen Application' option and then choose the 'Check Status' button. | Step 2: When you hit the track button, there will be two options displayed: 'By Name, Father's Name & Mobile No' and 'By Assessment ID'. | Step 3: Choose the 'By Assessment ID' option. | Step 4: Enter the Assessment ID & Mobile Number that was assigned when the form was filled and submitted. | Step 5: After filling in the details, click 'Submit'. | Step 6: The user can view the progress of his/her application. | Method-2: Using Name, Father's Name and Mobile Number. | Step 1: Log on to the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana website (pmaymis.gov.in) and go to the 'Citizen Application' option and then choose the 'Check Status' button. | Step 2: After clicking on the know your status button, choose the 'By Name, Father's Name & Mobile No' option. | Step 3: Once this is done, provide the State, District and City details. | Step 4: The next step is to fill in the Name, Father's name and Mobile Number. | Step 5: Once this done, Click 'Submit'. | Step 6: Once this done, the status can be viewed.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What Is Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)?
answer: 'Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)' is a campaign launched by the Department of Pharmaceuticals in association with Central Pharma Public Sector Undertakings to provide quality medicines at affordable prices to the masses through dedicated outlets called 'Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendra'. These provide generic medicines at a much lower price. The potency of these medicines is the same as compared to expensive branded medicines available on the open market.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What Is A Generic Medicine?
answer: Generic drugs are marketed under a non-proprietary or approved name rather than a proprietary or brand name. Generic drugs are equally effective and inexpensive compared to their branded counterparts.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What Is PMBI?
answer: PMBI (Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India) has been established under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Govt. of India, with the support of all the CPSUs for co-coordinating procurement, supply, and marketing of generic drugs through the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: How The Quality, Safety And Efficacy Of Medicines Are Ensured?
answer: The quality, safety, and efficacy of medicines are ensured by getting each batch of medicines procured from CPSUs as well as private suppliers tested from NABL-approved laboratories and conforming to the required standards before the same are supplied to Super stockists /Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras from the warehouse of PMBI.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: Are Generic Drugs As Effective As Branded Ones?
answer: Generic drugs have the same efficacy and therapeutic value as that of branded medicines.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: How Do Generic Medicines Benefit The Patients?
answer: By taking generic medicines, a patient can reduce his/her expenditure on medicines drastically.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What Are The Medicines Available From Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras And What Are Their Prices?
answer: The endeavor of PMBI is to make available all therapeutic medicines at Jan Aushadhi Stores. A list of medicines with their MRP which are presently available is given under the heading "PMBJP Products- Therapeutic groups" on the website of PMBI. More medicines are being added to this list.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: How Many Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras Have Been Opened And What Are Their Locations?
answer: More than 8604 are currently functional. A list of State-wise / District-wise PMBJK along with their locations are available under the heading "PMBJP => PMBJP Kendra" on the website of PMBI.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What Is The Timing (Opening And Closing) Of The Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras?
answer: The normal working hours of PMBJK are 8 AM to 8 PM.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: How The Medicines Are Procured And Supplied To Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras?
answer: Medicines are procured through an open tender system from private manufacturers as well as CPSUs. Each batch of procured medicines are duly tested from impanelled NABL laboratories and sent to Kendra through distribution network.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: Who Can Open A Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras?
answer: Individual entrepreneur / Proprietor | Partnership | Charitable Institute/Hospital | NGO/ Trust/ Society | Government/ Government Nominated Agency | Any Other (Please specify)

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What Are The Requirements For Opening A Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendra By An Organization / Individual Other Than A Government Nominated?
answer: Own space or hired space duly supported by the proper lease agreement Minimum required space conforming to standards as approved by the PMBI Sale license from competent authority (Retail drug license in the name of the applicant and/or Tin No.) | Proof of securing a pharmacist (name of the pharmacist, Registration with the State Council etc. needs to be furnished) | Financial capacity to run the Store by submitting the document (ITR, Bank Statement, PAN/Aadhar, etc.) | Drug License in name of "Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendra".

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What is the procedure for opening a Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras?
answer: For detailed guidelines and procedures, please click "Apply for Kendra" on our website.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What incentives are available to a Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras owner?
answer: - Operating agency will be provided with a 20% margin on the MRP (excluding taxes) of each drug. | - Special Incentive: A special incentive shall be granted for PMBJK opened by women entrepreneurs, Divyaang, SCs & STs, Ex-servicemen & any entrepreneurs open 'Janaushadhi Kendra (PMBJK)' at aspirational districts (backward district) as notified by the NITI Aayog & in Himalayan, Island territories and North- Eastern. An amount of ₹2.00 lakhs in addition to normal incentives as applicable is to be given to above-mentioned entrepreneurs as mentioned below :- | ₹1.50 lakh reimbursement of furniture and fixtures | ₹0.50 lakh as reimbursement for Computer, internet, printer, scanner etc. | This will be a one-time grant for the opening of a new PMBJK against submission of original bills and restricted up to actual expenditure incurred. | Note: "The Special incentive shall be granted to the Women entrepreneurs, Divyang, SCs & STs, Ex-servicemen & any entrepreneurs open 'Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendra (PMBJK)' at aspirational districts as notified by the Niti Aayog, In Himalayan, Island territories and North- Eastern states based on One Family - One Grant formula. It means any above-mentioned eligible PMBJK owner shall be granted a special incentive only once and no other person from his/her family/relative shall be granted special incentive thereafter. For this purpose, "Relative" means - "Relative", in relation to an individual, means the husband, Wife, unmarried dependent brother or sister or any lineal ascendant or descendant of that individual." | - Normal Incentive: PMBJK run by other entrepreneurs/Pharmacist/NGOs/NGOs & Charitable organization that are linked with PMBI headquarters through software will get incentive up to ₹ 5.00 lakhs. The incentive will be given @ 15% of monthly purchase made from PMBI by these PMBJKs subject to ceiling of ₹15,000/- per month up to total limit of 5.00 lakhs. It will also cover PMBJK opened by Women entrepreneurs, Divyang, SCs & STs, Ex-servicemen & any entrepreneurs open 'Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendra (PMBJK)' at aspirational districts as notified by the Niti Aayog, In Himalayan, Island territories and North- Eastern state. | This will be applicable to existing PMBJK also whose existing limit of incentives of ₹ 2.50 lakh is fully disbursed, moreover it will also cover the PMBJK opened in government premises to Whom one-time grant of ₹2.50 lakh was disbursed. They will get incentive of ₹2.50 lakh based on purchase made by them from PMBI as per other terms and conditions applicable to all PMBJKs. | Further, any PMBJK opened in Government premises will get normal incentives as applicable to PMBJK in private premises.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: What is the age limit for availing PM ECRG?
answer: The upper age limit for PM ECRG is 42 years, with a relaxation of three years for SC/ST/OBC/ Physically challenged and women candidates.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: What is the nature of support under PM ECRG scheme?
answer: PM ECRG is a one-time grant and carries a maximum research grant of Rs. 60 Lakhs (excluding overheads) for a period of three years. The research grant covers equipment, research personnel, consumables, travel and contingency apart from overheads.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: What is the duration of the PM ECRG project? Can it be extended?
answer: PM ECRG project period is of 3 years. There is no provision for extension of the project duration.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: When should I apply for PM ECRG? Can I apply for the projects throughout the year?
answer: The Call for applications will be notified through the website www.anrfonline.in and www.anrf.gov.in . The application form along with a proper research proposal highlighting the research work to be undertaken should be submitted online through the website www.anrfonline.in during the call opening period.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: How should I apply for PM ECRG?
answer: All applications should be submitted through the ANRF online portal www.anrfonline.in

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Can I have a Co-PI in PM ECRG project? Can I have a Mentor in PM ECRG?
answer: Co-PI or Mentors are not allowed in this scheme. However, foreign nationals are mandated to have an Indian Co-PI.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: I am working abroad as post-doc, and I want to return to India. I intend to apply for PM ECRG. But I have not yet finalized my place of work. Am I eligible to apply under the scheme?
answer: No. The applicant must hold a regular academic/research position in a recognized academic institution/ or national laboratories or any other recognized R&D institutions. Only after joining a research or academic institution, one can apply for the grants under this scheme.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: I am implementing an PM ECRG project for the last one year. Am I eligible to apply for another project under any other scheme/award or fellowship programs of ANRF?
answer: In general, a PI is allowed to operate only one ANRF project at a time. Exceptions are allowed for some specific calls under certain topics/programs/schemes. In all other cases, PI can submit another proposal under regular schemes of ANRF six months prior to the date of completion of the ongoing PM ECRG project.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: What documents should I send for receiving the next instalments of the grant?
answer: The PIs should upload annual Progress Report and financial statements at the end of each financial year. The release of the next instalment of the grant will be considered only after submission of Utilization Certificate (separately for Recurring & Non-recurring) and Statement of Expenditure, financial year wise.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: I intend to change my Host Institution? What procedure should I follow?
answer: Change of host institute will be considered only (i) from a private/public/government institution to any other public/government institution or (ii) General administrative transfers in government or public funded institutions. Change of institute will not be considered for any other cases. Change of host institution can be undertaken only after obtaining due approval from ANRF.Transfer of the project along with balance grant and the assets to the new institute is allowed, provided the administrative authority of both institutes agree in writing. NOC from the previous host institute and Endorsement Form from the new host Institute must be sent to ANRF through the online portal.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: What is the procedure for surrendering PM ECRG project?
answer: For termination of the project, PI need to inform the ANRF through the host institution immediately. The implementing institute should not incur any expenditure from the date of termination of the project or the date of resignation of PI. The institute must also arrange for the submission of relevant documents.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Can I be away from the implementing Institute when I am implementing the PM ECRG project?
answer: The PIs must seek the consent of ANRF if he/she intends to be away from the implementing institute (except for field work related to the project) continuously for a period of more than eight weeks.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: What should be done for the unspent grant under PM ECRG project after the completion of the tenure of the project?
answer: The following documents should be sent to the ANRF after the duration of the project is completed: | - Final Consolidated Statement of Expenditure (in duplicate) , giving expenditure financial year wise (FY) from date of start till date of completion. | - Utilization Certificates (FY wise) for all FYs (in duplicate) matching with Statement of Expenditure figures in that FY. | - Project Completion Report (PCR) with a list of publications, and patents filed/granted. | - DD/ cheque for the unspent grant, drawn in favor of 'Science & Engineering Research Fund'. | - The Principal Investigator is responsible for the timely submission of progress reports, utilization certificates, project closure report (PCR), refund of unspent balance amount etc. at the end or early closure of the project.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: I am an INSPIRE Faculty Fellow. Am I eligible to apply for PM ECRG?
answer: Yes. INSPIRE Faculty, Ramanujan and Ramalingaswamy Fellows are eligible to apply under PM ECRG subject to fulfilling all other eligibility criteria.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: I was National Post Doctoral Fellow (NPDF). Am I eligible to apply for PM ECRG?
answer: Yes. Applicants who have availed NPDF, SIRE are eligible to apply under PM ECRG subject to fulfilling all other eligibility criteria.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: I have an ongoing TARE project. Can I apply for PM ECRG?
answer: Applicants having ongoing TARE project can submit proposal under PM ECRG six months prior to the completion of ongoing project, subject to fulfilling all other eligibility criteria.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: What is the budget limit under 'Travel' and 'Contingency' Heads in PM ECRG?
answer: Budget upto Rs.1 lakh per year each under 'Travel' and 'Contingency' heads will be provided. Higher amount under 'Travel' head based on the recommendation of Expert Committee will be provided where the research work involves field work.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Are the funds sanctioned under recurring head flexible?
answer: The funds sanctioned under the Recurring-I head are flexible, meaning the PI can use money allocated for consumables, manpower, travel, contingency, publications, or patent filing. However, there are some conditions to follow (See terms and conditions of the scheme, under travel and contingency).

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Are there any upper limit on travel expenditure for the project?
answer: Yes. The expenditure under the travel head is limited to Rs. 3 Lakh for a three year project, and proportionately lower for projects of shorter duration, except (where the project entails field work etc.) in cases where a higher amount for travel is explicitly sanctioned in the project. International travel is permitted within this limit.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Are there any limits on contingency expenditure for the project?
answer: Yes, the expenditure under the contingency head is also limited to Rs. 3 Lakh for a three-year project, or proportionately lower for shorter projects.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Can I use the contingency funds for paying registration fees for international conferences?
answer: Yes. Contingency funds can be used for registration charges for international conferences.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Are there specific guidelines for engaging research personnel in the project?
answer: Yes, the PI can engage research personnel as per ANRF norms, as informed through OMs - ANRF/OM/N/01/2024 and SB/S9/Z-06/2019. Additionally, the total funds under the recurring budget should not be exceeded in any case.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: One JRF is approved in my project. Can I engage a SRF or an R.A or multiple research personnel in the project?
answer: Yes, the Principal Investigator (PI) has the flexibility to recruit research personnel of any designation, or multiple personnel, as needed during the course of the project. However, the PI / host institution must ensure that (a) guidelines as per ANRF's OMs viz., ANRF/OM/N/01/2024 and SB/S9/Z-06/2019 are followed, (b) total funds sanctioned under the recurring head are not exceeded in any case and (c) Any future revision of emoluments by the ANRF will apply only to the originally approved or sanctioned research personnel for the revised fellowships.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Can I delay the acceptance of the project implementation?
answer: No. The Principal Investigator (PI) must generally complete the documentation process within one month from the date the approval letter is issued. Any delay or lack of correspondence beyond one month from the PI, shall result in the withdrawal of the proposal approval.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Can I reallocate or reappropriate funds between recurring and non recurring budgets?
answer: No, interoperability or reappropriation between the non-recurring and recurring budgets is not permitted under any circumstances.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Can the approved equipment list be changed during the project?
answer: The change of approved or sanctioned equipment is generally not permitted and may only be considered on a case-by-case basis. The PI must obtain prior approval from ANRF to change the approved or sanctioned equipment.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: How can I seek approval for publication-related expenditures?
answer: The PI must submit a request through the ANRF online portal to obtain prior approval for publication-related expenditure.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is Maximum Project Cost Allowed Under PMEGP?
answer: Rs.25.00 lakhs for the manufacturing unit and Rs.10.00 lakhs for Service Unit

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is The Component Of Project Cost?
answer: Capital Expenditure Loan, one cycle of working capital and 10% of project cost as own contribution in case of General category and 5% of project cost in case of weaker section.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Which Are The Financial Agencies?
answer: 27 Public Sector Banks, Regional Rural Banks(RRB), Co-operative Banks, and Private Scheduled Commercial Banks approved by respective State Task Force Committee.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: How The Capital Expenditure Loan / Cash Credit Limit Be Utilized ?
answer: Working Capital at least once should touch the 100% limit of Cash Credit within three years of the Lock-in period of M.M. and not less than 75% of the utilization of the sanctioned limit on average.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Where The Beneficiary Has To Submit His/Her Application/ Project?
answer: The beneficiary can submit his/her application/Project online on kvic website www.kvic.org.in / kviconline.gov.in/pmegpeportal. A list of office addresses of KVIC/KVIB/DIC is available at our website.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is Village Industry ?
answer: Any Village Industry (except those mentioned in the negative list) located in the Rural Area which produces any goods or renders any service with or without the use of power and in which the fixed capital investment for head of a full time artisans or worker does not exceed Rs.1.00 lakh in plain area and Rs.1.50 lakhs in hilly areas and for A & N Island and Laxdeep Rs.4.5 Lakhs.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is Rural Area ?
answer: Any area classified as Village as per the revenue record of the State, irrespective of the population. It also includes an area even if classified as town provided its population does not exceed 20000.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is Age Limit ?
answer: Any adult beneficiary above 18 years is eligible for financing under PMEGP.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Are The Main Criteria Of Project?
answer: It should fulfill the criteria of rural area (for Rural Area project), per capita investment, own contribution, negative list, and the unit should be a new one

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Whether EDP Training Is Compulsory?
answer: Before MM Claim through the PMEGP portal, EDP training of 10 working days for a Project cost of More than 5.00 lakhs and 6 Working days of training for up to Project Cost of 5.00 lakhs to the beneficiary is compulsory

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Whether Collateral Security Is Mandatory?
answer: As per RBI guidelines, the project costing up to Rs.10.00 lakhs under PMEGP loans are free from collateral security. The CGTSME provided a collateral guarantee for the project beyond Rs.5.00 lakhs and up to Rs.25.00 lakhs under the PMEGP scheme.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is PMEGP Scheme, And What Are Its Objectives?
answer: Answer: PMEGP stands for Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme, which is a credit-linked subsidy scheme launched by the Ministry of MSME, Government of India, to generate employment opportunities in the country. The main objective of the scheme is to create self-employment opportunities for unemployed youth and women entrepreneurs in rural and urban areas.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Who Is Eligible To Apply For PMEGP Scheme, And What Is The Age Limit For The Applicants?
answer: Answer: Any individual above 18 years of age can apply for the PMEGP scheme. However, the maximum age limit for applying is 35 years for general category applicants and 40 years for SC/ST/OBC/PH/Women candidates.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: How Can I Apply For The PMEGP Scheme, And What Is The Application Procedure?
answer: Answer: You can apply for the PMEGP scheme through the online portal of KVIC, or offline by submitting the application form to the nearest KVIC office or bank. The application procedure involves filling up the application form, attaching the necessary documents, and submitting it along with the project report.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Are The Different Types Of Projects That Can Be Set Up Under The PMEGP Scheme?
answer: Answer: The PMEGP scheme supports various types of projects, including manufacturing, service, and business projects. The projects should be viable and have the potential to generate employment opportunities.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: How Much Financial Assistance Can I Expect To Receive Under The PMEGP Scheme, And What Is The Repayment Period?
answer: Answer: Under the PMEGP scheme, financial assistance is provided in the form of a subsidy, which ranges from 15% to 35% of the project cost, depending on the category of the applicant. The remaining amount can be obtained as a bank loan. The repayment period for the loan is generally 3 to 7 years.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Can I Apply For Multiple Projects Under The PMEGP Scheme, And What Is The Maximum Limit?
answer: Answer: No, an individual can apply for only one project under the PMEGP scheme. However, a group of individuals can apply for a group project, subject to a maximum of 10 members.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Are The Documents Required To Apply For The PMEGP Scheme?
answer: Answer: The documents required for PMEGP scheme application include a project report, proof of identity and address, caste certificate (if applicable), educational qualification certificate, and bank account details.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: How Long Does It Take For The PMEGP Scheme Application To Be Processed?
answer: Answer: The processing time for the PMEGP scheme application varies from state to state and depends on various factors such as the completeness of the application, the availability of funds, and the number of applications received.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Can I Apply For The PMEGP Scheme For An Existing Business?
answer: Answer: No, the PMEGP scheme is meant for setting up a new business or for expanding an existing business. An existing business is not eligible for financial assistance under the PMEGP scheme.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is The Role Of The Khadi And Village Industries Commission (KVIC) In The PMEGP Scheme?
answer: Answer: KVIC is the nodal agency for implementing the PMEGP scheme. It is responsible for receiving and processing the applications, conducting training programs, and disbursing the subsidy to the beneficiaries through the banks.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is The Project Report, And How Do I Prepare It?
answer: Answer: The project report is a detailed document that provides information about the proposed project, its feasibility, and financial viability. It includes details like project cost, sources of funding, marketing plan, and expected income and expenses. KVIC provides a format for preparing the project report, which can be downloaded from their website.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Can I Apply For The PMEGP Scheme Offline?
answer: Answer: Yes, you can apply for the PMEGP scheme offline by submitting the application form along with the project report and necessary documents to the nearest KVIC office or bank.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Can I Apply For The PMEGP Scheme Online?
answer: Answer: Yes, you can apply for the PMEGP scheme online through the KVIC portal. The process involves registering on the portal, filling up the application form, and uploading the necessary documents.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Are The Documents Required For The PMEGP Scheme Application?
answer: Answer: The documents required for the PMEGP scheme application include proof of identity and address, educational qualification certificate, caste certificate (if applicable), project report, and bank account details.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Can I Make Changes To My PMEGP Scheme Application After Submission?
answer: Answer: No, you cannot make changes to your PMEGP scheme application after submission. Therefore, it is important to ensure that all the information provided in the application is accurate and complete before submitting it.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: How Will I Know If My PMEGP Scheme Application Has Been Approved?
answer: Answer: Once your PMEGP scheme application is approved, you will receive an approval letter from KVIC or the bank, along with the sanction letter stating the amount of subsidy and loan that you are eligible for.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: I'm a tenant farmer without formal land ownership documents. Can I still apply for crop insurance under PMFBY if I can prove I cultivate the land?
answer: Yes, tenant farmers and sharecroppers can apply with a valid land tenure agreement. You must provide evidence of your cultivation rights through state-recognized documents or agreements.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: My crops were damaged by unseasonal rains after harvesting while drying in the field. Does PMFBY cover such losses?
answer: Coverage is available for up to 14 days post-harvest for crops kept in "cut & spread" condition in the field, specifically for damage from cyclonic/unseasonal rains. You must report the damage immediately.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: What is the exact premium rate for Kharif paddy, and how is the government subsidy calculated?
answer: Farmers pay 2% of the sum insured for Kharif food crops. The difference between the actuarial premium rate and farmer's share is jointly subsidized by Central and State governments equally.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: If a drought prevents me from sowing crops despite preparation, what percentage of compensation can I claim?
answer: You can claim up to 25% of the sum insured under prevented sowing coverage, provided the majority of farmers in your notified area were also prevented from sowing due to adverse conditions.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: I farm in Himachal Pradesh. Do I need to pay any premium for my apple crop under PMFBY?
answer: No, farmers in Himachal Pradesh, along with other North-Eastern states and Jammu & Kashmir, receive 100% premium subsidy from the government for all notified crops.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: Can I claim compensation if my entire village faced crop damage from a landslide, but neighboring villages were unaffected?
answer: Yes, PMFBY covers localized calamities like landslides on an individual farm basis, even if the damage is isolated to specific areas within the notified region.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: How long after reporting crop damage should I expect to receive the claim amount?
answer: PMFBY aims to process and settle claims within two months of harvest, provided all documentation is complete and damage assessment is finalized.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: If I've taken a bank loan for farming, do I need to separately apply for PMFBY, or is it automatic?
answer: For loanee farmers, coverage is compulsory but not automatic. You must ensure your bank has processed your PMFBY enrollment within the specified timeframe.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: What happens if I'm unable to pay the premium online due to technical issues on the last date?
answer: You can visit a nearby CSC or bank branch to submit your premium payment. Keep proof of your online payment attempt for any deadline-related disputes.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: If I've already registered on the PMFBY portal last season, do I need to create a new registration for this season?
answer: No, use your existing registration. However, you must submit a fresh application and premium payment for each season you want coverage.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: I discovered pest damage in my field but couldn't document it immediately due to hospitalization. Will my claim be rejected?
answer: Report the damage as soon as possible with medical documentation of your hospitalization. Each case is evaluated based on provided evidence and circumstances.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: How can I ensure my claim isn't rejected due to wrong information if the CSC operator fills my form?
