scheme_name: Reimbursement of membership Fee in Government promoted E-Commerce Portals
question: May the other caste person also get the benefits ?
answer: No.

scheme_name: Reimbursement of membership Fee in Government promoted E-Commerce Portals
question: How to register for the scheme benefits?
answer: - Applicant need to visit the official website https://www.scsthub.in. | - For registration click on sign-up and provide the following details | Full Name | Valid Email ID | Mobile Number | Password and confirm password

scheme_name: Reimbursement of membership Fee in Government promoted E-Commerce Portals
question: What documents are required ?
answer: - Self-certified copy of Udyam Registration (UR). | - Self-certified copy of PAN card - in case of proprietorship, PAN card of SC/ST proprietor ought to be submitted. | - Copy of Caste Certificate of all promoters. | 4.Cancelled Cheque of the current account of the enterprise from which the EPC membership fee has been debited. | - Proof of transferred amount as reimbursement by NSSHO/ NSIC through PFMS under the scheme, where any such assistance is availed earlier with in the same financial year. | - Details of shareholding in case of partnership / Pvt. Ltd / LLP firm. In case of partnership concerns, shareholding of the enterprise would be required to ascertain status of the MSE as SC/ST MSE (shareholding of SC/ST entrepreneur to be > 51%). Attested copy of Partnership Deed for Partnership Firm / Memorandum and Article of Association in case of LLP/Private Limited Company are required. | - Attested copy of valid membership/registration certificate issued from e-commerce portal along with the copy of receipt of amount paid for membership.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Parivar Sahayata Yojana
question: What is this scheme ?
answer: This scheme is being executed for the family members who are unable to make their livelihood after the death of the primary breadwinner of the family.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Parivar Sahayata Yojana
question: What are the benefits ?
answer: Eligible applicants are entitled to a lump sum grant of Rs. 20,000/-

scheme_name: Rashtriya Parivar Sahayata Yojana
question: What Is Deceased Eligible Age ?
answer: The deceased's age should be between 18 to 59 years.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Parivar Sahayata Yojana
question: What Is financial eligibility criteria for Deceased
answer: The deceased should belong to Below Poverty Line.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Parivar Sahayata Yojana
question: Can this benefit be given to any member of the family?
answer: The deceased should be the primary breadwinner of the family.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Parivar Sahayata Yojana
question: Is this scheme only for rural areas ?
answer: No, This scheme is applicable to Urban and rural both areas.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Parivar Sahayata Yojana
question: How to get the benefits in case of rural areas ?
answer: Applicants have to visit Gram Panchayat/Janpad Panchyat for rural areas.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Parivar Sahayata Yojana
question: How To Get The Benefits In Case Of urban Areas ?
answer: Applicants Have To Visit Nagar Nigam/Nagar Panchayat/Nagar Parishad for urban areas

scheme_name: Rashtriya Parivar Sahayata Yojana
question: What documents are required while submitting the application form?
answer: - Age Certificate. | - Death Certificate. | - B.P.L. Card. | - Lodged Primary report with the police, in case of accidental death.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Parivar Sahayata Yojana
question: Is this scheme only for males
answer: No, This Scheme Is Applicable To Males and females both

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: What are "Exit Permits," and who receives them?
answer: Answer: "Exit Permits" are issued to refugees who are willing to go back to Sri Lanka or any other country at their own cost. They are issued by the respective District Collectors.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: How is transportation, including vehicles and petrol, handled under the scheme?
answer: Answer: Four vehicles have been approved by MHA, and the expenditure on petrol for these vehicles is reimbursed by MHA.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: What infrastructure facilities are provided at the refugee camps?
answer: Answer: The camps have facilities like internal roads, electricity, and drinking water.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: Can you explain the cash dole assistance provided to Sri Lankan Refugees in Camps?
answer: Answer: The cash dole assistance varies based on family members. The head of the family receives ₹400, other adults receive ₹288, the first child receives ₹180, and other children receive ₹90.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: How are the health and growth of children monitored in the camps?
answer: Answer: Nurses from PHCs monitor the growth of both the child and the mother. Nutritious food, vitamin tablets, milk, and fruits are provided free of cost under ICDS. Polio drops are administered to children at no cost.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: What happens after the birth of a child in the refugee camps?
answer: Answer: After the birth of a child, the child's birth certificate can be obtained through the hospital. The details are recorded with the Village Administrative Officer and Special Revenue Inspector for cash doles.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: Question: What healthcare services are offered to pregnant Sri Lankan Tamil refugee women?
answer: Answer: Pregnant women receive tetanus injections, regular medical check-ups, vitamin tablets, milk, fruits, and bread under the Integrated Child Development Scheme (ICDS). They can also receive free admission to nearby PHCs or hospitals for child delivery.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: How does the scheme provide medical assistance to refugees upon arrival in Transit Camp?
answer: Answer: Refugees receive health check-ups and assistance upon arrival in Transit Camp. Medical assistance is provided by Primary Health Centres/Government Hospitals, including preventive medicine like inoculation for measles, administered free of cost.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: What is porterage, and how is it related to the repatriation process?
answer: Porterage is the service of carrying goods. It is provided to refugees on repatriation as per approved rates, assisting them in carrying their belongings when they return to their home country.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: What types of aluminum utensils are provided under the scheme?
answer: The scheme provides rice boiling utensils (5 ltr. Capacity), sambar, curry utensils (2 ltr. Capacity), large spoons, dining plates, and tumblers.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: What clothing materials are provided to different categories of refugees?
answer: Clothing materials provided include dhoti and vests for adult males, half trousers, inner garments, and half sleeve shirts for male children, saris and blouses for adult females, skirts and blouses for female children, towels for every family, mats for every adult, and blankets every two years for every adult.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: What is the subsidized rice program, and how much rice is provided to family members?
answer: Family members above 8 years receive 400 grams of rice daily, and children below 8 years receive 200 grams of rice daily.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: Can you explain the benefits provided for food during the temporary stay in different camps?
answer: In Quarantine Camps, adults receive cooked food at ₹45 per day, and children receive it at ₹30 per day. Refugees in Special Camps receive cooked food at ₹70 per day per adult. Additionally, clothing materials are provided.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: How much has the Government of India spent on providing relief and accommodation to these refugees from July 1983 to March 2022?
answer: An amount of ₹1,226 crore (approximately) has been spent by the Government of India during this period.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: What is the objective of providing relief to Sri Lankan refugees under this scheme?
answer: The ultimate objective of providing relief is the repatriation of the refugees to Sri Lanka. Relief is given pending such repatriation.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: How is the expenditure for this scheme managed between the State Government and the Government of India?
answer: The entire expenditure is initially incurred by the State Government and is subsequently reimbursed by the Government of India (GoI).

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: What kinds of relief materials are provided under this scheme?
answer: Relief materials include Feeding Charges, Subsidized Rice, Clothing Materials, Utensils, Transportation Charges (on arrival and repatriation), Cash Doles, Infrastructure Facilities (at the camps), Electricity and Drinking Water, Vehicles and Petrol to the Sri Lankan Refugees.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: Who is responsible for implementing the "Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps" scheme?
answer: The scheme is implemented by the Freedom Fighters & Rehabilitation Division of the Department of Home, Ministry of Home Affairs.

scheme_name: Relief and Rehabilitation Assistance to Sri Lankan Refugees in the Refugee Camps
question: When were these eight schemes clubbed under the "Relief and Rehabilitation of Migrants and Repatriates" umbrella scheme?
answer: On 4th July 2018, the Government of India approved clubbing eight schemes under the "Relief and Rehabilitation of Migrants and Repatriates" umbrella scheme.

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: Who Is Eligible To Apply?
answer: Indian nationals working abroad as Post-doctoral fellows/Scientists in any area of Life Sciences & Biotechnology, Bio-Engineering, Health Care (human and animal), Agriculture and Veterinary Biotechnology, Bio- Energy and allied areas are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: Are Overseas Citizens Of India Eligible To Apply?
answer: No, overseas citizens of India are not eligible to apply

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: How Many Years Of Post-Doctoral Experience Do I Require To Apply?
answer: A minimum of three years of post-doctoral experience in overseas laboratories is required for applying.

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: Can I Apply If I Have Already Returned To India?
answer: Yes, you can apply for this fellowship if you have already returned to India provided it is less than a year (2 years for women candidates) as on the closing date of advertisement. However, if you have secured a permanent position in India during this period, you can not apply for the fellowship

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: Will My Research Experience After Returning To India Be Taken Into Account?
answer: No, only the research experience abroad would be counted.

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: From Which Date On My Postdoctoral Experience Will Be Considered?
answer: Postdoctoral experience will be counted from the date of your joining as Post-doctoral fellow after your Ph. D degree has been awarded.

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: If My Postdoctoral Experience Is Just Short Of One Month As On The Last Date Of Application Then, Can I Apply?
answer: No, in that case you are not eligible.

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: Can I Apply For The Fellowship If I Already Have A Job/ Position In India After My Return From Overseas?
answer: No, in that case you are not eligible

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: Is There Any Age Bar For Applying?
answer: The upper age limit for applying is 45 years as on last date of receiving applications.

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: Will Experience In Industry Be Counted As Research Experience?
answer: Any research experience (post-PhD/post-MD or equivalent) regardless of the type of organization where it was carried out would be considered.

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: . Am I Eligible To Apply In Two Different Schemes Simultaneously?
answer: Yes, you can apply for two different schemes simultaneously. But upon selection you need to choose only one fellowship.

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: Do I Need A Host Institute In India While Applying For RLS Fellowship?
answer: Yes, you need to choose a host institute/university/ industry in India where you would like to carry out your research during the tenure of the fellowship. The forwarding should be from Head of the Institution like Registrar/Vice Chancellor/ Director/Dean Research (as the case may be). Forwardal from the Head of the division will not be considered.

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: Can My Application Be Forwarded By Two Different Host Institutes?
answer: You can submit your nomination through single host institute only. However, host institute can nominate more than one candidate.

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: What Would Be My Professional Status In The Host Institute Once I Join As RLS Fellow?
answer: Your position will be temporary only, however, Department encourages the host institutions to treat the fellow at par with faculty- Assistant Professor/Scientist D level, for the facilities like medical benefits, etc. from the institution's resources. In addition, the host institute may also allow you to take Ph.D/dissertation students.

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: What Will Be The Duration Of Fellowship?
answer: The duration of the fellowship will be for a period of three years. In exceptional cases, the duration of the award may be extended by another two years after a fresh appraisal. Those who have already been absorbed as permanent faculty during the tenure will not be considered for extension.

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: What Is The Amount Of Fellowship That Is Provided To RLS Fellows?
answer: A consolidated monthly remuneration of Rs. 1,00,000/- p.m. (consolidated) is | provided to the Ramalingaswami fellows upon selection after joining their respective host institutes. In addition, a House Rent Allowance of Rs. 18,500/- p.m. is given to fellows.

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: Is There Any Research/ Contingent Grant Provided?
answer: A research/contingency grant of Rs. 13.00 lakh/year for purchase the of consumables, minor equipment, domestic travel, engaging manpower, and other contingent expenditures to be incurred for the implementation of the research proposal would be provided to the Ramalingaswami fellows. Institutional overhead Rs. 50,000/ year is also provided

scheme_name: Ramalingaswami Re-Entry Fellowship
question: Is The Fellowship Taxable?
answer: The fellowship is taxable as per Govt. of India rules. For any matter related to the tax, the Department dealing with tax related matters may be contacted directly.

scheme_name: Research Study/Seminar (Grant-in-Aid Scheme)
question: If my institution focuses on research related to official statistics, what minimum staffing capability is required regarding statisticians, economists, and social scientists?
answer: The institution must have qualified statisticians, economists, and social scientists on its staff.

scheme_name: Research Study/Seminar (Grant-in-Aid Scheme)
question: If I have already received assistance for presenting a research paper abroad during this current financial year, can I still submit a separate request for this type of grant?
answer: An applicant official will not be recommended for more than one proposal for Travel Grant Assistance during the current financial year if the purpose is presenting their paper abroad.

scheme_name: Research Study/Seminar (Grant-in-Aid Scheme)
question: What specific areas of statistical inquiry are ineligible for funding, particularly regarding the theoretical nature of the research work?
answer: The proposals relating strictly to pure theoretical research in statistics are not eligible for financial assistance.

scheme_name: Research Study/Seminar (Grant-in-Aid Scheme)
question: For an officer seeking travel grants, must the topic of the paper being presented at the international conference be directly related to the specific duties and responsibilities of the officer?
answer: Yes, the purpose of the visit must be directly related to the area of work of the concerned officer.

scheme_name: Research Study/Seminar (Grant-in-Aid Scheme)
question: What is the minimum operational history required for a professional or research institution working in the field of official statistics to be considered eligible for grant assistance?
answer: The professional or research institution or organization must have been engaged in the field of official statistics for a minimum period of three (3) years.

scheme_name: Research Study/Seminar (Grant-in-Aid Scheme)
question: When submitting a proposal for travel funds to an international statistical conference, what official proof is required to demonstrate that my paper has been accepted for presentation?
answer: You must provide appropriate documentary evidence confirming the acceptance of the paper for presentation by the agencies organizing the international statistical conference, seminar, or workshop.

scheme_name: Research Study/Seminar (Grant-in-Aid Scheme)
question: Are all proposals concerning statistics research eligible for funding, or are there specific types of academic activities that are specifically excluded from financial assistance?
answer: Proposals for holding annual meetings of statistical associations or societies will not be eligible for financial assistance.

scheme_name: Research Study/Seminar (Grant-in-Aid Scheme)
question: If the Project Director or certain experts are regular, salaried employees of the applicant institution, can their existing salaries be covered or charged to the scheme's budget during the project duration?
answer: The salary of the Project Director or Experts, if they are already working as regular employees of the institute, cannot be charged from the project cost during the project period.

scheme_name: Research Study/Seminar (Grant-in-Aid Scheme)
question: What are the mandatory governmental permissions, such as clearance from the Ministry of External Affairs and the Ministry of Home Affairs, that I must secure before submitting my application for travel assistance?
answer: All necessary clearances must have been obtained, including political clearance from the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), and Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) clearance from the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), wherever required.

scheme_name: Research Study/Seminar (Grant-in-Aid Scheme)
question: If my organization is seeking a Grant-in-Aid specifically for hosting a National or International Seminar, Conference, or Workshop on official statistics, what status must the organization hold?
answer: For the purpose of Grant-in-Aid for National and International Seminars, Conferences, or Workshops, the institution or organization shall be registered as "not-for-profit" to be eligible for assistance under this Scheme.

scheme_name: Research Study/Seminar (Grant-in-Aid Scheme)
question: When applying for assistance to present a technical paper internationally, is it acceptable if the paper was developed solely through the officer's independent choice or private endeavor?
answer: No, the technical paper must have been submitted through the proper official channel for the event and not solely out of the officer's own volition.

scheme_name: Research Study/Seminar (Grant-in-Aid Scheme)
question: Since various types of expenses are covered by the scheme, is financial assistance provided for the acquisition of new infrastructure or permanent assets related to the project?
answer: No, financial assistance is explicitly not available for the purpose of incurring any capital expenditure.

scheme_name: Research Study/Seminar (Grant-in-Aid Scheme)
question: Are there specific government employees or academic personnel who are eligible to seek financial assistance under the Travel Grants Assistance component of the scheme?
answer: Travel Grants Assistance is exclusively available for officials of the Central Government, Central autonomous institutions, or university personnel.

scheme_name: Research Study/Seminar (Grant-in-Aid Scheme)
question: If an official receives a direct invitation from the host organization to attend an international event, should this invitation be addressed only to the individual officer, or to a higher authority?
answer: An official invitation must be available from the host organization, and it must be addressed to the officer's administrative Ministry, Department, or Organization.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: Will Short-Listed Candidates Be Required To Attend An Interview Or Presentation?
answer: Yes, short-listed candidates may be called for an interview or presentation in Delhi as part of the final selection process.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: Can Individuals Working Under Central/State Government Or Public Sector Undertakings Apply For The Program?
answer: Yes, individuals working under Central/State Government or Public Sector Undertakings are eligible to apply. They need to submit their applications through proper channel and may send an advance copy along with the required enclosures.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: What Happens If An Application Is Incomplete?
answer: Incomplete applications are liable to be rejected, so it is important to ensure that all the required information and documents are included.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: Are Only Indian Nationals Eligible To Apply For The Fellowship?
answer: Yes, only Indian nationals are eligible to apply for the fellowship program.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: Will Any Form Of Canvassing Affect The Selection Process?
answer: Yes, canvassing in any form will lead to disqualification from the selection process. Applicants are expected to follow a fair and unbiased approach.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: Will There Be Any Interim Enquiries Or Correspondence Entertained?
answer: No, no interim enquiries or correspondence will be entertained. Applicants will be informed of the final decision once the selection process is completed.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: What Should The Research Proposal Indicate?
answer: The research proposal should clearly indicate the deliverable or output that will be produced at the end of the fellowship. This could be in the form of a monograph, features/news stories, investigative stories, or even short video films or stories, depending on the applicant's field of expertise.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: Who Will Own The Copyright Of The Research Output?
answer: The copyright of the research output will vest in the Government of India, which may publish the research output or use it in any other way to strengthen the working of the RTI regime.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: Can The Fellows Choose The Format Of Their Research Output?
answer: Yes, fellows can choose the format of their research output based on their expertise and preferences. It could be a monograph, features/news stories, investigative stories, short video films, or other suitable formats.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: Will The Government Of India Publish The Research Output?
answer: The Government of India may publish the research output and use it to enhance the functioning of the RTI regime. They have the right to utilize the research output for various purposes.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: Will The Fellows Retain Any Rights Over Their Research Output?
answer: While the copyright of the research output belongs to the Government of India, the fellows may be granted permission to use the output if the government does not utilize it within one year.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: Is There A Specific Word Count Requirement For The Monograph?
answer: The proposal should include a monograph of approximately 10,000 words, which should be ready for publication. However, the specific word count requirement may vary depending on the nature and depth of the research.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: Can Fellows From Various Fields, Such As Journalism Or Audio-Video Media, Apply For The Program?
answer: Yes, professionals from various fields, including journalism or audio-video media, are eligible to apply for the program. They can contribute their expertise and deliver research output in their respective domains.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: Can Fellows Propose Innovative Approaches Or Methodologies For Their Research?
answer: Yes, fellows are encouraged to propose innovative approaches or methodologies that can add value to their research. The program aims to foster creativity and new perspectives in addressing RTI-related issues.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: What Happens If A Fellow Is Unable To Deliver The Proposed Research Output?
answer: Fellows are expected to fulfill their commitment and deliver the proposed research output. However, in exceptional circumstances, such as unforeseen challenges or genuine reasons, they should communicate with the concerned authorities to discuss alternative arrangements.

scheme_name: Right To Information Fellowship
question: Will The Research Output Be Evaluated Before Publication Or Use By The Government?
answer: The research output may go through an evaluation process before publication or use by the government. The evaluation may include reviewing the quality, relevance, and alignment with the objectives of the RTI regime

scheme_name: Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar
question: What is Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar (RVP)?
answer: Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar is a prestigious national-level award in India, recognizing outstanding contributions in the field of science and technology.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar
question: Who organizes Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar?
answer: The award is organized and presented by the Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar
question: What are the categories for Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar?
answer: RVP is awarded in various categories such as Physical Sciences, Chemical Sciences, Biological Sciences, Mathematical Sciences, Earth & Atmospheric Sciences, and Engineering Sciences.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar
question: Who is eligible for Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar?
answer: Scientists, researchers, and individuals who have made significant contributions to their respective fields in science and technology are eligible for the award.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar
question: Is Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar only for Indian citizens?
answer: Yes, the award is specifically designed for Indian citizens who have excelled in the domain of science and technology.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar
question: How does one nominate a candidate for Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar?
answer: Nominations for RVP are invited through a formal process, and individuals or organizations interested in proposing a candidate need to follow the guidelines provided by the Ministry of Science and Technology.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar
question: Can the public attend the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar ceremony?
answer: The award ceremony is usually attended by invitees, including scientists, government officials, and dignitaries. While it is not open to the general public, the event is often covered by the media.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar
question: How does Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar contribute to promoting scientific research in India?
answer: RVP plays a crucial role in promoting a culture of excellence in scientific research by recognizing and rewarding outstanding achievements, thus encouraging further innovation.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar
question: Who can apply for the awards?
answer: - Individual | - Organization

scheme_name: Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar
question: How Individual can register ?
answer: Step-1: Visit the official website. | Step-2: Click on the Registration button. | Step-3: Choose type Individual. | Step-4: Provide the required details. | Step-5: Submit.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar
question: What documents are required ?
answer: - Nomination Form. | - Curriculum Vitae (CV) of the nominee. | - Detailed description of the nominee's contribution. | - Supporting documents (research papers, patents, awards certificates, testimonials, letters of recommendation, etc., depending on the specific nomination). | - Aadhaar Card. | - Photograph.

scheme_name: Scheme For Arjuna Awards For Outstanding Performance In Sports And Games
question: What Are The Required Documents For Applying To This Scheme?
answer: - Date of Birth Proof | - User Photograph (Image should be in JPEG/PNG/JPG & size not exceed 5 MB) | - Upload user signature (Signature should be in JPEG/PNG/JPG & size not exceed 250 KB) | - Vigilance Certificate (in case of Govt./PSU/Autonomous organization) | - Certificates of International Achievement details | - Signed Undertaking (as per the given format) by the sportsperson

scheme_name: Scheme For Arjuna Awards For Outstanding Performance In Sports And Games
question: What Is The Amount Of The Cash Prize That Will Be Awarded To The Winner?
answer: The award consists of a statuette, a certificate, a ceremonial dress, and a cash award of ₹ 15,00,000 which will be presented to the winners in a function to be held at a place and on a date to be decided by the Government of India.

scheme_name: Scheme For Arjuna Awards For Outstanding Performance In Sports And Games
question: Is Good Performance Over The Previous Four Years At The International Level Enough In Order To Be Eligible For The Award?
answer: To be eligible for the Award, a sportsperson should have had not only good performance over the previous four years at the International level but also should have shown qualities of leadership, sportsmanship, and a sense of discipline.

scheme_name: Scheme For Arjuna Awards For Outstanding Performance In Sports And Games
question: What Are WADA And NADA? What Is Their Role In The Award?
answer: Sportspersons who have been penalized or against whom inquiry is pending/ongoing for use of drugs/substances banned by the World Anti Doping Agency (WADA) based on a sample collected by the National Anti Doping Agency (NADA) or any other agency authorized by WADA and tested by National Dope Testing Laboratory or any other WADA accredited laboratory, will not be eligible for the Award.

scheme_name: Scheme For Arjuna Awards For Outstanding Performance In Sports And Games
question: What Are The Disciplines Under Which The Government Can Consider Conferring Arjuna Award?
answer: The Government will only consider conferring Arjuna Award in the disciplines falling under the following categories: | a) Olympic Games/Asian Games/Commonwealth Games/World Cup/Word Championship disciplines and cricket or any equivalent recognized international Tournament. | b) Indigenous Games. | c) Sports for the physically challenged.

scheme_name: Scheme For Arjuna Awards For Outstanding Performance In Sports And Games
question: Where Will Be Award Ceremony Be Held?
answer: The function for the presentation of the Award to be held at a place and on a date to be decided by the Government of India.

scheme_name: Scheme For Arjuna Awards For Outstanding Performance In Sports And Games
question: How Many Awards Can Be Conferred In A Calendar Year?
answer: Ordinarily, not more than one award will be given in each discipline in a particular year subject to deserving sportspersons being available. However, at least one award is to be given exclusively for sports for the physically challenged. Further, the principle of one award per discipline may be relaxed in the case of team sports and across gender. That is to say that, the Selection Committee may recommend, in deserving cases with proper justification, more than one sportsperson in respect of team sports and sportspersons of both genders. | Normally not more than 15 awards could be given in any calendar year. However, keeping in view the performance of Indian sportspersons in the Commonwealth, Asian Games, and Olympic Games during a particular year, Arjuna Awards exceeding 15 in number may be allowed with proper justification and approval of Minister-in-charge for Youth Affairs & sports.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Assistance To Disabled Persons For Purchase/Fitting Of Aids/Appliances
question: Q.1 What Is Scheme Of Assistance To Disabled Persons For Purchase/Fitting Of Aids/Appliances ADIP Scheme And How It Is Helping Empowering Divyangjan?
answer: Under the ADIP Scheme, assistive devices are given to PwDs with the aim to improve their independent functioning and arrest the extent of disability and occurrence of secondary disability. The scheme also envisages the conduct of corrective surgery whenever required before providing an assistive device. Detailed scheme can be downloaded from download section on the homepage.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Assistance To Disabled Persons For Purchase/Fitting Of Aids/Appliances
question: Q.3 What Are The Documents Required?
answer: - Passport Size Photographs. | - A copy of the disability certificate. | - Address proof (copy of Aadhaar Card or/ Voter Id Card or/ Ration Card etc.) | - A copy of Income Certificate. | - An undertaking that he/she has not received the same aids & assistive devices from any source during the last three years.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Assistance To Disabled Persons For Purchase/Fitting Of Aids/Appliances
question: Q.4 Who Is The Competent Authority To Issue Income Certificate For Getting Benefit Under The ADIP Scheme ?
answer: - Revenue Agencies or BPL Card or MGNREGA Card | - Disability Pension Card. | - Certificate by M.P./MLA/Councilor/Gram Pradhan | - Notarized Affidavit C/o Implementing Agencies

scheme_name: Scheme Of Assistance To Disabled Persons For Purchase/Fitting Of Aids/Appliances
question: Q.5 Whether Children With Intellectual Disability/ Developmental Delay Below The Age Of 6 Years Are Eligible For Getting Benefits Under The Scheme?
answer: Yes. A temporary Disability Certificate issued by the Competent Medical Authority for Children up to the age of 6 years or a Developmental Delay Certificate issued by the Competent Medical Authority for children up to the age of 6 years is considered for the distribution of TLM Kits under the ADIP Scheme. However, there is no dilution of the condition of a minimum 40% disability.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Assistance To Disabled Persons For Purchase/Fitting Of Aids/Appliances

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: Q1. What Is The Inspiration For Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY)?
answer: Answer:- Ideology of Gram Swaraj of Mahatma Gandhi is the inspiration for Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY)

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: Q2. What Is The Goal Of Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY)?
answer: Answer:- The goal of Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY) is to translate the comprehensive and organic vision of Mahatma Gandhi into reality, keeping in view the present context

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: Q3. What Are The Values That Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY) Propagates?
answer: Answer:- The values that Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY) propagates are | Adopting people's participation as an end in itself ensuring the involvement of all sections of society in all aspects related to the life of village, especially in decision making related to governance | Adhering to Antyodaya enabling the "poorest and the weakest person" in the village to achieve well-being | Affirming gender equality and ensuring respect for women | Guaranteeing social justice | Instilling dignity of labour and the spirit of community service and voluntarism | Promoting a culture of cleanliness | Living in consonance with nature development and ecology ensuring a balance between | Preserving and promoting local cultural heritage | Inculcating mutual cooperation, self-help and self-reliance | Fostering peace and harmony in the village community xi. Bringing about transparency, accountability and probity in public life | Nurturing local self-governance | Adhering to the values enshrined in the Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties of the Indian Constitution

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: Q4. What Are The Main Objectives Of Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY)?
answer: Answer:- The main objectives of Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY) are | To trigger processes which lead to holistic development of the identified Gram Panchayats | To substantially improve the standard of living and quality of life of all sections of the population through | improved basic amenities | higher productivity | enhanced human development | better livelihood opportunities | reduced disparities | access to rights and entitlements | wider social mobilization | enriched social capital | To generate models of local level development and effective local governance which can motivate and inspire neighbouring Gram Panchayats to learn and adapt | To nurture the identified Adarsh Grams as schools of local development to train other Gram Panchayats

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: Q5. What Are The Challenges Related To Local Level Developments As Revealed By Past Experiences?
answer: Answer:- Few challenges related to local level development are | Inability to develop a shared vision of development over a longer period | Disconnect between development inputs delivered and the genuine needs of the community | Lack of participation of all sections of society, especially the marginalized and the aged | Focus on infrastructure and expenditure ignoring the social aspects and sustainable outcomes | Reliance primarily on government grants and not emphasising community contributions and self help | Absence of organic convergence of different schemes | Unfair decisions regarding allocation of benefits to locations and households leading to alienation | Political partisanship perceived and real | Disregard of socio-cultural values of different sections of the community | Existence of multiple power structures and absence of a reconciling mechanism | Ignoring environmental concerns for immediate gains | Prevalence of social evils like drinking, dowry, casteism, communalism and discrimination against women

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: Q6. In Order To Achieve The Objectives Of Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY), What Should Be The Approach?
answer: Answer:- SAGY would be guided by the following approach: | Leveraging the leadership, capacity, commitment and energy of the Members of Parliament (MP) to develop model Gram Panchayats. | Engaging with and mobilizing the community for participatory local level development. | Converging different government programmes, private and voluntary initiatives to achieve comprehensive development in tune with people's aspirations and local potential. | Building partnerships with voluntary organisations, co-operatives and academic and research institutions. | Focusing on outcomes and sustainability

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: Q7. What Areas Should Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY) Activities Should Focus Upon?
answer: Answer:- Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY) activities should focus on holistic development covering personal development, human development, social development and economic development of the citizens.

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: Q8. What Activities Can Be Taken Up Under The Personal Development Of The Villagers?
answer: Answer:- The activities that can be taken up under the personal development of the villagers are | Inculcating hygienic behaviour and practices | Fostering healthy habits including daily exercise and games | Reducing risk behaviour-alcoholism, smoking, substance abuse, etc.

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: Q9. What Activities Can Be Taken Up Under The Human Development Of The Village?
answer: Answer:- The activities that can be taken up under the human development of the village are | Universal access to basic health facilities consisting of health card, medical examination | Total immunization | Balancing the sex-ratio | 100% institutional delivery | Improving nutrition status for all, with special focus on children, adolescent girls, pregnant women, and lactating mothers | Strong focus on the special needs of Persons with Disability (PWD), especially children and women | Universal access to education facilities up to Class 10th and retention | Conversion of schools into 'smart schools'. Smart schools will have IT enabled classrooms, e-libraries, web based teaching and will make all students e-literate required for providing quality education | Adult literacy | E-literacy | Village libraries including e-libraries

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: Q10. What Activities Can Be Taken Up Under The Social Development Of The Village?
answer: Answer:- The activities that can be taken up under the social development of the village are | Activities for promotion of voluntarism like Bharat Nirman Volunteers | Building the capacity of the people to fully participate and contribute to local development | Activities for honouring village elders, local role models especially women, freedom fighters and martyrs iv. Activities for violence and crime free villages such as: | Setting up Citizen Committees | Sensitization, especially of youth | Village sports and folk arts festivals | Having a village song to instil a sense of pride among the people | Celebrating 'Village Day' | Proactive steps for inclusion and integration of socially excluded groups, especially Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: Q17. How To Identify The Village To Convert Into Adarsh Gram?
answer: Answer:- The MP would be free to identify a suitable Gram Panchayat for being developed Adarsh Gram, other than his/her own village or that of his/her spouse. | Lok Sabha MP has to choose a Gram Panchayat from within his/her constituency and Rajya Sabha MP a Gram Panchayat from the rural area of a district of his/her choice in the State from which he/she is elected. Nominated MPs may choose a Gram Panchayat from the rural area of any district in the country. In the case of urban constituencies, (where there are no Gram Panchayats), the MP will identify a Gram Panchayat from a nearby rural constituency.

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: Q18. What Should Be The Ideal Population Of The Adarsh Gram?
answer: Answer:- Gram Panchayat would be the basic unit. It should have a population of 3000 5000 inplain areas and 1000-3000 in hilly, tribal and difficult areas. If these sizes are not available, Gram Panchayats of other sizes could be identified as far as possible approximating the laid down sizes of population.

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: How Is The Post Project Sustainability Of Adarsh Gram Ensured Through SAGY?
answer: Answer:- Post project sustainability is expected to be achieved through the following: | Continuing leadership and guidance of the MP | Strong ownership and leadership of the Gram Panchayat and the village community with role clarity on operation and maintenance of the assets created under the programme. | Involvement of the private sector in operation and maintenance of bigger assets like sewerage and large water supply schemes. | Involvement of SHGs in the operation and maintenance of smaller community assets like vermin compost systems, small water supply schemes, nutrition centres, citizen service centres, libraries etc. | Clear protocols in respect of departmental responsibilities in operation and maintenance to be laid down and agreed upon, upfront at the time of approval of projects under the Plan.

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: Are There Any Incentives In The Implementation Of SAGY?
answer: Answer:- The incentives are in the form of Awards and they are proposed to be given in the following categories: | Best practices | Best Charge Officers | Best District Collectors | Best Adarsh Grams

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: What Is The Mechanism Adopted For Evaluation Of SAGY?
answer: Answer:- A mid-term evaluation of performance would be conducted through a competent independent agency. Also a post-project assessment of performance and outcomes would be similarly undertaken.

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: What Would Be The Expected Outcomes Of The SAGY?
answer: Answer:- The expected outcomes of SAGY would be the following: | Increased livelihoods/employment opportunities | Reduction in distress migration | Freedom from bonded labour, child labour and manual scavenging | 100% registration of deaths and births | Evolution of alternate dispute resolution system acceptable to all sections of the community | Peace and Harmony | Demonstration effect on other Gram Panchayats

scheme_name: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
question: What Will MORD Do For The Capacity Building Of The Functionaries In SAGY?
answer: Answer:- The Ministry of Rural Development would: | Prepare detailed handbooks for operationalizing the different components for the stakeholders. | Document and disseminate best practices related to innovative village development. | Set up a help desk in the NIRD & PR to serve as a single point for clarification of doubts and for giving advice where necessary. | Identify the best performing Gram Panchayats for peer-group learning through twinning arrangements.

scheme_name: Scheme for Action Research and Studies on Judicial Reforms

scheme_name: Scheme For Award Of Senior/Junior Fellowships To Outstanding Persons In The Fields Of Culture

scheme_name: Scheme For Award Of Senior/Junior Fellowships To Outstanding Persons In The Fields Of Culture

scheme_name: Scheme For Award Of Senior/Junior Fellowships To Outstanding Persons In The Fields Of Culture

scheme_name: Scheme For Award Of Senior/Junior Fellowships To Outstanding Persons In The Fields Of Culture

scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance to State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations

question: How is the share capital contribution divided between the Central Government and State Governments for this development program?

scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance to State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations

scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance to State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations

scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance to State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations
question: When was this particular financial assistance program for economic development first introduced by the government?
answer: The program was introduced in the year 1978-79 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme in States and Union Territories.

scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance to State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations
question: How many states and territories currently have these development corporations operating to provide assistance?
answer: Currently, State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations are functioning in 23 States and 4 Union Territories.

scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance to State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations
question: What is the minimum recovery rate requirement that affects the release of central share equity capital?
answer: The minimum recovery rate requirement is 60% of loans disbursed by State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations to beneficiaries.

scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance to State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations
question: Are there any relaxed recovery rate conditions available for states with high Scheduled Castes population?
answer: Yes, eleven high Scheduled Castes population states have relaxed recovery rates based on their performance during previous plan periods.

scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance to State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations
question: What percentage of the Share Equity Capital released by Central Government must be utilized before further assistance?
answer: 75% of the Share Equity Capital released by Central Government to State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations must be utilized.

scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance to State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations
question: Who determines the cost norms and project guidelines for the various economic development activities covered?
answer: The cost norms of the projects and schemes are determined by the State Government and State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations.

scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance to State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations
question: What is the interest rate structure for the margin money loans provided under this financial assistance program?
answer: Margin money loans are provided at a low rate of interest, though the specific rate is not mentioned in the guidelines.

scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance to State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations
question: How are the funds from Central Government typically channeled to reach the State development corporations?
answer: Central share of equity capital is sent directly to State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations, or routed through National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation when necessary.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission – Grameen PHASE I
question: What is the aim of the scheme?
answer: The aim of the scheme is to eliminate open defecation in rural India through toilet construction and behavioral change.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission – Grameen PHASE I
question: Who is eligible to apply under the scheme?
answer: Rural households without toilet facilities, especially those that are poor, underprivileged, or marginalized.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission – Grameen PHASE I
question: Are households with existing toilets eligible?
answer: No, households with existing functional toilets are not eligible for the incentive.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission – Grameen PHASE I
question: What steps are involved in applying for the scheme?
answer: Contact the local Gram Panchayat, submit documents, construct the toilet, verify it through geo-tagging, and receive the incentive.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission – Grameen PHASE I
question: What kind of toilets were promoted under this scheme?
answer: The scheme promoted twin-pit toilets as a cost-effective and sustainable sanitation solution.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission – Grameen PHASE I
question: How does twin pit toilet technology work?
answer: Two pits are used alternately, and the filled pit is sealed for decomposition, turning waste into safe manure.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission – Grameen PHASE I
question: How long does each pit last?
answer: Each pit is typically designed to last around three years, depending on usage.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission – Grameen PHASE I
question: What is the IMIS system used in this scheme?
answer: IMIS (Integrated Management Information System) is used for real-time tracking of toilet construction and verification.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II
question: What is the Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II?
answer: "Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II" is focused on sustaining the Open Defecation Free (ODF) status of villages and enhancing cleanliness through Solid and Liquid Waste Management (SLWM) in rural areas. It aims to make villages ODF Plus by addressing ODF sustainability, solid waste management, liquid waste management, and visual cleanliness.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II
question: What are the main objectives of SBM(G) Phase II?
answer: The main objectives of SBM(G) Phase II are: | - ODF-Sustainability: Ensuring that villages maintain their ODF status. | - Solid Waste Management: Establishing waste segregation and composting systems. | - Liquid Waste Management: Setting up soak pits and treatment for greywater and stormwater. | - Visual Cleanliness: Enhancing the overall cleanliness and hygiene of rural areas.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II
question: What changes have been made in SBM(G) Phase-II as compared to SBM(G) ?
answer: New eligible households will be provided incentive @ Rs.12000 per household for construction of IHHL, which is the existing norm of financial incentive. Only new eligible households will be provided the incentive money. Ineligible households will be motivated to construct the toilet on their own. | The Community Sanitary Complex has been renamed as Community Managed Sanitation Complex (CMSC). The financial assistance for the CMSC has been enhanced from Rs.2,00,000/- to Rs. 3,00,000/- with sharing of 30% funds from 15th Finance Commission grants to Rural Local Bodies, and remaining 70% under SBM(G). | Provision for IEC and Capacity Building will be at 5% of total project cost, with 2% to be utilised at the Central level (Government of India level) and 3% at State/district level. | Provision for administrative cost will be 1% of the project cost. | Under SBM-G Phase II, block and district level interventions have also been introduced for certain activities related to SLWM. | Generally, funding for SLWM will be on a per capita basis instead of earlier provision based on the number of households in a GP. While 30% of the funding for village level SLWM activities will be from 15th Finance Commission grants, the remaining 70% will be borne under SBM(G). However, for some activities such as Plastic Waste Management at block level and model GOBAR-dhan projects at district level, there will be a fixed amount of financial assistance for a block and a district. | For the first time, 50% funds of 15th Finance Commission grants to rural local bodies is earmarked for water and sanitation as tied funds.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II
question: Who is eligible for the SBM(G) Phase II incentives?
answer: Eligible households include: Below Poverty Line (BPL), Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs), Households with physically disabled persons, Landless labourers with homestead, Small and marginal farmers, Women-headed households. | Eligibility is also contingent on the household's need for a toilet and whether they have previously received benefits from other government programs for toilet construction.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II
question: What are the main activities carried out under the SBM(G) Phase-II ?
answer: The main activities are : | (i) Construction of Individual Household Latrines (IHHL) | (ii) Construction of Community Managed Sanitation Complexes (CMSCs) | (iii) Solid and Liquid Waste Management (SLWM) activities | (iv) Continued Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) and Capacity Strengthening at all levels.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II
question: What is the financial support provided for constructing Individual Household Latrines (IHHLs)?
answer: A financial support of ₹12,000/- is provided for the construction of IHHLs, which includes storage for handwashing and cleaning of the toilet.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II
question: What is the process for retrofitting existing toilets?
answer: Retrofitting involves upgrading existing toilets to address issues such as faulty construction or inadequate components. This is done through local interventions and promoting necessary modifications.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II
question: How are Community Sanitary Complexes (CSCs) prioritized?
answer: CSCs are prioritized for ODF-plus villages with over 100 households, focusing on SC/ST areas and locations frequented by migrant workers. Accessibility, water availability, and separate facilities for men, women, and Divyangjans are key considerations.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II
question: How can I apply for SBM(G) Phase II incentives?
answer: Applications can be submitted online through the SBM(G) official website. Visit https://swachhbharatmission.ddws.gov.in/, register if you are not already, and then log in to complete and submit your application.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II
question: How are applications for SBM(G) Phase II verified and approved?
answer: Applications are verified by concerned block or district authorities to confirm eligibility. Only applications that meet the criteria and are approved will be eligible for receiving incentives under the program.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission – Urban 2.0
question: How will I receive my financial support under the Scheme?
answer: All financial incentives will be deposited directly (by electronic clearing service) into the bank accounts of the beneficiary households (including accounts opened under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana). No cash/cheque disbursals shall take place.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission – Urban 2.0
question: Will I receive the entire amount in one go if I am eligible for the scheme?
answer: No, 50% of the incentive will be released on approval by the ULB. Remaining 50% of Central Government incentive as 2nd instalment should be released to the identified beneficiary household upon verification of physical progress of construction of the household toilet.

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission – Urban 2.0
question: Where can I upload the picture of the toilet to claim remaining amount?
answer: You can upload the picture at http://swachhbharaturban.gov.in/ihhl/writereaddata/UserManual_ToiletPhotoUpload_CSC_ULB_Applicant.pdf

scheme_name: Seva Bhoj Yojna
question: What is the objective of the scheme?
answer: Under the Scheme, Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) and Central Government's share of Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) paid on purchase of specific raw food items by Charitable/Religious Institutions like Gurudwaras, Temples, Dharmik Ashrams, Mosques, Dargahs, Churches, Math, Monasteries, etc. for distributing free food to public shall be reimbursed as Financial Assistance by the Government of India.

scheme_name: Seva Bhoj Yojna
question: Which ministry has started the scheme?
answer: Ministry of Culture, Government of India

scheme_name: Seva Bhoj Yojna
question: Is this Central Sector Scheme?
answer: Yes, this is a Central Sector Scheme.

scheme_name: Seva Bhoj Yojna
question: When was this scheme launched?
answer: The Scheme has been made operational with effect from the 1st of August, 2018.

scheme_name: Seva Bhoj Yojna
question: What is the scope of the scheme?
answer: This is a Central Sector Scheme for providing reimbursement of CGST and the Central Government's share of IGST paid by charitable/religious institutions on the purchase of specific raw food items for serving free food to the public/devotees. The scheme shall be applicable only to such institutions which are eligible under the Scheme.

scheme_name: Seva Bhoj Yojna
question: What are the types of activities supported under the Scheme?
answer: Free 'Prasad' or free food or free 'Langar'/'Bhandara' (community kitchen) offered by charitable/religious institutions like Gurudwara, Temples, Dharmik Ashram, Mosques, Dargah, Church, Math, Monasteries, etc.

scheme_name: Seva Bhoj Yojna
question: What are the benefits of the scheme?
answer: Financial assistance in the form of reimbursement shall be provided to the institution that has already paid GST on all or any of the raw food items such as Ghee, Edible oil, Sugar/Burra/Jaggery, Rice, Atta /Maida/Rava /Flour, Pulses.

scheme_name: Seva Bhoj Yojna
question: What is the creation of providing financial assistance?
answer: Financial assistance will be provided on First-cum-First Serve basis of registration linked to funds available for the purpose in a financial year.

scheme_name: Seva Bhoj Yojna
question: Which Institutions/organizations are eligible for this scheme?
answer: A Public Trust or society or body corporate or organization, or institution covered under the provisions of section 10 (23BBA) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 (as amended from time to time) or registered under the provisions of section 12AA of the Income Tax Act, 1961, for charitable/ religious purposes, or a company formed and registered under the provisions of section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 or section 25 of the Companies Act, 1956, as the case may be, for charitable/ religious purposes or a Public Trust registered as such for charitable/religious purposes under any Law for the time being in force, or a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, for charitable/religious purposes.

scheme_name: Seva Bhoj Yojna
question: How old should an institution be to apply for the scheme?
answer: The institutions/organizations should have been in existence for the preceding three years before applying for assistance.

scheme_name: Seva Bhoj Yojna
question: How many people have to be given free food in a calendar month?
answer: The institutions shall serve free food to at least 5000 people in a calendar month.

scheme_name: Seva Bhoj Yojna
question: How can an institution apply under the scheme?
answer: Charitable/Religious Institutions shall first register with the Darpan Portal of NITI Aayog and get a Unique ID generated by Darpan Portal (if not already obtained). Thereafter, the institution shall enroll itself in the CSMS Portal on the Ministry of in a prescribed format. Thereafter, the Charitable/Religious Institution shall apply 'online' in the prescribed application form and upload the required documents as listed below in the CSMS Portal of the Ministry of Culture's website: www.indiaculture.nic.in

scheme_name: Scheme For Campus Accommodation & Facilities Enhancing Social Experience
question: What Are The Objectives Of The "CAFES" Scheme?
answer: Objective | (a) The scheme is initiated to facilitate the continuation of education and also the interaction between the students beyond class hours for their all-around development. | (b) The scheme aims to support Government/ Government-aided engineering colleges/ University departments/ Polytechnics for the construction of hostels for providing residential accommodation for students/researchers. | (c) This AICTE scheme also allows the extension of existing hostels in the institute by additional construction work to benefit the students. | (d) This scheme has three variants addressing the needs of: | (i) CAFES - SC/ST students | (ii) CAFES - NER (Institute located in North Eastern Region) | (iii) CAFES - Differently Abled students

scheme_name: Scheme For Campus Accommodation & Facilities Enhancing Social Experience
question: How Many Variants Are To This Scheme?
answer: This scheme has three variants addressing the needs of: | (i) CAFES - SC/ST students | (ii) CAFES - NER (Institute located in North Eastern Region) | (iii) CAFES - Differently Abled students

scheme_name: Scheme For Campus Accommodation & Facilities Enhancing Social Experience
question: Does The Scheme Also Provide Support To Polytechnics?
answer: Yes, the scheme aims to support Government/ Government-aided engineering colleges/ University departments/ Polytechnics for the construction of hostels for providing residential accommodation for students/researchers.

scheme_name: Scheme For Campus Accommodation & Facilities Enhancing Social Experience
question: Is There An Upper Ceiling To The Financial Assistance Of The Universities?
answer: Yes, the limit of Funding from AICTE is ₹ 3.25 crore

scheme_name: Scheme For Campus Accommodation & Facilities Enhancing Social Experience
question: What Amount Out Of The Total Fund Must Go For The Construction Of The Hostel?
answer: Construction of Hostel: ₹ 3,00,00,000

scheme_name: Scheme For Campus Accommodation & Facilities Enhancing Social Experience
question: What Amount Out Of The Total Fund Must Go For The Establishment Of Gym Equipment?
answer: Establishment of Gym equipment: ₹ 5,00,000

scheme_name: Scheme For Campus Accommodation & Facilities Enhancing Social Experience
question: Are The Funds Disbursed In Installments Or As A Lump Sum?
answer: Disbursement of the Funds is done in installments - | (a) Disbursement of 50% of the amount (1st installment) in advance upon sanction of the proposal, out of funds for the construction of the hostel. | (b) Disbursement of 40% of the amount (2nd installment), out of funds for the construction of the hostel on utilization of the 1st installment to be released only after spot inspection carried out by an Evaluation Committee comprising of two engineers (one each from Civil & Architect) from AICTE approved panel to be organized by concerned RO AICTE. The EVC report should contain all the mandatory documents. | (c) Disbursement of the remaining 10% of the amount (3rd installment), out of funds for the construction of the hostel on submitting a completion certificate by registered Civil Engineer/ Architect/ PWD and submission of all other mandatory documents as mentioned in the sanction letters and the parameter of the scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme For Campus Accommodation & Facilities Enhancing Social Experience
question: What Are The Conditions Regarding The Funds For The Establishment Of The Gym, And Indoor Sports Club?
answer: The funds for the establishment of the gym, indoor sports club, and the establishment of the library would be granted on submission of a proper quotation at a competitive rate after the release of the 2nd installment amount and handing over the building in all respects.

scheme_name: Scheme For Campus Accommodation & Facilities Enhancing Social Experience
question: Are Newly Opened Institutes Eligible To Apply To This Scheme?
answer: No, the Institute must be in existence for the last five years in order to be eligible to apply to this scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme For Campus Accommodation & Facilities Enhancing Social Experience
question: Are All The Institutes Throughout The Country Eligible For "CAFES - SC/ST Students"?

scheme_name: Scheme For Campus Accommodation & Facilities Enhancing Social Experience

scheme_name: Scheme For Campus Accommodation & Facilities Enhancing Social Experience

scheme_name: Scheme For Campus Accommodation & Facilities Enhancing Social Experience

scheme_name: Scheme of Grants-in-Aid for supporting professional associations/ organisations of social scientists, companies and trusts duly registered under the Companies Act for their development

scheme_name: Scheme of Grants-in-Aid for supporting professional associations/ organisations of social scientists, companies and trusts duly registered under the Companies Act for their development

scheme_name: Scheme of Grants-in-Aid for supporting professional associations/ organisations of social scientists, companies and trusts duly registered under the Companies Act for their development

scheme_name: Scheme of Grants-in-Aid for supporting professional associations/ organisations of social scientists, companies and trusts duly registered under the Companies Act for their development
question: Where should the application be sent?
answer: PRS Division, ICSSR, Aruna Asaf Ali Marg, New Delhi-110067.

scheme_name: Scheme of Grants-in-Aid for supporting professional associations/ organisations of social scientists, companies and trusts duly registered under the Companies Act for their development
question: Can applications be submitted anytime?
answer: Yes, applications are open throughout the year.

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS) for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe
question: What is Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS)?
answer: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS) is to facilitate capacity augmentation of existing SC/ST MSEs and for creation on new enterprises among SC/ST communities, 25 percent capital subsidy is provided for purchase of plant & machinery / equipment through institutional finance (bank loan).

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS) for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe
question: Which department has launched this scheme?
answer: This scheme has been launched by the Ministry Of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises.

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS) for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe
question: What are the provisions available under SCLCSS?
answer: Under SCLCSS, 25% subsidy to SC/ST MSEs on institutional finance for procurement of Plant & Machinery / equipment without any sector specific restrictions is provided.

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS) for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe
question: Which products/ sub-sectors have been approved under the SCLCSS component?
answer: There is no such restriction. The scheme covers SC/ST MSEs of both manufacturing and service sectors. However, the industries covered under the RED category as per the Classification of industries for consent management (Schedule- VIII, rules 3(2) and 12 of Ministry of Environment & Forests, Govt. of India) shall not be eligible for subsidy under the above scheme.

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS) for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe
question: Whether the Scheme is applicable for new MSEs?
answer: Yes.

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS) for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe
question: Is SCLCSS applicable for medium and large-scale Enterprises?
answer: No, only Micro and Small-Scale Enterprises (existing & new) are eligible under SCLCSS.

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS) for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe
question: Whether the subsidy can be availed for replacement of machinery and equipment?
answer: The subsidy shall be admissible for investment in acquisition/replacement of plant & machinery/equipments & technology up-gradation of any kind through institutional finance. But fabricated /second-hand machinery /equipment will not be eligible for subsidy under the component of the scheme.

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS) for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe
question: Whether this subsidy can be claimed in combination with any other scheme?
answer: The units availing subsidy under the SCLCSS shall be eligible for all other types of subsidies except any other Central Government /State Government Subsidy for technology upgradation.

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS) for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe
question: What is the tenure of term loan eligible for this subsidy?
answer: To avail the subsidy benefit under the scheme, the sanctioned term loan should not be for less than three years including moratorium period for MSEs.

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS) for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe
question: What is the mechanism for disbursement of subsidy to the unit?
answer: Banks will follow the principle of First -In -First -Out (FIFO) while submitting the claims online under SCLCSS Scheme. The principle of First -In -First -Out (FIFO) will also be followed by the NSSH Cell for disbursement of subsidy to the eligible beneficiary unit.

scheme_name: Senior Citizens Saving Scheme
question: How Can I Open A Senior Citizen Savings Schemes Account Online?
answer: Online application facility is not available for SCSS. In order to open a SCSS account, the customer must visit the post office or bank branch and fill up the related form. The same form should be attached with KYC documents, age proof, ID proof, Address proof and cheque for deposit amount.

scheme_name: Senior Citizens Saving Scheme
question: Is 80C Applicable On Senior Citizen Savings Schemes?
answer: Yes, investments made in SCSS are eligible for income tax deduction benefits under the Section 80C of Income Tax Act, 1961.

scheme_name: Senior Citizens Saving Scheme
question: Can I Open A Senior Citizen Saving Account With SBI Bank?
answer: Yes, any eligible candidate can open a senior citizen savings account with banks such as the State Bank of India. However, according to SBI's guidelines, a depositor can hold two or more SCSS accounts only if the deposits in all accounts taken together do not exceed Rs.15 lakh.

scheme_name: Senior Citizens Saving Scheme
question: What Is The Maximum Age Of Senior Citizen Saving Account Opening?
answer: Any individual, above the age of 60, can open Senior citizen savings account accompanied by all the required documents.

scheme_name: Senior Citizens Saving Scheme
question: What Is The Eligibility Criteria Of Joint Senior Citizen Saving Account?
answer: While opening a joint SCSS account, the age of first depositor is supposed to be above 60 years. However, there is no age limit for the second applicant. The joint account can be opened only with the spouse. However, the entire amount in a joint account will be attributable only to the first account holder.

scheme_name: Senior Citizens Saving Scheme
question: Can Both The Spouses Open Separate Accounts?
answer: Yes, individual accounts can be opened as well, provided the deposit limit is a maximum of Rs.15 lakh. Of course, it has to adhere to the rules of the scheme.

scheme_name: Senior Citizens Saving Scheme
question: Is There Any Income Tax Rebate / Exemption?
answer: Yes, tax deduction of up to Rs.1.5 lakh can be claimed under Section 80C of the Indian Tax Act, 1961.

scheme_name: Senior Citizens Saving Scheme
question: Is TDS Applicable To The Scheme?
answer: Yes if the interest exceeds Rs.10,000 per annum, TDS is applicable. In this scheme, interest payments are no exemption to deduction of tax at source.

scheme_name: Senior Citizens Saving Scheme
question: Any Minimum Limit Has Been Prescribed For Deduction Of Tax At Source?
answer: As per government regulations, tax has to be deducted at source as per the minimum balance.

scheme_name: Senior Citizens Saving Scheme
question: Can A Person Holding A Power Of Attorney Sign For The Nominee In The Nomination Form?
answer: No, a person holding a Power of Attorney cannot sign in place for the nominee in the nomination form.

scheme_name: Senior Citizens Saving Scheme
question: In Case Of A Joint Account, If The First Holder / Depositor Expires Before Maturity, Can The Account Be Continued?
answer: Yes, the nominee can hold the account of the expired depositor in case of a death, provided it pertains to the SCSS Rules.

scheme_name: Senior Citizens Saving Scheme
question: Is There Any Fee Prescribed For Nomination And / Or Change / Cancellation Of Nomination?
answer: No fee is charged.

scheme_name: Senior Citizens Saving Scheme
question: Can An Account Holder Obtain Loan By Pledging The Deposit / Account Under The SCSS, 2004?
answer: Periodic withdrawals for loans are not possible in this scheme as it defies the very nature of the scheme.

scheme_name: Star College Scheme For Strengthening Of Science Education And Training At Undergraduate Level
question: When Is The Call For DBT Star College Scheme Announced?
answer: The call for the DBT-Star College scheme for both Urban and Rural categories is announced annually and is advertised on the DBT website.

scheme_name: Star College Scheme For Strengthening Of Science Education And Training At Undergraduate Level
question: What Are The 'Urban' And 'Rural' Categories Of Colleges?
answer: DBT is focused on the equitable percolation of benefits of the Star College Scheme throughout the country and is committed to ensuring that geographical location and access to means of communication and technology should not be a deterrent for securing this highly competitive grant. Therefore, since 2018-19 Colleges have been categorized into Urban and Rural categories based on the physical location of the college. | Colleges applying under the Rural category should mandatorily attach a certificate (with the application) from competent authority (local administration and not the Principal of the College) either in Hindi or English stating that the college is located in a Rural area, failing which applications shall not be considered further.

scheme_name: Star College Scheme For Strengthening Of Science Education And Training At Undergraduate Level
question: Can A College Request Addition Of New Departments During The Ongoing Tenure Of Support?
answer: Colleges requesting the addition of new departments should first complete one cycle of support i.e. 3 years with the departments that the grant was recommended for.

scheme_name: Star College Scheme For Strengthening Of Science Education And Training At Undergraduate Level
question: Who Can Be A Coordinator For A Star College Scheme?
answer: The Star College Scheme encourages young and energetic faculty of a College to assume greater responsibilities besides their routine roles and functions. A Coordinator should be active, engage in networking with other Departments seeking support under the DBT-Star College Scheme, and should be involved with the overall functioning of the scheme in respective Colleges. | The Coordinator for the Star College Scheme shall be responsible for the coordination between the Colleges and DBT; thus the change of coordinator shall not be entertained during the entire duration of the support unless there is some personal issue due to which the coordinator is not available, for the duration of more than six months at a stretch.

scheme_name: Star College Scheme For Strengthening Of Science Education And Training At Undergraduate Level
question: Is There Any Guidance Provided By DBT During The Tenure Of Support?
answer: For any assistance, recipients of the DBT-Star College grant / Co-ordinators may contact: | Adviser: Dr. Anamika Gambhir, Sc.
