scheme_name: Star College Scheme For Strengthening Of Science Education And Training At Undergraduate Level
question: Is There A Mechanism For Mentoring Colleges Aspiring For Support Under The DBT Star College Scheme?
answer: Each College supported under the DBT-Star College scheme is envisaged to promote networking and strengthen ties with neighboring institutions and a separate fund is provided for mentoring activities. | A College aspiring to apply for a Star College grant may get in touch with the neighboring Star College. A list of Colleges supported under the DBT-Star College The scheme with contact details of the coordinators is provided below. | Additionally, DBT also conducts workshops and outreach activities periodically throughout the country. Details are provided on the Twitter handle of DBT.

scheme_name: Star College Scheme For Strengthening Of Science Education And Training At Undergraduate Level
question: What Are The Objectives Of This Scheme?
answer: The following are the objectives of this scheme: | - To strengthen the academic and physical infrastructure for achieving excellence in teaching and training. | - To enhance the quality of the learning and teaching process to stimulate original thinking through 'hands-on' exposure to experimental work and participation in summer schools. | - To promote networking and strengthen ties with neighboring institutions and other laboratories. | - To conduct specialized training programs for faculty improvement for optimizing technical capabilities. | - To increase the capabilities of core instrumentation resources by procuring new equipment and upgrading of existing facilities. | - To provide access and exposure to students to research laboratories and industries in the country. | - To help in devising standard curricula and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) / kits for practicals.

scheme_name: Star College Scheme For Strengthening Of Science Education And Training At Undergraduate Level
question: What Benefits Do The Students Have In This Scheme?
answer: For Students, there are the following benefits: | Student training via the introduction of practicals, prescribed in the curriculum.Introduction of conceptual clarity via engaging students in minor projects, either singly or in groups of students not exceeding 4 in number. | Inclusion of techniques for 'hands-on' training to strengthen concepts taught otherwise via theoretical approach. | Summer training preferably via engaging students in research projects. | Visits to neighboring industries, research institutions, or places of academic value. | Use of IT in classroom, laboratory, and library activities. | Organizing lectures by eminent scientists, and career counseling lectures specifically for creating awareness among students about their future career options in science.

scheme_name: Star College Scheme For Strengthening Of Science Education And Training At Undergraduate Level
question: What Benefits Do The Faculties Have In This Scheme?
answer: For Faculties, there are the following benefits: | Faculty improvement program. | Participation in summer courses for skill upgradation to be able to train students. | Curriculum change to ensure more, 'hands-on' laboratory work.Greater emphasis on communicating research and research process to students. | Introduce an internal review process by students regarding the implementation of various activities under the Star College Scheme. | Feedback from students regarding the competence of faculty, adequacy of teaching/laboratory environment, and additional needs, if any.

scheme_name: Star College Scheme For Strengthening Of Science Education And Training At Undergraduate Level
question: Where Can I Find The State/UT Wise List Of Colleges Supported Through This Scheme?
answer: The State/UT Wise List Of Colleges Supported through this Scheme can be found at this link - | https://dbtindia.gov.in/sites/default/files/uploadfiles/List%20of%20ongoing%20colleges%20supported%20under%20Star%20College%20Scheme.pdf

scheme_name: Star College Scheme For Strengthening Of Science Education And Training At Undergraduate Level
question: Where Can I Find The Link To The Scheme Terms & Conditions?
answer: The Scheme Terms & Conditions can be found at this link - | https://dbtindia.gov.in/sites/default/files/Terms%20%26%20Conditions%20of%20Star%20College%20Scheme.pdf

scheme_name: Skill Development and Training of Candidates in Technical Textiles
question: What is this scheme?
answer: It is a skill development and training program under the National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM) by the Ministry of Textiles to train 50,000 candidates for the technical textiles industry.

scheme_name: Skill Development and Training of Candidates in Technical Textiles
question: Who can benefit from this scheme?
answer: The scheme is designed for unskilled workers seeking employment in technical textiles, professionals looking to upskill or reskill, and personnel already engaged in various technical textile applications. It ensures opportunities for a wide range of candidates to enhance their employability.

scheme_name: Skill Development and Training of Candidates in Technical Textiles
question: Who can implement the training programs?
answer: Training programs can be conducted by recognized training institutes, textile companies, export councils, Centers of Excellence, and public academic institutions under the Ministry of Textiles. Only empaneled implementing agencies approved by the Ministry can execute the programs.

scheme_name: Skill Development and Training of Candidates in Technical Textiles
question: What sectors are covered under the scheme?
answer: The scheme is implemented in two phases. Phase I includes Agrotech, Buildtech, Geotech, Indutech, Meditech, Mobiltech, and Protech, while Phase II covers Clothtech, Hometech, Oekotech, Sportech, and Packtech. These sectors represent strategically important areas of the technical textiles industry.

scheme_name: Skill Development and Training of Candidates in Technical Textiles
question: What are the benefits for trainees?
answer: Trainees gain industry-aligned skill training, certification, better employment opportunities, exposure to diverse technical textile applications, and the development of transferable skills. The scheme also enhances adaptability and prepares candidates to meet industry requirements.

scheme_name: Skill Development and Training of Candidates in Technical Textiles
question: Is financial support provided?
answer: Yes, the Ministry of Textiles shares the training cost with the trainees. The Ministry's contribution covers candidate mobilization, curriculum development, trainer salaries, teaching aids, equipment, raw materials, assessment costs, and other components as per the Common Norms for Skill Development Schemes.

scheme_name: Skill Development and Training of Candidates in Technical Textiles
question: What is the eligibility for applicants?
answer: Eligible applicants include Indian citizens of working age, unskilled workers, undergraduates, professionals seeking upskilling or reskilling, and personnel already engaged in technical textile sectors. Specific eligibility may vary based on the type of training program.

scheme_name: Skill Development and Training of Candidates in Technical Textiles
question: How are agencies selected?
answer: The Skill Development Committee (SDC) under NTTM reviews applications from agencies and shortlists eligible candidates. Empanelment is communicated via an official Ministry order, and only empaneled agencies can conduct the training programs.

scheme_name: Skill Development and Training of Candidates in Technical Textiles
question: Is certification provided after training?
answer: Yes, upon successful completion of the training, candidates receive industry-recognized certification, which is aligned with market requirements and international curriculum standards. Certification is endorsed by at least five industry partners to ensure credibility.

scheme_name: Scheme for ‘Skill Development in ESDM for Digital India’
question: What is the objective of the Scheme?
answer: The scheme aims to create a skilled workforce in the Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector by providing training, certification, and placement-linked support.

scheme_name: Scheme for ‘Skill Development in ESDM for Digital India’
question: Who can apply for this scheme?
answer: Candidates studying in Class 9 or above, school dropouts (8th pass onwards), ITI certificate holders, diploma holders, undergraduates, graduates, and individuals registered with employment exchanges can apply, subject to course eligibility.

scheme_name: Scheme for ‘Skill Development in ESDM for Digital India’
question: What is the minimum age required to apply?
answer: The applicant should be at least 17 years old at the time of enrolment.

scheme_name: Scheme for ‘Skill Development in ESDM for Digital India’
question: Is Aadhaar mandatory for enrolment?
answer: Yes, the applicant should have a valid Aadhaar Number or Aadhaar Enrolment ID and must provide consent for Aadhaar authentication or e-KYC.

scheme_name: Scheme for ‘Skill Development in ESDM for Digital India’
question: What kind of training is provided under the scheme?
answer: Training is provided in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector across NSQF Level 1 to Level 5 courses in both manufacturing and service domains.

scheme_name: Scheme for ‘Skill Development in ESDM for Digital India’
question: Is there any fee for the training?
answer: Yes, candidates need to pay a Registration-cum-Certification Fee (RCCF). Course fee is subsidised: | - 75% reimbursed for the General category | - 100% reimbursed for SC/ST/EWS candidates (subject to conditions)

scheme_name: Scheme for ‘Skill Development in ESDM for Digital India’
question: Will the fee be refunded?
answer: Yes, the RCCF and course fee (as applicable) are reimbursed after successful certification and placement, as per scheme norms.

scheme_name: Scheme for ‘Skill Development in ESDM for Digital India’
question: Is placement guaranteed under the scheme?
answer: The scheme is placement-linked and Training Partners are required to facilitate placement. A minimum of 70% placement is targeted for full reimbursement.

scheme_name: Scheme for ‘Skill Development in ESDM for Digital India’
question: Can a candidate apply more than once?
answer: No, a candidate can avail the benefit only once. However, for manufacturing job roles, progression to a higher NSQF level may be allowed.

scheme_name: Scheme for ‘Skill Development in ESDM for Digital India’
question: Are there any attendance requirements?
answer: Yes, the candidate should maintain at least 70% attendance to be eligible for assessment.

scheme_name: Scheme for ‘Skill Development in ESDM for Digital India’
question: Is there any reservation under the scheme?
answer: Yes, 40% of seats are reserved for SC, ST, and EWS categories, with specific percentage allocations for each category.

scheme_name: Scheme for ‘Skill Development in ESDM for Digital India’
question: What is the income limit for EWS category?
answer: The applicant's family income should not exceed ₹2,00,000/- per annum to be eligible under the EWS category.

scheme_name: Scheme for ‘Skill Development in ESDM for Digital India’
question: How is the financial assistance disbursed?
answer: Financial assistance is disbursed in two stages: | - After certification | - After placement

scheme_name: Scheme for ‘Skill Development in ESDM for Digital India’
question: Where can a candidate apply for the scheme?
answer: Candidates can apply through the official portal or by approaching affiliated Training Partners under the scheme.

scheme_name: SEBI ITD Internship Program
question: How Many Interns Does The SEBI ITD Internship Program Accept?
answer: The program accepts up to 15 interns.

scheme_name: SEBI ITD Internship Program
question: What Kind Of Projects Will The Interns Work On During The Program?
answer: The interns will work on different Information Technology (IT) projects, including Data Analytics (DA), regulatory business processes and reporting, and FinTech at SEBI.

scheme_name: SEBI ITD Internship Program
question: What Is The Duration Of The Internship Program?
answer: The internship program is proposed to be for a contiguous period of minimum 1 year, which may comprise of either 2 semesters and 1 summer/winter internship or 3 trimesters and 1 summer/winter internship.

scheme_name: SEBI ITD Internship Program
question: What Is The Schedule For The Internship At SEBI?
answer: Interns are expected to intern at SEBI for at least 3 days a week, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and Public Holidays.

scheme_name: SEBI ITD Internship Program
question: Who Is Eligible To Apply For The SEBI ITD Internship Program?
answer: Candidates pursuing a full-time MBA/MCA or equivalent degree or diploma of a duration of two years, holding a full-time graduate degree in engineering or a BCA degree, having a strong aptitude for computer programming and data analytics, and with a minimum of 60% aggregate marks at the graduate level or equivalent CGPA are eligible to apply. The age of the applicant should not exceed 30 years as of January 1 of the respective year, and they should be Indian citizens.

scheme_name: SEBI ITD Internship Program
question: Is A Basic Understanding Of Financial Markets Mandatory For Applicants?
answer: No, a basic understanding of financial markets is desirable but not mandatory.

scheme_name: SEBI ITD Internship Program
question: What Facilities Are Provided To Interns During The Internship Program?
answer: Interns undergoing internship at SEBI for 3 days a week receive a monthly stipend of ₹25,000, and interns undergoing internship for 4 days a week receive a monthly stipend of ₹30,000. Interns are entitled to a certain number of leaves per year. Outstation candidates may be provided with unfurnished shared accommodation, subject to availability. Lunch at the SEBI office is provided, and interns receive a certificate of completion of the internship program.

scheme_name: SEBI ITD Internship Program
question: What Documents Need To Be Submitted By Eligible Institutes To Express Their Interest In Participating In The SEBI ITD Internship Program?
answer: Eligible institutes need to express their interest by submitting the prescribed format (Annexure 1) along with the relevant enclosures. They also need to submit the profiles of interested eligible candidates in the prescribed format (Annexure 2).

scheme_name: SEBI ITD Internship Program
question: Where Should All Correspondences Be Addressed?
answer: All correspondences should be addressed to the Chief General Manager, Information Technology Department, SEBI Bhavan, C4-A, G Block, Bandra Kurla Complex, Bandra (East), Mumbai - 400051, Maharashtra, India.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: What is the main objective of the SECI internship?
answer: To provide practical experience and insights into the renewable energy sector.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: Who can apply for the SECI internship?
answer: Students pursuing degrees in engineering, renewable energy, finance, HR, IT, and related fields.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: Can I apply more than once in a financial year?
answer: No, you can apply only once per financial year.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: Are there any fees for the internship program?
answer: No, there are no fees charged to the interns.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: Is there any compensation for boarding or transportation?
answer: No, the internship does not include boarding or transportation compensation.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: Can I apply offline for the SECI internship?
answer: No, only the online process is available

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: How do I apply for the SECI internship?
answer: Apply online via SECI's website from the 1st to the 10th of each month.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: Can SECI terminate my internship?
answer: Yes, SECI can terminate the internship at any time without notice.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: Can I leave the internship program early?
answer: Yes, by giving seven days' prior notice to the Project Head/Mentor.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: Will I get a job at SECI after the internship?
answer: No, the internship does not guarantee employment at SECI.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: What should be included in the final report?
answer: A summary of your learning experience, suggestions for improvement, and any innovative ideas.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: Who assigns the Project Head/Mentor?
answer: The Heads of Departments assign Project Heads/Mentors to interns.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: What if I don't complete the internship?
answer: No completion certificate will be issued.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: Are international students eligible?
answer: Yes, students enrolled in recognized institutions abroad are eligible.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: What is the role of the HR Department?
answer: HR manages the internship program, including design, implementation, and modifications.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: How many interns can a department take at once?
answer: Up to three interns, or six in specific cases like engineering/M-Tech/CA/CMA students.

scheme_name: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Internship
question: Who is responsible for intern supervision?
answer: The assigned Project Head/Mentor.

scheme_name: Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes - "Educational Empowerment" Component
question: What is the maximum family income limit for a candidate to be eligible for benefits under this educational empowerment program?
answer: The total family income from all sources must be ₹2,50,000/- or less per annum. Income declaration should be obtained from Revenue Officer not below rank of Tehsildar for self-employed families and from employer for employed parents.

scheme_name: Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes - "Educational Empowerment" Component
question: Can I apply for coaching assistance if I am currently studying in the final year of my bachelor's degree program?
answer: Yes, students studying in final year of bachelor degree course are eligible for competitive exams requiring graduation qualification. You must be either completed or studying in final year at the time of receiving benefits.

scheme_name: Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes - "Educational Empowerment" Component
question: How many times can I avail the coaching benefits throughout my academic career under this educational support program?
answer: Benefits can be availed maximum twice in your lifetime, irrespective of number of chances you may be entitled for any particular competitive examination. You must submit affidavit confirming you have not exceeded this limit.

scheme_name: Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes - "Educational Empowerment" Component
question: What is the monthly stipend amount provided to students who attend coaching institutes outside their home location?
answer: Outstation students receive ₹3,000/- per month while local students get ₹1,500/- per month. Stipend is paid till duration of course or for one year, whichever is less, through Direct Benefit Transfer mode.

scheme_name: Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes - "Educational Empowerment" Component
question: Are there any additional financial benefits available for students with disabilities pursuing coaching under this educational support initiative?
answer: Students with disabilities having valid disability certificate showing 40% or more disability receive Special Allowance of ₹2,000/- per month. This covers reader allowance, escort allowance, helper allowance in addition to regular stipend.

scheme_name: Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes - "Educational Empowerment" Component
question: Which competitive examinations are covered under the free coaching component of this educational empowerment program for marginalized communities?
answer: Coverage includes Union Public Service Commission, Staff Selection Commission, Railway Recruitment Boards, State Public Service Commissions, Banking, Insurance, Public Sector Undertakings, Engineering (Indian Institute of Technology Joint Entrance Examination), Medical (National Eligibility cum Entrance Test), Management (Common Admission Test), Law (Common Law Admission Test), and various eligibility tests.

scheme_name: Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes - "Educational Empowerment" Component
question: When does the online application portal open for receiving applications from eligible candidates throughout the year?
answer: The portal remains open twice annually during July and January months for one month each. No offline applications are entertained and all incomplete applications will be summarily rejected.

scheme_name: Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes - "Educational Empowerment" Component
question: What happens if I cannot join my selected coaching institute within the specified time frame after receiving the first installment?
answer: If first installment is not paid to selected institute within 6 months, you must return the amount to Government immediately. Second installment will not be eligible and you must submit affidavit confirming this commitment.

scheme_name: Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes - "Educational Empowerment" Component
question: How is the selection process conducted when the number of eligible applications exceeds the available coaching slots?
answer: Selection is done in decreasing order of marks obtained in qualifying examinations. Priority is given to students who have qualified preliminary examination at least once for two-stage competitive exams.

scheme_name: Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes - "Educational Empowerment" Component
question: Can I receive coaching assistance for both preliminary and main stages of competitive examinations that are conducted in multiple phases?
answer: Yes, you are entitled for free coaching up to two times each for Preliminary and Main examinations. There is no restriction on number of coaching chances for Interview stage if selected.

scheme_name: Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes - "Educational Empowerment" Component
question: What type of income certificate is required if my parents are employed but have additional sources of income?
answer: Employed parents must obtain income certificate from their employer and additionally get consolidated certificate from Revenue Officer for any other additional sources of income beyond their employment.

scheme_name: Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes - "Educational Empowerment" Component
question: Is it possible to choose any coaching institute of my preference or are there restrictions on institute selection?
answer: You have liberty to choose coaching institute of your preference, but it must be empanelled under Free Coaching Scheme for Scheduled Caste and Other Backward Classes students as maintained by the Ministry.

scheme_name: Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes - "Educational Empowerment" Component
question: What is the maximum course fee limit covered under this educational assistance program for different competitive examination categories?
answer: Course fee varies by examination type - Civil Services ₹1,20,000/-, Staff Selection Commission/Railway Recruitment Boards ₹40,000/-, Banking/Insurance/Public Sector Undertakings/Common Law Admission Test ₹50,000/-, Joint Entrance Examination/National Eligibility cum Entrance Test ₹1,20,000/-, Common Admission Test ₹60,000/-, and others as specified in scheme annexure.

scheme_name: Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes - "Educational Empowerment" Component
question: Are students from De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes communities who belong to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes or Other Backward Classes also eligible?
answer: Yes, De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes students are eligible irrespective of whether they belong to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes or Other Backward Classes. However, they cannot avail similar benefits from other government schemes simultaneously.

scheme_name: ICSSR Senior Fellowship
question: What is the monetary benefit of the Senior Fellowship?
answer: The fellowship provides ₹45,000 per month and a contingency grant of ₹40,000 per annum.

scheme_name: ICSSR Senior Fellowship
question: How is the fellowship amount disbursed?
answer: The amount is disbursed in instalments through the affiliating institution upon submission of the required reports and bills.

scheme_name: ICSSR Senior Fellowship
question: What is the contingency grant meant for?
answer: It covers research assistance, books, stationery, fieldwork, and computer-related expenses.

scheme_name: ICSSR Senior Fellowship
question: Who can apply for the Senior Fellowship?
answer: Indian citizens aged between 45 and 70 years with a Ph.D. and a strong publication record in social sciences.

scheme_name: ICSSR Senior Fellowship
question: Can a candidate currently holding another fellowship apply?
answer: No, concurrent fellowships or research projects from other institutions are not allowed.

scheme_name: ICSSR Senior Fellowship
question: What are the educational qualifications required?
answer: - Ph.D. in any field of social sciences or allied disciplines is mandatory.

scheme_name: ICSSR Senior Fellowship
question: Is affiliation to an institution mandatory?
answer: Yes, applicants must be affiliated with a UGC-recognized or ICSSR-recognized institution.

scheme_name: ICSSR Senior Fellowship
question: What are the educational qualifications required?
answer: Ph.D. in any field of social sciences or allied disciplines is mandatory.

scheme_name: ICSSR Senior Fellowship
question: How can one apply for the Senior Fellowship?
answer: Applications must be submitted online through the ICSSR website during the open call period.

scheme_name: ICSSR Senior Fellowship
question: Can I submit multiple applications under different ICSSR schemes?
answer: Yes, but only one application under the Senior Fellowship scheme is allowed per call.

scheme_name: ICSSR Senior Fellowship
question: What documents are required at the time of application?
answer: Ph.D. certificate, age proof, list of publications, formatted research proposal, plagiarism report, institutional affiliation letter and other essential documents mentioned in the call.

scheme_name: ICSSR Senior Fellowship
question: What language can the research proposal be submitted in?
answer: Proposals can be submitted in either English or Hindi (using Unicode UTF-8 font).

scheme_name: ICSSR Senior Fellowship
question: Can I submit a hard copy of the application?
answer: Only if explicitly required in the call; otherwise, submission is online only.

scheme_name: SERB-Technology Translation Award
question: What is the aim of this scheme?
answer: SERB-TETRA aims to provide awards to competitively funded Core Research Grants (CRG) and similar projects, holding potential and promise for translation at TRL 5 or beyond.

scheme_name: SERB-Technology Translation Award
question: Who is eligible for TETRA?
answer: Principal Investigators/Inventors (PIs) of ongoing SERB Projects and all extramural projects completed in the last three years, where PI holds or has applied a patent, with an acknowledgement to SERB support.

scheme_name: SERB-Technology Translation Award
question: What is the nature of support provided under the scheme?
answer: Under the scheme, the award will entail an unstructured budget of up to ₹15 lakhs per year (without international travel), including overhead.

scheme_name: SERB-Technology Translation Award
question: How often the awards will be granted?
answer: Call for application would be made and awards would be granted once in a year.

scheme_name: SERB-Technology Translation Award
question: What is the duration of support?
answer: The funding will be provided normally for a period of two years.

scheme_name: SERB-Technology Translation Award
question: I am already implementing another SERB project. Am I eligible for TETRA?
answer: Yes. TETRA is an award of recognition and can be concurrently held with other SERB projects.

scheme_name: SERB-Technology Translation Award
question: I have applied for a number of patents. Can I submit multiple application?
answer: No. You can submit only one application at a time mentioning about the patent details having the best translational potential.

scheme_name: SERB-Technology Translation Award
question: I have forgotten to acknowledge SERB in many of my publications and patent, but I have large number of publications from the project. Will I be considered for the award?
answer: Only publications in which SERB grant is acknowledged will be considered as project output.

scheme_name: SERB-Technology Translation Award
question: Will all the PIs who holds or applied for a patent receive award under TETRA Scheme?
answer: No. The selection committee would choose the awardees based on the potential of translation for applied or granted patents.

scheme_name: SERB-Technology Translation Award
question: I have completed an CRG project 5 years ago and hold a patent with acknowledgement of SERB support. Will I be considered for the award?
answer: No. Only PIs of ongoing projects and all extramural projects completed in the previous three financial years will be considered.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: Who is eligible for SERB Power Fellowship?
answer: Those who are eligible for SERB Power Fellowship are: | Outstanding women researchers and innovators working in Indian academic institutions and R&D laboratories, holding Ph.D. degrees in any branch of science and engineering. | The nominee should be an active scientist with an excellent record of research performance as an independent investigator or innovator. | The nominee should be in regular service throughout the duration of the Fellowship.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: Is there any age limit for PI to be eligible for the award?
answer: PI should be within 35-55 years at the time of submission of proposal.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: I am already availing another Fellowship. Am I eligible for SERB Power Fellowship?
answer: No, you can avail only one fellowship at a time from government source.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: Is the Fellowship received under SERB Power Fellowship taxable?
answer: Yes, the Fellowship received under SERB Power Fellowship is taxable as per I.T. rules.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: What are the areas covered under SERB Power Fellowship?
answer: All Areas of Science (in the broadest terms) are covered by this Fellowship.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: What is the nature of support the SERB Power Fellow is entitled for?
answer: Nature of Support SERB Power Fellow is entitled for are: | Fellowship of ₹15,000/- per month in addition to regular income. | Research grant of ₹ 10 lakhs per annum. | Overhead for the institute.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: What is the duration of the SERB Power Fellowship?
answer: The SERB Power Fellowship duration is for 3 years only, without any possibility of extension.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: How many times a person can avail SERB Power Fellowship?
answer: A person can avail SERB Power Fellowship only once. Successful POWER Fellows cannot be nominated for a second time.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: When can a person apply for the SERB Power Fellowship? What is the last date of acceptance of the application?
answer: The nominations for the SERB Power Fellowship are accepted throughout the year through online portal only(www.serbonline.in) and there is no last date of acceptance of the nomination.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: Who can nominate for SERB Power Fellowship?
answer: Heads of Institutions or Fellows of National academies can send the nominations.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: How does a SERB Power Fellow get her subsequent Grant?
answer: The Grant for the subsequent years is released after receiving the two hard copies of Statement of Expenditure (SE) and Utilization Certificate (UC)in the prescribed format (available in the website). The SE and UC are to be submitted financial year wise i.e. from 01stApril to 31stMarch. For the first year it would be from the Date of Start (DOS) to 31stMarch and subsequently from 01stApril to 31stMarch.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: Can a fellow change the host institute during implementation of SERB Power Fellowship?
answer: A SERB Power fellow can change the host institute during implementation of SERB Power Fellowship. She has to forward NOCs from both the Institutes along with final financial papers indicating balance unspent grant from the old institute, undertaking certificate and appointment letter from the new Institute indicating the joining date and duration of the appointment.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: Is there a provision for extension of the fellowship?
answer: No, there is no provision for extension.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: What is the selection criteria of POWER Fellowship?
answer: Selection of POWER Fellows will be made twice a year by a specially constituted Search-cum-Selection Committee.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: Under which heads research grant can be used?
answer: Research Grant of ₹10 lakh per annum can be used for minor equipment, research personnel, consumables, contingencies, and domestic travel.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: What is the procedure to apply for a SERB Power Fellowship?
answer: In first step, an applicant will fill the application form on online portal. After submission of the form, a mail containing a link will be sent to the nominator by SERB. In second step, nominator will click on the link as provided in the mail to find the details of the application. After verification of the details he/she will forward the nomination to SERB.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: Can SERB POWER Fellowship research grant be used for international travel?
answer: No, SERB POWER Fellowship research grant can not be used for international travel.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: I am away from my institute/university for more than 6 weeks. Do I have to take permission from SERB?
answer: Yes, you have to take permission from SERB.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: I am a SERB-POWER fellow, and I am visiting abroad for more than 8 weeks. Can I avail the fellowship amount and research grant for my duration of visit?
answer: The PI will not be eligible to avail the fellowship amount or receive the research grant and overhead charges under SERB POWER Fellowship during the tenure of visit (if no student is drawing fellowship/salary/emoluments from the project).

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: I am travelling abroad to attend a conference. Can I use the research grant for the travel expense?
answer: The travel expenses related to foreign assignment will not be covered from the research grant under the SERB POWER Fellowship.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Fellowship
question: I am a SERB POWER fellow, and I am planning to visit abroad for a certain period as part of one collaboration work. Can I get an extension for that period after the completion of the project?
answer: The PI will not be allowed any kind of extension based on the claimed visit in the SERB POWER Fellowship.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Research Grants
question: What is the maximum amount of the grant the Board will fund?
answer: POWER Grants will empower women researchers by funding them under the following two categories: | Level I: The scale of funding up to 60 Lakhs for three years. | Level II: The scale of funding up to 30 Lakhs for three years.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Research Grants
question: What is level I & Level II in SERB- POWER research grant?
answer: Applicants from IITs, IISERs, IISC, NITs, Central Universities, and national Labs of Central government Institutions will be considered under level I category. Whereas applicants from state Universities/ Colleges and Private Academic Institutions should apply under Level II category.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Research Grants
question: Does the Board has any priority areas for funding under SERB- POWER research grant?
answer: No. The Board funds all the areas of Science and Engineering without discriminating between disciplines. The proposal will be funded if it has novelty and the investigator has the competence to execute the project.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Research Grants
question: I am currently executing an CRG project. I want to apply for another project under SERB- POWER research grant. Will I be funded another project?
answer: No. The Board funds only one project to an Investigator at a time, except in cases where calls for proposals are invited for specific areas/schemes/programs.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Research Grants
question: Are Co-Investigators allowed in SERB- POWER research grant project? If they are from different institutions, can the budget be provided separately to both the Principal Investigator and Co-Investigator(s)?
answer: Yes. Only female Co-Investigator(s) are allowed in SERB- POWER research grant project; provided the work proposed requires complementary expertise for its implementation. A separate budget can also be provided to the female Co-Investigator (s) even if they belong to different institutions.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Research Grants
question: Under which heads SERB-POWER research grant can be utilized?
answer: The SERB-POWER research grant is provided for Equipment, Research Personnel, Consumables, Travel and Contingency. Overheads is also being provided to the Implementing institution as per prevailing Norms of SERB.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Research Grants
question: What is the mode of selection for SERB-POWER research grant?
answer: The selection will be based on the recommendations of Program Advisory Committee (PAC) constituted by the Board. If required, the applicants may be called for discussion/presentation

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Research Grants
question: Whether a woman Scientist can hold both SERB-POWER Fellowship & SERB-POWER RESARCH Grant at the same time?
answer: No, Woman Scientists cannot hold SERB-POWER Fellowship & SERB-POWER research grant at the same time.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Research Grants
question: I am away from my institute/university for more than 6 weeks. Do I have to take permission from SERB?
answer: Yes, you have to take permission from SERB.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Research Grants
question: I am a Co-PI in an ongoing CRG project. Can I apply for POWER-GRANT?
answer: Yes, you can apply for POWER-GRANT.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Research Grants
question: I have an ongoing EMEQ/IRPHA/ MATRIX project. Can I apply for POWER-GRANT?
answer: Yes, you can apply for POWER-GRANT.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Research Grants
question: I have an ongoing CRG/SRG/SURE/SUPRA project. Can I apply for POWER-GRANT?
answer: No, you can not apply for POWER-GRANT.

scheme_name: SERB - POWER Research Grants
question: How to apply for SERB POWER Research Grants?
answer: The Call for applications will be notified through the website "https://www.serbonline.in" and "https://serb.gov.in/". The application form along with a proper research proposal highlighting the research work to be undertaken should be submitted online through the website "https://www.serbonline.in/".

scheme_name: SERB Research Scientist Scheme
question: What is the "SERB Research Scientist Scheme"?
answer: SERB Board has launched a new 'SERB Research Scientist (SRS) Scheme' for the awardees of INSPIRE Faculty and Ramanujan Fellowships, who fail to secure regular positions after completion of the regular tenure of five years in the respective schemes. The scheme provides an opportunity for them to continue their research activities and also to explore regular positions during the intervening period.

scheme_name: SERB Research Scientist Scheme
question: What is the objective of the Scheme?
answer: The objective of the scheme is to identify and provide a platform for sustainment of the research career of INSPIRE Faculty and Ramanujan Fellows for an additional period of two years after completion of the regular tenure of five years in the respective schemes.

scheme_name: SERB Research Scientist Scheme
question: Which is the implementing agency of this scheme?
answer: Science and Engineering Research Board, Government of India

scheme_name: SERB Research Scientist Scheme
question: What are the eligibility criteria for applying/availing the Fellowship?
answer: The scheme is open only to INSPIRE Faculty and Ramanujan Fellows. | The applicant should have completed or nearing completion of the tenure of INSPIRE Faculty of DST or Ramanujan Fellowship of SERB. | The upper age limit for INSPIRE Faculty/Ramanujan Fellows is 40 years at the time of submission of application.

scheme_name: SERB Research Scientist Scheme
question: What are the areas covered under this Fellowship?
answer: Chemical Sciences, Earth & Atmospheric Sciences, Engineering Sciences, Life Sciences, Mathematical Sciences, Physical Sciences

scheme_name: SERB Research Scientist Scheme
question: What is the nature of support for the Fellow?
answer: Under this scheme, Emolument: Consolidated amount of ₹1,20,000/- per month Research Grant ₹7,00,000/- per annum Overheads ₹1,00,000/- per annum.

scheme_name: SERB Research Scientist Scheme
question: Can a fellow (SERB Research Scientist) be eligible to receive any other research project/fellowship?
answer: No, the SERB Research Scientists are not eligible to receive any other research project/fellowship from any Government or Non-Governmental source during the tenure of the Scheme.

scheme_name: SERB Research Scientist Scheme
question: How many times can a fellow avail this fellowship?
answer: Only once, the eligible fellow can avail this fellowship in his/her career.

scheme_name: SERB Research Scientist Scheme
question: What is the duration of this fellowship?
answer: The scheme is tenable for a period of 2 years, extendable to one more year, subject to performance evaluation. Under any circumstances, the support is not extendable beyond three years.

scheme_name: SERB Research Scientist Scheme
question: When can an applicant apply for the Fellowship? What is the last date of acceptance of the application?
answer: The application for SRS will be opened throughout the year. Application shall be submitted within six months before or after completion of regular tenure of the schemes. However, previous batches may be allowed to apply now at the opening of this new scheme.

scheme_name: SERB Research Scientist Scheme
question: How can an application submit under the scheme?
answer: The candidates should submit 3 copies of the application printed on both sides of A4 size paper and send to: | Dr. Harish Kumar, Scientist F | Science and Engineering Research Board | 3rd & 4th floor, Block -II, Technology Bhawan, | New Mehrauli Road, New Delhi- 110016, INDIA

scheme_name: SERB Research Scientist Scheme
question: How will the applications be evaluated?
answer: The application will be evaluated by a Selection Committee constituted for the purpose. The Committee may consider the performance evaluation by the relevant subject expert committee during the tenure of the INSPIRE Faculty/Ramanujan Fellowship Scheme. If required, the applicants may be called for personal interviews.

scheme_name: Scheme of Financial Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTM/ICI/NCHMCT/PSUs
question: If a State Government intends to upgrade an existing Food Craft Institute into a State Institute of Hotel Management, what mandatory administrative steps must be taken regarding the existing society structure?
answer: The State Government must dissolve the original Food Craft Institute Society and then form and register a new Society specifically in the name of the State Institute of Hotel Management under the Societies Registration Act 1860.

scheme_name: Scheme of Financial Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTM/ICI/NCHMCT/PSUs
question: What is the minimum acceptable area of developed land, free from all encumbrances, that a State Government must transfer for setting up a new Institute of Hotel Management?
answer: The State Government or Union Territory Administration must transfer a piece of developed land, free from all encumbrances, measuring not less than 5 (five) acres.

scheme_name: Scheme of Financial Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTM/ICI/NCHMCT/PSUs
question: What necessary documentation concerning property ownership must accompany the initial proposal when seeking assistance to set up a new Institute of Hotel Management?
answer: The proposal must be accompanied by the land transfer documents showing that the developed land has been transferred specifically into the name of the Institute of Hotel Management Society.

scheme_name: Scheme of Financial Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTM/ICI/NCHMCT/PSUs
question: If difficulties arise in officially transferring the required land to the Society, what must the applicant government provide to the Central Government to proceed with the proposal?
answer: The reasons explaining the difficulties in transferring the land to the Society must be formally recorded in writing and subsequently found acceptable by the Central Government.

scheme_name: Scheme of Financial Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTM/ICI/NCHMCT/PSUs
question: What specific legal requirements must a governmental body or administration meet to qualify its society for financial assistance under these guidelines?
answer: The applicant must be a Society formed by the Central Government, State Government, or Union Territory Administration, which is registered under the Societies Registration Act 1860.

scheme_name: Scheme of Financial Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTM/ICI/NCHMCT/PSUs
question: When applying for the establishment of a new Food Craft Institute by a State Government or Union Territory Administration, what is the mandatory minimum acreage requirement for the developed land?
answer: The State Government or Union Territory Administration must transfer a piece of developed land, free from all encumbrances, measuring not less than 3 (three) acres to the Food Craft Institute Society.

scheme_name: Scheme of Financial Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTM/ICI/NCHMCT/PSUs
question: If a Central Institute of Hotel Management wishes to construct an Applied Training Centre, what is the minimum land prerequisite for the proposal to be considered for funding?
answer: The proposal will only be considered if the Institute already has 2 (two) acres of surplus land available, or if the State Government provides the additional land required for the purpose.

scheme_name: Scheme of Financial Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTM/ICI/NCHMCT/PSUs
question: Are there special considerations or preconditions for receiving financial assistance if a State Institute of Hotel Management is intended to be housed within a pre-existing governmental building?
answer: Yes, financial assistance is admissible provided the existing building is certified as suitable for housing the Institute of Hotel Management by the National Council for Hotel Management & Catering Technology.

scheme_name: Scheme of Financial Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTM/ICI/NCHMCT/PSUs
question: What is the minimum required size for developed land when setting up a new Food Craft Institute, if the proposed location is within the notified hilly areas or metropolitan Urban Agglomerations?
answer: For a Food Craft Institute set up in hilly areas or the six classified large Urban Agglomeration cities, a developed piece of land measuring not less than 1 (one) acre would be sufficient.

scheme_name: Scheme of Financial Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTM/ICI/NCHMCT/PSUs
question: When proposing a new Centre for institutions like the Indian Culinary Institute or National Council for Hotel Management, what minimum land size must the State Government commit to providing?
answer: The State Government or Union Territory Administration concerned must transfer a piece of developed land, free from all encumbrances, measuring not less than 5 (five) acres.

scheme_name: Scheme of Financial Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTM/ICI/NCHMCT/PSUs
question: What specific administrative action related to the proposed society must be finalized before the Central Government can even begin considering financial assistance for a new Institute of Hotel Management?
answer: Central Financial Assistance will only be considered after the Institute of Hotel Management Society has been officially registered under the Societies Registration Act 1860 by the relevant government body.

scheme_name: Scheme of Financial Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTM/ICI/NCHMCT/PSUs
question: If the transfer of land directly into the Institute of Hotel Management Society's name is administratively challenging or legally restricted, what alternative arrangement is acceptable?
answer: The land must be clearly demarcated for the Institute of Hotel Management and must be in the possession of the concerned State Government or Union Territory Administration, specifically under the name of the Tourism Department.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: What is the objective of the scheme?
answer: The objective of the scheme is to promote, protect and preserve the cultural heritage of the Himalayan region spreading in UT of Jammu & Kashmir, UT of Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttrakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh through research, documentation, dissemination, etc.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: Which ministry has started the scheme?
answer: Ministry of Culture, Government of India

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: Is this scheme centrally sponsored?
answer: Yes, this scheme is centrally sponsored.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: How much financial assistance will be provided under the scheme?
answer: The financial assistance is given up to a maximum of ₹10.00 lakhs to any single organization.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: How much amount of grant shall be released by the central government under the scheme?
answer: The maximum grant admissible to an organization would be 75% of the total expenditure to be incurred on any item subject to the maximum ceiling fixed. The remaining 25% expenditure or more should be met by the State Govt./U.T. Administration failing which the grantee organization could contribute the amount from their own resources.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: How much funding will be given to Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim by the central government under the scheme?
answer: In the case of Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim, funding will be shared between the Government of India and the organization in the ratio of 90:10 respectively.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: Which type of organization is eligible to apply under the scheme?
answer: The voluntary organizations which are registered as a society under the Societies Registration Act 1860 or as a public trust under the Indian Trust Act, 1882, and shall have been functioning for a period of three years are eligible to apply under the scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: Are the Colleges and Universities eligible to apply?
answer: Yes, Colleges and Universities are also eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: Which organization will be given preference for providing funds?
answer: Organizations that are doing good work in the field and have resources for meeting matching funds will be given preference.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: What will be the nature of grants?
answer: The grants will be ad-hoc and of non-recurring nature.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: How shall the grant be given to the organizations?
answer: The grant shall be given based on the appraisal of applications and recommendations by the Expert Advisory Committee and thereafter administrative approval and financial concurrence of competent authorities in the Ministry of Culture.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: How will the payment be made to the organizations?
answer: All payments will be made through electronic transfers.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: What is the Special Provision under the scheme?
answer: The Expert Advisory Committee (EAC) on the scheme is empowered to recommend or reject any proposal received without or with the recommendation of State Government/U.T. administration/ Local Administration and also to recommend the amount beyond the maximum limit but not exceeding ₹30.00 lacs from this scheme, in respect of any proposal which is of outstanding merit for which the EAC feels that the maximum limit would not be sufficient for undertaking the said project, with the approval of Minister (Culture) and concurrence of AS & FA, Ministry of Culture.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: How shall the grant be paid?
answer: The Grants will be paid in two equal installments, the first being normally released with the approval of the project. The second installment will be released on completion of the project and on receipt of duly audited statement of accounts showing the utilization of the entire amount of grant plus the share of the grantee/concerned State/U.T. Government and other documents. The release of the balance of the grant will be decided on the basis of the actual expenditure incurred on the project subject to the maximum limit.

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: Where can an organization find the application form?
answer: The application form can be downloaded from the official website of the Ministry of Culture. https://indiaculture.gov.in/sites/default/files/Schemes/FormHimHeritage.pdf

scheme_name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
question: How can an organization apply under the scheme ?
answer: The application in the prescribed format complete in all respect, duly spiral bound and continuously page numbered, along with a check-list duly recommended should be sent to the Section Officer, BTI Section, Ministry of Culture, 2nd Floor, Puratatav Bhawan, D Block, GPO Complex, INA, New Delhi-110023.

scheme_name: Scheme For Financial Assistance For Veteran Artists
question: What is the "Scheme for Financial Assistance for Veteran Artists"?
answer: The Scheme is meant for improving the financial and socio-economic status of the old artists and scholars who have contributed significantly in their specialized fields of arts, letters, etc. in their active age or are still contributing in the field of arts, letters, etc. but due to old age, they have to lead a miserable life or are in penury condition.

scheme_name: Scheme For Financial Assistance For Veteran Artists
question: Is it a Centrally Sponsored Scheme?
answer: Yes, it is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme For Financial Assistance For Veteran Artists
question: Which ministry has launched this scheme?
answer: Ministry of Culture, Government of India

scheme_name: Scheme For Financial Assistance For Veteran Artists
question: Who is eligible to get the benefits under the scheme?
answer: A person or traditional scholars who have made significant contributions in the field of arts, letters, etc. are eligible to apply under the scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme For Financial Assistance For Veteran Artists
question: What is the income criterion to apply under the scheme?
answer: The personal income of the applicant (including the income of the spouse) must not exceed ₹48,000/- per annum.

scheme_name: Scheme For Financial Assistance For Veteran Artists
question: Will the artist's pension assistance be included in his/her annual income?
answer: No, artist's pension assistance will be excluded which is getting from the Government.

scheme_name: Scheme For Financial Assistance For Veteran Artists
question: What should be the age criterion to apply under the scheme?
answer: The applicant should not be less than 60 (sixty) years of age (This does not apply in the case of a spouse).

scheme_name: Scheme For Financial Assistance For Veteran Artists
question: Will an applicant be eligible to apply if he/she is getting financial assistance under other Schemes of the Ministry?
answer: No, the applicant artist should not be getting financial assistance under other Schemes of the Ministry viz. Repertory Grant etc.

scheme_name: Scheme For Financial Assistance For Veteran Artists
question: What is the benefit of the scheme?
answer: Under the scheme, a total allowance of ₹6000/- per month will be given to an eligible beneficiary.

scheme_name: Scheme For Financial Assistance For Veteran Artists

question: Who Is A Good Samaritan?
answer: A Good Samaritan is a person who, in good faith, without expectation of payment or reward and without any duty of care or special relationship, voluntarily comes forward to administer immediate assistance or emergency care to a person injured in an accident, or crash, or emergency medical condition, or emergency situation.

scheme_name: Good Samaritan Scheme
question: What Is Good Samaritan Law?
answer: The Good Samaritan Law allows a person, without expectation of payment or reward and without any duty of care or special relationship, voluntarily come forward to administer immediate assistance or emergency care to a person injured in an accident, or crash, or emergency medical condition. Good Samaritan Law protects Good Samaritans from harassment on the actions being taken by them to save the life of the road accident victims.

scheme_name: Good Samaritan Scheme
question: Why The Need For Good Samaritan Law?
answer: India is an unfortunate victim of a large number of road crash fatalities. Three out of four people in the country are hesitant to help injured accident victims on roads due to fear of police harassment, detention at hospitals, and prolonged legal formalities. Even if someone wants to help, these factors stop them from doing so.

scheme_name: Good Samaritan Scheme
question: How Did India Get A Good Samaritan Law?
answer: In the last ten years, road crashes have killed over 13 lakh people in India. According to the Law Commission of India, 50% of these victims died of preventable injuries and could have been saved if they had received care on time. The role of the bystander is critical in providing emergency care to the victim. Yet, in India, bystanders have been hesitant to help the injured for fear of legal repercussions and procedural hassles. | In 2012, a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) was filed in the Supreme Court of India, requesting the Hon'ble court to safeguard Good Samaritans who come forward to help the injured.

scheme_name: Good Samaritan Scheme
