scheme_name: Good Samaritan Scheme
question: How many National Level Awards are granted each year For The Most Worthy Good Samaritans?
answer: There will be 10 National Level Awards for the most worthy Good Samaritans (who will be selected from all those who have been awarded during the whole year) and they would be given an Award of ₹ 1,00,000/- each.

scheme_name: Good Samaritan Scheme
question: How many times can a Good Samaritan be awarded?
answer: An individual Good Samaritan can be awarded a maximum of 5 times a year.

scheme_name: Good Samaritan Scheme
question: Will the Good Samaritan receive a "Certification of Appreciation"?
answer: Yes, every cash award would be accompanied by a "Certification of Appreciation".

scheme_name: Good Samaritan Scheme
question: What if More Than One Good Samaritan Saves The Life Of More Than One Victim?
answer: If more than one Good Samaritan saves the life of more than one victim of a fatal accident involving a motor vehicle, the amount of award will be ₹ 5000/- per victim saved subject to a maximum of ₹ 5000/-per Good Samaritan.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools
question: What type of organizations are eligible to receive grant-in-aid for running schools under this educational assistance program?
answer: The organization must be a reputed school chain, Corporate Social Responsibility foundation, or reputed organization running good quality schools recognized by the State Government and affiliated to State or Central Boards. Additionally, the organization must be registered on the Non-Governmental Organization Darpan portal of National Institution for Transforming India Aayog.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools
question: How much financial assistance can our organization receive per Scheduled Caste student annually for residential school operations?
answer: For primary level residential schools, organizations receive ₹44,000/- per Scheduled Caste student per year, while for secondary level residential schools, the assistance is ₹55,000/- per Scheduled Caste student per year.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools
question: What happens if the attendance of Scheduled Caste students in our school falls below 75% during inspection?
answer: If attendance is between 50% to less than 75%, you will receive 75% of the grant amount. If attendance is between 25% to less than 50%, only 50% grant will be provided. If attendance falls below 25% without valid grounds, no grant-in-aid will be released.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools
question: Are there any additional non-recurring grants available for infrastructure development and how frequently can we apply for them?
answer: Yes, non-recurring grants are available every 5 years for infrastructure items. For example, a secondary residential school accommodating 100 students can receive ₹3,85,000/- for fixed items plus ₹900/- per student for items like furniture, bedding material, laboratory equipment, and Closed Circuit Television installation.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools
question: What minimum academic performance standards must our school maintain to continue receiving grant-in-aid under this program?
answer: Your school must maintain Class 10th and Class 12th pass percentage that is not less than the average Board result of the respective State or Central Board. Teachers must also be qualified graduates with Bachelor of Education qualification for high schools.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools
question: Do we need to maintain separate financial accounts for the grants received and what are the auditing requirements?
answer: Yes, you must maintain separate accounts for grants received under this program, which shall always be open for inspection by Government officers or Comptroller and Auditor General. You must also submit audited statement of accounts with utilization certificate after each financial year closure.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools
question: What infrastructure facilities are mandatory for residential schools to qualify for grant-in-aid and maintain funding eligibility?
answer: Essential infrastructure includes one classroom per class, adequate furniture for all students, one decent cot and bed per child, proper lighting and fans, hygienic toilets at ratio of 1:10 children, hygienic kitchen and dining facilities, clean drinking water, medical facilities with regular doctor visits, and Closed Circuit Television installation with live streaming capability.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools
question: How many installments will our organization receive annually and what is the process for fund release?
answer: Grants are released in three installments per year after submission of complete proposal and Programme Management Unit inspection report. Funds are transferred electronically directly to your organization's bank account through the e-Anudaan portal.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools
question: What are the consequences if our organization provides false information or fails to comply with the terms and conditions?
answer: If false information is provided or unethical practices are found, your organization will be blacklisted and this information will be communicated to National Institution for Transforming India Aayog for removal from Non-Governmental Organization Darpan portal. You may also be required to refund grants with 12% interest.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools
question: Can organizations charging any fees from beneficiary students still qualify for grant-in-aid under this educational support program?
answer: No capitation fees or donations can be charged from beneficiaries. If any fee is collected, it must be declared in accounts furnished to the Ministry and the corresponding amount will be deducted from the admissible grant-in-aid amount.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools
question: What is the deadline for submitting applications on the e-Anudaan portal and when does the application window open?
answer: The e-Anudaan portal opens tentatively on 1st April every year for entry of renewal students and remains open till 30th June for entry of fresh students. All required documents and student details must be submitted within this timeframe.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools
question: Are there any specific teacher qualification requirements and minimum staffing norms that must be maintained throughout the program duration?
answer: Teachers in high schools must be at least graduates in their respective fields with Bachelor of Education qualification. The minimum number of teachers must not be less than 6 in a school and not less than 2 in a hostel, with honorariums paid as per minimum district rates.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
question: What is the maximum annual family income limit for students applying under this residential education program for Scheduled Caste students?
answer: The parental income shall not exceed ₹2,50,000/- per year for eligibility under this scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
question: Which classes can students apply for admission and what are the academic prerequisites for each level in this quality education initiative?
answer: Students can apply for admission in Class 9th after passing Class 8th in the immediately preceding academic year, or for Class 11th after passing Class 10th in the immediately preceding academic year.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
question: How much financial assistance is provided annually for each class under this scholarship program for residential schooling?
answer: The scholarship amounts are Class 9th: ₹1,00,000/-, Class 10th: ₹1,10,000/-, Class 11th: ₹1,25,000/-, and Class 12th: ₹1,35,000/- per student per annum covering school fee and hostel fee.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
question: What is the selection process and testing mechanism for students seeking admission to these premier private residential institutions?
answer: Students must qualify through the National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA conducted by National Testing Agency, followed by merit-based selection and web counselling for school choice.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
question: How many seats are allocated annually across the country for fresh admissions under this educational opportunity program?
answer: The tentative allocation provides 1500 seats in Class 9th and 1500 seats in Class 11th each year from 2023-24 to 2025-26, totaling 3000 fresh admissions annually.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
question: Can students already receiving benefits under other scholarship schemes of the department apply for this residential education program?
answer: Students applying under this scheme should not be covered under Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
question: What type of schools are recognized and selected under this initiative for providing quality education to Scheduled Caste students?
answer: The best performing private residential schools are selected based on Central Board of Secondary Education database, schools recommended by District Authorities, and other eligible private residential schools affiliated to State or Central Boards.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
question: What additional academic support is provided to help students adapt to the new learning environment in these institutions?
answer: A bridge course may be conducted outside school hours covering academic topics and personality development, with funding up to 10% of annual fee for up to 3 months duration.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
question: How long will students continue to receive financial support once they are admitted under this residential education scheme?
answer: Students admitted in Class 9 or 11 shall automatically be funded for the next classes till they complete 12th class, subject to passing the exams of the previous class.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
question: What are the minimum operational requirements and infrastructure standards that participating schools must maintain under this program?
answer: Schools should have existed for at least 5 years, maintain more than 75% pass percentage in Class 10 and 12 for the last 3 years, and have adequate infrastructure for admitting at least 10 additional Scheduled Caste students.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
question: Within what timeframe are the scholarship funds transferred directly to the selected schools after student admission confirmation?
answer: The fee covering school fee and hostel fee would be released directly to schools by the Ministry within 30 days from the date of confirmation of admission on the Information Technology portal.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
question: What happens if a student decides to leave the school after admission and fee payment has been made to the institution?
answer: If any student leaves after getting admitted and payment of fee to the school, it should be brought to notice of Central Government immediately and fees paid should be refunded to the Consolidated Fund of India.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
question: Are there any charges or fees that students need to pay directly to the schools under this residential education program?
answer: No fee or any other charges will be charged from the beneficiary by the schools participating in this scheme as all costs are covered by the scholarship amount.

scheme_name: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
question: What counselling and support mechanisms are available for students to help them settle in their new residential school environment?
answer: Schools designate one of the teachers as counsellor who would resolve difficulties faced by students and provide necessary assistance to settle down in the new environment.

scheme_name: Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)  (OBC & Others)
question: What is the objective of the scheme?
answer: The objective of the National Fellowship for Other Backward Classes is to provide financial assistance in the form of fellowship to Other Backward Classes students for pursuing quality higher education and advanced research leading to M.Phil. and Ph.D. degrees, thereby promoting their educational empowerment through support for regular and full-time research programmes in recognised institutions.

scheme_name: Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)  (OBC & Others)
question: Which authority implements the scheme?
answer: The scheme is implemented by the University Grants Commission.

scheme_name: Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)  (OBC & Others)
question: Who can apply for this fellowship?
answer: Candidates belonging to the Other Backward Classes category who have qualified UGC-NET JRF or CSIR-UGC NET-JRF and are enrolled in a regular M.Phil. or PhD programme.

scheme_name: Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)  (OBC & Others)
question: How many fellowships are available under the scheme?
answer: A total of 1,000 Junior Research Fellowships are awarded every year.

scheme_name: Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)  (OBC & Others)
question: How are the fellowship slots distributed?
answer: Out of 1,000 slots, 750 are allocated for UGC-NET JRF subjects and 250 for CSIR-UGC NET-JRF Science streams.

scheme_name: Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)  (OBC & Others)
question: Is there any reservation for persons with disabilities?
answer: Yes, 5% of the total fellowship slots are reserved for students with disabilities.

scheme_name: Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)  (OBC & Others)
question: What is the duration of the fellowship?
answer: The fellowship is awarded for up to 5 years, including 2 years as Junior Research Fellow and up to 3 years as Senior Research Fellow, subject to satisfactory progress.

scheme_name: Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)  (OBC & Others)
question: What is the fellowship amount?
answer: The fellowship amount is ₹31,000/- per month for Junior Research Fellow and ₹35,000/- per month for Senior Research Fellow, as per University Grants Commission norms.

scheme_name: Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)  (OBC & Others)
question: Are fellows entitled to House Rent Allowance?
answer: Yes, House Rent Allowance is payable as per University Grants Commission norms if hostel accommodation is not provided.

scheme_name: Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)  (OBC & Others)
question: Can a fellow receive another scholarship or fellowship simultaneously?
answer: No, a fellow is not permitted to receive any other fellowship or similar financial benefit from any source during the tenure.

scheme_name: Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)  (OBC & Others)
question: How is the fellowship amount paid?
answer: The fellowship amount is disbursed through Direct Benefit Transfer into the beneficiary's bank account after monthly confirmation by the host institution.

scheme_name: Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)  (OBC & Others)
question: Can employed candidates apply for this fellowship?
answer: No, employees of any University, Educational Institution, or Central, State, or Union Territory Government are not eligible, even if on study leave or Extraordinary Leave.

scheme_name: Study in India Programme
question: Who can apply under the programme?
answer: Foreign nationals seeking admission to Indian higher education institutions are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Study in India Programme
question: Is registration mandatory on the portal?
answer: Yes, registration on the Study in India portal is mandatory for admission and visa processing.

scheme_name: Study in India Programme
question: What is a Study in India Student ID?
answer: It is a unique identification number generated during registration and required for admission and visa issuance.

scheme_name: Study in India Programme
question: Are scholarships provided under the programme?
answer: No scholarships are provided under the programme; however, institutes may offer fee waivers as per their policies.

scheme_name: Study in India Programme
question: How many institutions are part of the programme?
answer: More than 600 partner institutions are associated with the Study in India Programme.

scheme_name: Study in India Programme
question: How many courses are available?
answer: Over 8,000 courses across diverse academic disciplines are available under the programme.

scheme_name: Study in India Programme
question: Can a student apply to multiple institutions?
answer: Yes, students can apply to multiple institutions simultaneously through the portal.

scheme_name: Study in India Programme
question: Is the admission process transparent?
answer: Yes, the fully online and system-driven process ensures transparency with no human intervention.

scheme_name: Study in India Programme
question: Does the programme help with visas?
answer: Yes, the programme provides assistance for visa and immigration processes.

scheme_name: Study in India Programme
question: Are Indian nationals eligible?
answer: No, Indian nationals are not eligible under the Study in India Programme.

scheme_name: Study in India Programme
question: Is support available after admission?
answer: Yes, post-admission support and alumni engagement are provided.

scheme_name: Study in India Programme
question: How are updates communicated to students?
answer: Updates are communicated through the website, email, social media platforms, WhatsApp, and notifications.

scheme_name: Study in India Programme
question: Where can students get help or guidance?
answer: Students can seek assistance through the 24×7 contact center, official helpdesk email, and social media channels.

scheme_name: SAHAKAR MITRA: NCDC’s Scheme on Internship Programme
question: What is 'SAHAKAR MITRA Scheme on Internship Programme (SIP)'?
answer: Under the scheme, NCDC will provide short-term (not exceeding four months) opportunities to young professionals to acquire learning experience by applying skills and knowledge in an organizational context to facilitate professional development.

scheme_name: SAHAKAR MITRA: NCDC’s Scheme on Internship Programme
question: What is the objective of the SIP?
answer: The objective of the scheme is to provide work-related learning experience in the core and special fields of functioning of NCDC to students of professional courses and to project contribution and achievements of NCDC in the development of cooperatives.

scheme_name: SAHAKAR MITRA: NCDC’s Scheme on Internship Programme
question: What is the aim of the scheme?
answer: The Scheme aims at providing an opportunity for professional graduates to get experience in areas of functioning of NCDC and related aspects of cooperatives.

scheme_name: SAHAKAR MITRA: NCDC’s Scheme on Internship Programme
question: When was the SIP introduced, and why?
answer: The SIP was introduced in the year 2012-13 to facilitate work-related learning experiences for students and contribute to the development of cooperatives.

scheme_name: SAHAKAR MITRA: NCDC’s Scheme on Internship Programme
question: How has the SIP evolved over the years?
answer: Originally launched for general professional courses, the scheme expanded to include students in the 2nd year of MBA Agri-Business from State Agricultural Universities in states where NCDC's Regional Offices are located.

scheme_name: SAHAKAR MITRA: NCDC’s Scheme on Internship Programme
question: What is the maximum duration of the internship period at NCDC?
answer: The internship period at NCDC shall not exceed four months for a person.

scheme_name: SAHAKAR MITRA: NCDC’s Scheme on Internship Programme
question: Is the financial support meant to cover only out-of-pocket expenses?
answer: Yes, the consolidated monthly amount of ₹10,000/- is intended to partly cover the interns' out-of-pocket expenses during the four-month SIP.

scheme_name: SAHAKAR MITRA: NCDC’s Scheme on Internship Programme
question: What is the total financial support offered by NCDC during the SIP?
answer: The total financial support provided by NCDC to interns during the SIP is ₹45,000/-, inclusive of the consolidated monthly amount and expenses related to report preparation.

scheme_name: SAHAKAR MITRA: NCDC’s Scheme on Internship Programme
question: Where will the interns be placed?
answer: Interns will be placed at the Head Office (HO), LINAC, or Regional Offices (ROs) based on their preferences and the requirements of NCDC.

scheme_name: SAHAKAR MITRA: NCDC’s Scheme on Internship Programme
question: Can a person participate in the internship program more than once?
answer: No, a person cannot be taken as an intern more than once as per the program guidelines.

scheme_name: SAHAKAR MITRA: NCDC’s Scheme on Internship Programme
question: How can I apply for Sahakar Mitra?
answer: Visit the official Portal NCDC: Sahakar Mitra (https://sip.ncdc.in/Default.aspx)

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship for Post-Graduate/Research Students
question: What Are The Objectives Of The "Scheme Of Internship For Post-Graduate/Research Students By MoSPI"?
answer: Aim, Objectives & Scope | To facilitate the students pursuing post-graduate/research in statistics to study and get familiarized with the prevailing system of Official Statistics in the Country. | To familiarize the interested and willing post-graduate/research students with the Official Statistical System of the Country, with specific reference to data collection, processing & analysis, publication and dissemination needs. | To create awareness amongst the students of Statistics/ Mathematical Statistics/ OperationsResearch/ Economics/ Demography or any of the applied fields of Statistics about the Indian Statistical Service and Subordinate Statistical Service. | To sensitize the students of Statistics/ Mathematical Statistics/ Operational Research/ Economics/ Demography or any of the applied fields of Statistics about choosing their career in the field of Statistics.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship for Post-Graduate/Research Students
question: How Many Total Slots Are There In This Internship Scheme?
answer: The total available number of internships during 2023-24 would be 193.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship for Post-Graduate/Research Students
question: Will The Amount Of The Token Stipend Be Paid As A Lump Sum Or In Installments?
answer: A token stipend of ₹10,000/- (consolidated) @ ₹5,000/- per month would be paid to the selected intern on successful completion of his /her internship, at the end of the internship period.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship for Post-Graduate/Research Students
question: Will The Amount Of The Stipend Be Paid In Cash?
answer: The stipend to interns would be transferred directly into their bank account only through electronic mode of funds transfer/ Aadhaar Payments Bridge (APB)/ Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AEPS) by selection points.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship for Post-Graduate/Research Students
question: Will The Certificate Of Completion Be Paid To All The Interns?
answer: The Certificate will be issued to the successful interns, upon completion of the internship, by the respective offices where they are attached.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship for Post-Graduate/Research Students
question: Will MoSPI Pay Travelling Allowance Or Daily Allowance To The Interns?
answer: No Travelling Allowance or Daily Allowance etc. will be paid by the Ministry for joining the place of internship allotted to them or after the completion of the internship.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship for Post-Graduate/Research Students
question: Are There Any Arrangements For Lodging And Boarding Of The Interns?
answer: The selected candidates have to make their own arrangements for their lodging, boarding and transport etc.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship for Post-Graduate/Research Students
question: Does This Internship Program Include Field Visits? If Yes, What Shall Be Its Duration?
answer: The students opting for NSSO (FOD) Zonal/Regional Offices will be paid an additional amount of ₹250/- per day, so as to enable them to undertake Field Visits if required, which should not exceed a maximum of 10 days in the entire period of 2 months of internship.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship for Post-Graduate/Research Students
question: What Additional Facilities Will Be Provided To The Interns?
answer: To facilitate the interns in the pursuit of their assignment, internship offices/centers would try their best to provide a minimum logistics support i.e. office space, with intercom facility and computer, with internet facility etc. However, interns may have to bring their own laptops if the situation demands so.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship for Post-Graduate/Research Students
question: Will The Interns Have Access To The Office Library?
answer: For study material, the intern will have access to the literature available in the Library/Office and can interact with the concerned Division(s)/Officer through the guide, with whom they would be attached. Internship Centers will designate a guide/nodal officer for each intern allocated to them.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship for Post-Graduate/Research Students
question: What Should Be The Educational Stream Of The Intern?
answer: The applicant should be pursuing his/her post-graduation/research from a recognized College/ University/ Research institute in Statistics/ Mathematical Statistics/ Operational Research/ Economics/ Demography or any of the applied fields of Statistics.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship for Post-Graduate/Research Students
question: What Types Of Outputs Are Expected From The Interns?
answer: Each intern/student shall be required to submit a report/paper (along with a soft copy) at the end of the assignment, including inter-alia, his/her observations and suggestions, if any, regarding any possible improvement in the system.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: How Many Student Interns Will Be Engaged By The CAG Of India?
answer: The number of student interns will depend on the actual requirement from time to time.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: What Is The Duration Of The Internship For A Student Intern?
answer: The duration of the internship will be 2-3 months.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: Who Is Eligible To Apply For The Internship?
answer: Candidates pursuing undergraduate/postgraduate/research programs in any discipline from recognized and reputed institutions, with a stellar academic record, and not exceeding 25 years of age, are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: What Are The Preferred Attributes For Applicants?
answer: Applicants with skills in Information Technology (IT) and Information Communication Technology (ICT), along with good communication and interpersonal skills, are preferred.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: Is There A Secrecy And Non-Disclosure Agreement Required Before Starting The Internship?
answer: Yes, student interns are required to sign a secrecy and non-disclosure agreement before reporting for the internship.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: Will Travel Allowances Or Other Perks Be Provided To Student Interns?
answer: No, TA/DA or other perks and facilities such as accommodation, transportation, medical reimbursement, etc., will not be provided.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: What Is The Remuneration For Student Interns?
answer: Student interns will receive a token remuneration of ₹10,000 (all inclusive) per month, payable upon satisfactory completion of their internship and submission of their report/paper.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: When Will The Payment Be Released To The Student Interns?
answer: The payment will be released by the CAG of India upon completion of the internship period and submission of the report by the student intern.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: What Are The Attendance And Working Days For Student Interns?
answer: Student interns are expected to work during regular office hours and will not receive extra remuneration for working beyond office hours or on weekends/gazette holidays.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: Are Student Interns Entitled To Any Kind Of Leave?
answer: No, student interns are not entitled to any kind of leave.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: What Kind Of Logistics Support Will Be Provided To Student Interns?
answer: Student interns will be provided with necessary logistics support, including office space and a computer with internet facility.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: What Is The Requirement For Submission Of A Paper By Student Interns?
answer: Student interns are required to present a report/paper on the assigned subject to the concerned head of the functional wing/field office at the end of the internship.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: Is There A Feedback Process For Student Interns?
answer: Yes, student interns are mandated to provide feedback on their experience of the program to the head of the functional wing/field office.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: Will Student Interns Receive An Experience Certificate Or Recommendatory Letter?
answer: Yes, at the end of the internship, an experience certificate or recommendatory letter will be given to the student interns.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: Where Will The Student Interns Be Placed?
answer: The place of posting will be the CAG's office in New Delhi or any of the CAG's field offices across India.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: How Can Students Apply For The Internship?
answer: Students can download the prescribed application format from the CAG website (www.cag.gov.in) and forward it to trgwing@cag.gov.in via email before the specified deadline.

scheme_name: Student Internship Programme
question: What Is The Full Form Of CAG?
answer: CAG stands for Comptroller & Auditor General of India.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Programme (PRL)
question: Who can apply for the program?
answer: Indian students pursuing or recently graduated from UG/PG programs, and teachers with at least 5 years of experience.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Programme (PRL)
question: What disciplines are eligible?
answer: Disciplines like Optics, Laser Physics, Space Physics, Geology, Atmospheric Sciences, Chemistry, Ocean Sciences, and related fields.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Programme (PRL)
question: What is the duration of the internship?
answer: The internship lasts for 45 days.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Programme (PRL)
question: Is the internship paid?
answer: No, the internship is unpaid. However, limited paid accommodation is available for offline participants.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Programme (PRL)
question: Can non-Indian nationals apply?
answer: No, only Indian nationals are eligible for this internship.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Programme (PRL)
question: What is the selection process?
answer: Candidates must first contact a project supervisor, who will inform the Dean's office of the selection. Formal approval will follow.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Programme (PRL)
question: Can I choose an online project?
answer: The nature of the project will determine if the internship will be conducted online or offline.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Programme (PRL)
question: Is there accommodation available?
answer: Yes, limited accommodation is available at ₹100 per day, provided on a first-come, first-served basis.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Programme (PRL)
question: What happens after selection?
answer: Selected candidates will be informed via email and must complete the formalities before starting the project.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Programme (PRL)
question: Is there any evaluation at the end of the program?
answer: Yes, students must give a final seminar and submit a project report certified by their project guide.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Programme (PRL)
question: What happens if I miss days during the internship?
answer: Absence without prior permission can lead to termination of the internship.

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: What is the aim of this scheme?
answer: This scheme aims to impart high-end research training in frontier areas of Science and Technology, which are of interest to India by providing an opportunity to visit leading institutions/universities across the globe for a period of 02-06 months.

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: What is the objective of the Scheme?
answer: The following are the objectives of the scheme: | To build national capacity in frontier areas of Science and Technology by providing opportunities for International R&D experience by SIRE fellows. | To tap the expertise gained by SIRE fellows to strengthen/initiate national programmes in their domain knowledge. | To encourage research activities in priority areas which are still less explored in Indian context.

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: Which is the implementing agency of this scheme?
answer: Science and Engineering Research Board, Government of India

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: Can I avail SIRE fellowship multiple times?
answer: No, any applicant is eligible to avail this fellowship only once in his / her career.

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: Can I apply for only one month visit?
answer: No. The duration of the proposed visit must be within 02-6 months.

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: Can I use SIRE fellowship to visit other nearby institutions during my stay in the proposed country?
answer: No, SIRE fellowship must be utilized only for the purpose for which it has been sanctioned.

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: Will flight cancellation / rescheduling charges or extra baggage charges be considered under SIRE fellowship?
answer: No. SERB will not provide any type of cancellation / rescheduling charges or extra baggage charges.

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: I am 41 years old. Can I avail SIRE fellowship?
answer: The maximum age limit to apply under SIRE programme is 40 years. However, SC/ST/OBC and Women candidates will be given age relaxation of 5 years, provided, the applicant has submitted the valid category proof.

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: What, if I have provided any incorrect/misleading information or breach of terms and conditions?
answer: Fellowship will be cancelled and given support will be withdrawn at any stage. SERB has all the rights to take any action in consultation with the applicant's parent organization / university / institute etc. including refund of entire amount spent on the SIRE Fellow along with the interest thereon to SERB.

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: I have an ongoing SERB project under CRG/SRG. Am I eligible to apply under SIRE?
answer: Yes.

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: I have availed ITS support of SERB this year / last year. Am I eligible to apply under SIRE?
answer: Yes.

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: I have done my Ph.D. from abroad. Am I eligible to apply?
answer: No. Only those candidates who have completed their Ph.D. from India are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: Are INSPIRE Faculty / Ramanujan Fellow eligible to apply under SIRE?
answer: No.

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: Is tenure track faculty position qualify as permanent position and are they eligible to apply under SIRE?
answer: Yes, however, the institution must endorse the tenure track faculty as permanent faculty.

scheme_name: SERB International Research Experience
question: How can I submit the application form under the scheme?
answer: The application for consideration under the SERB International Research Experience (SIRE) Program can be submitted through the SERB online portal www.serbonline.in only when the call for proposal in made.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Scheme Of DGFT
question: Is There A Requirement For Interns To Sign A Declaration Of Secrecy?
answer: Yes, interns are required to provide a declaration of secrecy to the Directorate before starting their internship.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Scheme Of DGFT
question: Are There Any Preferences Or Reservations For Certain Candidates?
answer: Candidates pursuing or having post-graduation in Economics, Finance, Management, or Law will be given preference during the selection process.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Scheme Of DGFT
question: What Is The Purpose Of The Summer Internship Scheme Offered By The Directorate General Of Foreign Trade (DGFT)?
answer: The internship aims to facilitate interaction between DGFT officers and young scholars/researchers, allowing for the exchange of ideas and critical analysis to improve the Directorate's activities. It also provides interns with valuable career advancement opportunities.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Scheme Of DGFT
question: Where Will The Internship Be Conducted?
answer: The internship will take place at the DGFT headquarters in New Delhi, where interns will be attached to the heads of different divisions and report directly to them.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Scheme Of DGFT
question: Will Interns Receive Any Remuneration For Their Work?
answer: Interns will receive a consolidated token remuneration of Rs.10,000 per month for the duration of their internship.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Scheme Of DGFT
question: Is There A Possibility Of Future Employment With DGFT After The Internship?
answer: Interns should note that they are not considered employees of DGFT, and there is no assurance of any future employment with the organization.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Scheme Of DGFT
question: Will Interns Receive Any Logistical Support During The Internship?
answer: Yes, necessary logistical support will be provided to interns to meet the functional requirements of their internship.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Scheme Of DGFT
question: What Is The Requirement At The End Of The Internship?
answer: Interns will be expected to submit a report or paper summarizing their work and experience during the internship to the Head of the respective Division.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Scheme Of DGFT
question: Will Interns Receive A Certificate Upon Completion Of The Internship?
answer: Yes, interns who successfully complete their internship and submit their report/paper for evaluation will be issued a certificate by the Head of the concerned Division.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Scheme Of DGFT
question: How Should Interested Students Apply For The Internship?
answer: Interested students can submit their applications via email, including scanned copies of their application and CV, to internship-dgft@gov.in.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Scheme Of DGFT
question: How Will Selected Candidates Be Notified?
answer: Selected candidates will receive the internship offer via email.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Scheme Of DGFT
question: Are There Any Additional Documents Required For The Application?
answer: Candidates interested in joining the internship during their coursework need to provide a permission letter from their Supervisor/Head of Department.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Scheme Of DGFT
question: Can Interns Present Their Work At Academic Bodies, Seminars, Or Conferences?
answer: Interns may present their work with prior permission from the Department; however, they must ensure that no confidential information is disclosed.

scheme_name: Summer Internship Scheme Of DGFT
question: How Should Interns Conduct Themselves During The Internship?
answer: Interns are expected to maintain professional conduct in their relationship with the Department and the public in general, adhering to the Code of Conduct provided by the Department.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship of Students to DRDO Labs/Estts for Project Training
question: What is the objective of this internship scheme?
answer: The main objective is to provide prospective graduates and postgraduates exposure to DRDO's state-of-the-art research and development activities in defence technologies.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship of Students to DRDO Labs/Estts for Project Training
question: Who is eligible to apply for this internship?
answer: Students pursuing undergraduate or postgraduate degrees in Engineering or General Sciences are eligible.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship of Students to DRDO Labs/Estts for Project Training
question: Is there any restriction on the type of labs the interns can access?
answer: Yes, interns will be permitted access only to UNCLASSIFIED areas of DRDO Labs/Establishments.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship of Students to DRDO Labs/Estts for Project Training
question: What is the duration of the internship?
answer: The internship duration generally ranges from 4 weeks to 6 months, depending on the course and at the discretion of the concerned Lab Director.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship of Students to DRDO Labs/Estts for Project Training
question: Can the internship duration be extended?
answer: Any extension is subject to approval by the Lab Director and availability of resources.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship of Students to DRDO Labs/Estts for Project Training
question: How can a student apply for the DRDO internship?
answer: Students can apply through their institutes or colleges by directly corresponding with the concerned DRDO laboratories or establishments aligned with their academic discipline.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship of Students to DRDO Labs/Estts for Project Training
question: Can students apply directly to DRDO HQ for internships?
answer: No, students must apply directly to the relevant DRDO Lab/Estt and not to DRDO HQ.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship of Students to DRDO Labs/Estts for Project Training
question: Is there any financial compensation offered during the internship?
answer: There is no mention of stipend or compensation. Additionally, DRDO shall not be liable for any compensation in case of personal injury during the internship.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship of Students to DRDO Labs/Estts for Project Training
question: Is the internship offered under the Apprentices Act, 1961
answer: No, the Apprentices Act, 1961 does not apply to this internship scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship of Students to DRDO Labs/Estts for Project Training
question: Does this internship guarantee a job at DRDO?
answer: No, DRDO is under no obligation to offer employment after the completion of the internship.

scheme_name: Scheme of Internship of Students to DRDO Labs/Estts for Project Training
question: What disciplines are accepted for this internship?
answer: Students from Engineering and General Sciences disciplines are considered for internship opportunities.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: What is Startup India Seed Fund Scheme?
answer: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) provides financial assistance to startups for proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market-entry, and commercialization. Eligible startups can apply for the scheme on the Startup India portal. The Seed Fund will be disbursed to selected startups through eligible incubators across India.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: What is the eligibility criteria for incubators to apply for SISFS?
answer: Any Indian incubator operational for at least two years (for Government-supported incubators) and for three years (for incubators non-supported by Government) on the date of application can apply to the scheme.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: What is the quantum of funds offered by the scheme to a selected incubator?
answer: A Grant of up to ₹ 5 (five) crore would be provided to a selected incubator in milestone-based three (or) more installments. The exact quantum of grant and instalments for each incubator will be decided by the Experts Advisory Committee (EAC) based on its evaluation.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: Is there a Management Fee provisioned in the scheme for selected incubators?
answer: Yes, a component of Management Fee @ 5% of Seed Fund grant to the incubator will be provisioned (i.e. if an incubator is granted ₹1 crore of Seed Fund, then by including management fee @ 5%, the total assistance would be ₹1.050 crore). The Management Fee will be utilized for administrative expenditure, selection and due diligence of startups, and monitoring of progress of beneficiary startups. The Management Fee provisioned for incubators shall not be used by the incubator for facility creation or any other administrative expenses. As Installments of the Grant are released to incubators, proportionate Management fee shall also be released with each installment.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: What can the incubator use this Grant of up to ₹ 5 Cr. for?
answer: Incubators shall use the grant for disbursal of seed fund to eligible startups as follows: | - Up to ₹20 Lakhs as grant for validation of Proof of Concept, or prototype development, or product trials. The grant shall be disbursed in milestone-based installments. These milestones can be related to development of prototype, product testing, building a product ready for market launch, etc. | - Up to ₹50 Lakhs of investment for market entry, commercialization, or scaling up through convertible debentures or debt or debt-linked instruments. | - Not more than 20% of the total grant to an incubator shall be given as grants to startups by incubator. | - A startup applicant can avail seed support in the form of grant and debt/convertible debentures each once as per the guidelines of the scheme. | Incubators shall not use the grant for facility creation or any other expenses. A component of Management Fee @ 5% of Seed Fund grant to the incubator will be provisioned (i.e. if an incubator is granted ₹ 1 crore of Seed Fund, then by including management fee @ 5%, the total assistance would be ₹ 1.050 crore). The Management Fee will be utilized for administrative expenditure, selection and due diligence of startups, and monitoring of progress of beneficiary startups. The Management Fee provisioned for incubators shall not be used by the incubator for facility creation or any other administrative expenses.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: How much time does the incubator have to disburse the entire sanctioned fund to startups?
answer: The grant should be utilized fully by the incubator within a period of three years from the date of receipt of the first installment of funds. If the Incubator has not utilized at least 50% of the total commitment within the first 2 years, then the Incubator will not be eligible for any further drawdowns. It will return all unutilized funds along with interest.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: What are my responsibilities under this scheme?
answer: The incubators shall be responsible for providing physical infrastructure to the selected startups for regular functioning, support for testing and validating ideas, mentoring for prototype or product development or commercialization, and developing capacities in finance, human resources, legal compliances, and other functions. They are also expected to provide networking with investors and opportunities for showcasing in various national and international events. If the selected startup does not want to utilize the physical infrastructure of the incubator, the incubator shall offer all other resources and services to the startup.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: What is the ISMC?
answer: Each of the incubators applying for the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme will constitute a committee called the Incubator Seed Management Committee (ISMC), consisting of experts who can evaluate and select startups for seed support. The composition of ISMC would be as follows: | - Nominee of Incubator (Chairman) | - Representative from State Government's Startup Nodal Team | - Representative of a Venture Capital Fund or Angel Network | - A domain expert from Industry | - A domain expert from academia | - Two successful Entrepreneurs | - Any other relevant Stakeholder | The final composition and members of ISMC of each incubator shall be approved by EAC and will be a critical parameter in selection of incubators.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: I am not able to find relevant members for ISMC. Can Startup India or EAC help me find members?
answer: Startup India or EAC shall not be directly involved in constituting the members of ISMC at each incubator. It is the responsibility of the selected incubator to constitute the ISMC.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: How can I apply to SISFS?
answer: An online call for applications is hosted on an ongoing basis on the Startup India portal at https://www.startupindia.gov.in

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: Is the SISFS application process completely online?
answer: The application submission is completely online, and no physical submission of documents is required.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: Is there a fee for applying to this scheme?
answer: There are no application fees for the scheme. Even after the selection of a startup by an incubator for assistance under this scheme, the startup shall not be charged any fees. The incubator or any of its staff members shall not charge any fee in cash or in kind from applicants or beneficiaries under the scheme for any process of selection, disbursement, incubation, or monitoring.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: Do I need to have a pool of startups ready to fund when I apply for the scheme?
answer: No. A central Call for Applications for startups will be hosted by DPIIT on Startup India portal. Applicants can apply for seed fund to any three incubators selected as disbursing partners for this scheme in order of their preference. All applications received will be shared online with respective incubators for further evaluation.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: Is the information provided by me in the application form kept Confidential?
answer: We maintain confidentiality of all the proposals we receive under the scheme. Your application is only shared with the EAC for the purpose of evaluation and monitoring.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: Is the information provided by me in the application form kept confidential?
answer: We maintain confidentiality of all the proposals we receive under the scheme. Your application is only shared with the incubators you apply to for the purpose of evaluation, and with the EAC for the purpose of monitoring.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: Can I apply to the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme again after receiving a rejection?
answer: Yes, you can apply to the SISFS again after 3 months of receiving a rejection. This buffer time is given to ensure that you have worked on the feedback received from incubators and are ready to be considered again.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: Who is going to review my application?
answer: An Experts Advisory Committee (EAC) has been constituted by DPIIT will evaluate and select incubators for allotment of Seed Funds, monitor progress, and take all necessary measures for efficient utilization of funds towards the fulfilment of objectives of the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: What are the evaluation criteria for the SISFS?
answer: Incubators shall be selected based on the following parameters: | - Fulfillment of eligibility criteria | - Quality of the team of Incubator | - Available infrastructure, testing labs etc. | - Composition of ISMC | - Incubation support provided by incubator in last three years: | - No. of startups incubated | - No. of startups graduated, i.e. progressed from one stage of business development cycle to the next | - No. of startups that raised follow on investments | - No. of startups that crossed a revenue of Rs 1 Cr in last 1 year | - 2-year survival rate of startups from the date of joining incubator | - Funding support extended to incubatees in last three years: | - Investment agreements signed between incubator and startups | - No. of startups invested in | - Total corpus allocated to incubatees | - Total investments raised by incubatees from external sources | - Mentoring provided to incubatees in last three years: | - No. of mentors hired | - Average mentoring hours allocated per startup per month | - No. of IP (patents, copyrights, designs, and trademarks) registered by incubatees | - Other support extended to incubatees in last three years: | - Industry/Corporate connects | - Events held for stakeholder engagements | - Participation in other events | - Number of startups that the incubator intends to support | - Quantum of funds applied for, along with fund deployment plan with timelines | - Any other relevant parameters that decided by the EAC

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: What is the process of evaluation?
answer: The Call for Applications for incubators will be open online throughout the year. Experts Advisory Committee (EAC) will convene at least quarterly to: | - Evaluate the applications received during the period | - Select incubators for funds under the Scheme | - Decide the total amount of fund and number of installments in which it is to be allocated to each incubator | - Specify milestones to be achieved by each incubator for release of installments

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: How much time will it take for my application to get processed?
answer: The Call for Applications for incubators will be open online throughout the year. Experts Advisory Committee (EAC) will convene at least quarterly to evaluate the applications received during the period, select incubators for funds under the Scheme and, decide the total amount of fund and number of installments in which it is to be allocated to each incubator.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: How can I track the status of my application?
answer: Once the incubator has submitted its seed fund scheme application, they will get access to their respective dashboard. The dashboard can be accessed using their login credential to check the real-time application status.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: I have been selected for seed fund, but the terms and conditions being set by the EAC are not agreeable to me. What should I do?
answer: Features of the scheme, as mentioned in Guidelines on https://dipp.gov.in/sites/default/files/Guidelines-FundScheme-Startup-29January2021.pdf, are non-negotiable. Any other terms, such as quantum of fund, quantum of each tranche, or milestones, are to be negotiated between the EAC and the incubator only. If a selected incubator chooses to not participate in the scheme for any reason, they can communicate the same to DPIIT and the EAC.

scheme_name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
question: What is the process of fund disbursement to be followed by incubators after getting selected by the EAC?
answer: After approval by EAC, the following actionables must be completed before release of first instalment:- | Before issuance of Sanction Order to Incubator from DPIIT (through email):- | - To open a Trust and Retention Account in any Nationalized Bank by the Incubator and share the ECS mandate form signed by the bank in prescribed format | - To share details on Public Financial Management System (PFMS) | a. For Incubators already registered on PFMS: To share Unique PFMS Agency Code | b. For Incubators not registered on PFMS: To share following information - | i. Type of registration: | ii.
