answer: Broken periods of imprisonment are totaled up to compute the qualifying period.

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme
question: How is the period of undertrial counted in calculating the qualifying period for pension eligibility?
answer: In the case of a trial ending in conviction, the undertrial period is counted towards the actual imprisonment suffered.

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme
question: What is the significance of the period of normal remission in imprisonment calculations?
answer: Up to one month of normal remission is treated as part of actual imprisonment.

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme
question: How is "imprisonment" defined under the scheme?
answer: Detention under the orders of the competent authority is considered as imprisonment.

scheme_name: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research
question: What is the aim of this programme?
answer: The aim of the programme is to provide advanced training in India and abroad to medical and health research personnel in cutting-edge research areas related to medicine and health to create trained human resources for carrying out advanced research activities.

scheme_name: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research
question: What is the objective of the programme?
answer: The objective of the scheme is to increase the overall availability of trained personnel for health research from medical colleges across the country through scholarships & fellowships for young medical doctors to take up medical and health research as a career.

scheme_name: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research
question: Which is the implementing agency of this programme?
answer: Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India

scheme_name: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research
question: What are the areas of research?
answer: Toxicology, Genomics, Proteomics, Geriatrics, Stem cell research, Clinical Trials, Good Clinical Practices (GCP), Good Laboratory Practices (GLP), Quality Control (QC) and Quality Assurance (QA), Modern Biology, Biotechnology, Genetics, Drugs Chemistry, Operational Research, Health Informatics, Medical Ethics, Disease Modelling, Health Economics, Environmental Health, Mental Health/Clinical Psychology, Any other area recommended by the committee as per National Health Policy/ National Health Goals.

scheme_name: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research
question: Who are eligible to apply?
answer: The Indian citizens holding M.D./ M.S./ M.D.S. or MBBS/BDS/ MVSc./ M.Sc./M.Pharma/M.Tech or equivalent with Ph.D. in health/biomedical research and working in Indian institutes are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research
question: How many years of experience do faculty need to apply under the programme?
answer: The faculty having at least three years' experience in the college/institute as a regular employee.

scheme_name: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research
question: What is the age limit to apply under the programme?
answer: The candidates up to 55 years of age as of the last date of receipt of application will be eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research
question: What is the duration of fellowship?
answer: The duration of fellowship is 1-3 months.

scheme_name: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research
question: What is the amount of fellowship given to the fellows in Indian institutes?
answer: A consolidated stipend of ₹40,000/- per month for a period of stay in the host institute, which is at a different station from the parent Institute. In case, the training is at the same station, the rate of stipend payable will be ₹20,000/- per month.

scheme_name: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research
question: How much contingency grant is given to the fellows in Indian institutes?
answer: One-time contingency grant of ₹20,000/- (maximum) to meet the expenses of local taxi charges, attending meetings, etc.

scheme_name: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research
question: What is the amount of fellowship given to the fellows in Foreign institutes?
answer: A consolidated stipend of US $ 3000/- per month (or equivalent in other foreign currency) for the period of stay in the host institute abroad.

scheme_name: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research
question: How much contingency grant is given to the fellows in Foreign institutes?
answer: One-time contingency grant of ₹30,000 (maximum) to meet the expenses of local taxi charges visa fee and Health insurance, attending meetings, etc., and ₹20,000/- for attending progress review meetings at DHR.

scheme_name: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research
question: How can an applicant apply under the programme?
answer: The full-length research proposals may be submitted online only and no proposal in physical/hard copy is to be submitted w.r.t. the advertisements published in leading newspapers and uploaded on the websites of DHR & ICMR. https://dhrschemes.icmr.org.in/

scheme_name: Stand-Up India
question: What is the nature and size of the loan under the Stand-Up India Scheme?
answer: Composite loan (inclusive of term loan and working capital) between 10 lakh and up to 100 lakh representing up to 85% of the project cost would be eligible.

scheme_name: Stand-Up India
question: How much will be the interest rate for the loan?
answer: The rate of interest would be lowest applicable rate of the bank for that category (rating category) not to exceed (base rate (MCLR) + 3%+ tenor premium).

scheme_name: Stand-Up India
question: By when am I expected to repay the loan?
answer: The loan is repayable in 7 years with a maximum moratorium period of 18 months.

scheme_name: Stand-Up India
question: Who are the eligible lending institutions for extending loans under the Scheme?
answer: All branches of Scheduled Commercial Banks located across the country.

scheme_name: Stand-Up India
question: What is Hand-holding Support?
answer: Any new entrepreneur requires guidance in his endeavor to set up his or her business enterprise starting from training to filling up loan applications as per bank requirements.

scheme_name: Stand-Up India
question: How do I get hand-holding support?
answer: You may navigate through the portal or seek assistance from the nearest branch of a Scheduled Commercial Bank to help you identify the nature of hand-holding support required.

scheme_name: Stand-Up India
question: What are the activities for which Stand-Up India loan is provided ?
answer: Stand-Up India loan may be provided to entrepreneurs for engaging in manufacturing, trading, services sectors including activities allied to agriculture.

scheme_name: Stand-Up India
question: What are the activities allied to agriculture ?
answer: Under the Stand Up India loan, activities allied to agriculture include pisciculture, beekeeping, poultry, livestock, rearing, grading, sorting, aggregation agro-industries, dairy, fishery, agri-clinic and agri-business centres, food and agro processing etc.

scheme_name: Stand-Up India
question: What is the purpose of the loan under "Stand-Up India" Scheme?
answer: The scheme is for setting up a new enterprise in manufacturing, trading, services sector or activities allied to agriculture by SC/ST and Women entrepreneur.

scheme_name: Stand-Up India
question: What is the Difference between Stand-Up India Scheme and Start Up India Scheme?
answer: Stand-Up India Scheme is intended to support SC/ST and Women entrepreneurs to set up green field projects through bank branches in India while Start Up India Scheme aims to boost innovative and technology led enterprises for new/existing enterprises.

scheme_name: Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan Yojana
question: What Is The Primary Aim Of SUMAN Yojana?
answer: This scheme aims to stabilise population, ensuring optimal maternal and child health and family planning.

scheme_name: Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan Yojana
question: Is SUMAN Yojana Applicable For Every Woman?
answer: Yes, SUMAN Yojana is applicable for every pregnant woman. They have to register themselves in a civil hospital.

scheme_name: Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan Yojana
question: What Is Infant Mortality Rate?
answer: Infant mortality rate (IMR) is the number of deaths per 1,000 live births of children under one year of age. The rate for a given region is the number of children dying under one year of age, divided by the number of live births during the year, multiplied by 1,000

scheme_name: Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan Yojana
question: What Is The Maternal Mortality Rate?
answer: Maternal mortality refers to deaths due to complications from pregnancy or childbirth. The maternal mortality ratio (MMR) is defined as the number of maternal deaths during a given time period per 100,000 live births during the same time period.

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector
question: What is the objective of the scheme?
answer: The scheme aims to enhance skill development capacity in the Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector and provide industry-relevant training to students and unemployed youth.

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector
question: Who can apply under this scheme?
answer: Students studying from Class 9 onwards and unemployed youth, including school dropouts, ITI certificate holders, diploma holders, and non-engineering graduates, can apply.

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector
question: Is there any financial assistance provided for course fees?
answer: Yes, 75% of the course fee is provided as assistance, and the remaining 25% is to be paid by the student.

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector
question: Are there any benefits for SC/ST or Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)?
answer: Yes, 100% of the course fee is provided for SC/ST and EWS candidates, subject to eligibility criteria.

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector
question: Is there any reservation under the scheme?
answer: Yes, 40% of the seats are reserved for candidates belonging to SC/ST/EWS categories.

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector
question: When is the financial assistance provided?
answer: Financial assistance is provided only after the candidate successfully clears the certification examination.

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector
question: Which certification bodies are recognized under the scheme?
answer: Certification is conducted by the National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT), Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), or bodies recognised by SSCs.

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector
question: Are examination fees covered under the scheme?
answer: Yes, 100% of the registration-cum-certification fee, including examination fees (theory, practical, and project evaluation), is reimbursed for candidates appearing for the first time.

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector
question: Is registration with an employment exchange mandatory?
answer: Yes, unemployed youth applying under the scheme should be registered with employment exchanges.

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector
question: What type of training is provided under the scheme?
answer: The scheme provides skill development training in the Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector through recognized institutions and training partners.

scheme_name: Swami Vivekananda Single Girl Child Fellowship for Research in Social Sciences
question: What is the Selection Procedure once a student has successfully applied for the scholarship?
answer: I. The fellowship will be awarded on the basis of the recommendation of the Expert Committee constituted by the Commission. The decision of the Commission will be final. Result shall be published on the UGC website. Award letters can be downloaded from UGC online application portal. | ii. If the Fellow is availing any other fellowship/ project from any organization at the time of selection, she shall be required to surrender one award. | iii. The Commission reserves the right to withdraw/cancel the award without assigning any reason.

scheme_name: Swami Vivekananda Single Girl Child Fellowship for Research in Social Sciences
question: When can the successful candidate Join The Fellowship?
answer: The candidate should join the fellowship within 3 months from the date of issue of the Award letter, failing which the award will be treated as canceled.

scheme_name: Swami Vivekananda Single Girl Child Fellowship for Research in Social Sciences
question: How will the progress of the candidate be monitored?
answer: On the progress of research work, the research fellow shall submit a yearly progress report duly signed by Guide and forwarded by HOD and Registrar/Principal/Director of the concerned institution to the identified agency

scheme_name: Swami Vivekananda Single Girl Child Fellowship for Research in Social Sciences
question: Can the fellow Accept Any Other Fellowship Or Hold Any Appointment?
answer: The fellow who is awarded Swami Vivekananda Fellowship for Single Girl Child for research in Social Sciences will not accept any other fellowship or hold any appointment, paid or otherwise, or receive any emoluments, salary, stipend, etc. from any other source during the tenure of the award (except in case of academic leave of one year).

scheme_name: Swami Vivekananda Single Girl Child Fellowship for Research in Social Sciences
question: What is the procedure if the Fellow Desirous Of Leaving The Research Mid-Way?
answer: The fellow desirous of leaving the research mid-way without completing research degree will have to submit her resignation duly forwarded by the concerned University/College/Institute to the designated agency under intimation to UGC office. The grant will be released upto the date of resignation tendered by the fellow.

scheme_name: Swami Vivekananda Single Girl Child Fellowship for Research in Social Sciences
question: Under what conditions can UGC cancel the fellowship of the candidate?
answer: UGC may terminate fellowship of any candidate in case of : | i. If the fellow is found to be ineligible to receive the fellowship, at any point of time during the entire duration of the fellowship. | ii. Any false information furnished by the applicant. | iii. Misconduct of fellow. | iv. Unsatisfactory progress of research work of the fellow. | v. Any other fellowship/scholarship is drawn from other source(s) during the tenure of the fellowship.

scheme_name: Shahari Waqf Sampatti Vikas Yojana
question: What is the primary objective of scheme?
answer: The scheme aims to protect vacant waqf land from encroachers and develop economically viable projects on these properties to generate more income and expand welfare activities.

scheme_name: Shahari Waqf Sampatti Vikas Yojana
question: Who implements the scheme?
answer: The Central Waqf Council (CWC) is the implementing agency for this scheme.

scheme_name: Shahari Waqf Sampatti Vikas Yojana
question: What types of projects are eligible for interest-free loans under scheme?
answer: Projects involving the construction or reconstruction of economically viable buildings on waqf lands, such as commercial complexes, marriage halls, hospitals, and cold storage facilities, are eligible.

scheme_name: Shahari Waqf Sampatti Vikas Yojana
question: Who can apply for the interest-free loan?
answer: All Waqf Boards (WBs) and registered waqf institutions that are in full possession of the property to be developed and are not insolvent are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Shahari Waqf Sampatti Vikas Yojana
question: Is there a geographical limitation for the projects?
answer: Yes, the waqf property to be developed must be situated in an urban area.

scheme_name: Shahari Waqf Sampatti Vikas Yojana
question: What is considered an 'urban area' under SWSVY?
answer: An urban area is defined as any area within the jurisdiction of a municipality, municipal corporation, notified area committee, town area committee, town committee, or any area within 8 kilometers from such jurisdictions, as specified by the government.

scheme_name: Shahari Waqf Sampatti Vikas Yojana
question: What is the maximum loan amount available under scheme?
answer: The maximum interest-free loan provided is ₹2.00 crore or 75% of the estimated project cost (excluding the value of the land), whichever is less.

scheme_name: Shahari Waqf Sampatti Vikas Yojana
question: Are there any provisions for grants-in-aid under the scheme?
answer: Yes, as a special case, grants-in-aid may be provided to State Waqf Boards or waqf institutions for social development projects on waqf land, with prior approval from the Ministry.

scheme_name: Shahari Waqf Sampatti Vikas Yojana
question: How can an agency apply for a loan?
answer: The agency must apply to the concerned Waqf Board using the prescribed application form, providing all necessary details and supporting documents.

scheme_name: Shahari Waqf Sampatti Vikas Yojana
question: Where can one obtain the application form?
answer: The application form can be downloaded from the official website of the Central Waqf Council or obtained from the relevant Waqf Board office. https://centralwaqfcouncil.gov.in/content/forms

scheme_name: Shahari Waqf Sampatti Vikas Yojana
question: To whom should the completed application be submitted?
answer: Completed applications should be submitted to: | To, | The Secretary, | Central Waqf Council, | Central Waqf Bhawan, | P-13 & 14, Sector-6, Pushp Vihar, | Opposite Family Court, Saket, | New Delhi - 110017.

scheme_name: Shahari Waqf Sampatti Vikas Yojana
question: Are there any penalties for defaulting on loan repayment?
answer: Yes, failure to repay the loan as per the agreed terms may result in penalties, including legal action as deemed appropriate by the Central Waqf Council.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: I am having a DST funded Project as a Co-PI, can I apply for TARE scheme?
answer: Researchers being part of another project as Co-PIs, can apply.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: In case of selection, is it mandatory to divide the funding and share 50% each to host and parent institutions? Can it be given to only host institution?
answer: Yes. A research fellowship of ₹60,000/- per year (in addition to the researcher's own salary) will be provided subject to completion of a minimum 90 days of research work per year in the host institution. Research grant of ₹5 lakhs per annum (50% each to host and parent institution) and overheads will be provided.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: What kind of management responsibilities does the parent institution get?
answer: Parent institute must undertake all project implementation related work including purchase, preparation of UC/ES, relieving PI for research work in the host institute, etc. as of any other funded projects.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Clarification on the term "Research work", whether it refers to fresh research work only or ongoing research work without any external grant or fund?
answer: Fresh and ongoing research work not supported by any externally funded individual centric projects.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Can I choose Panjab University as Host institution for TARE because Panjab University is not a central university nor state university?
answer: Only central institutes / national research labs and Central Universities are eligible as host institute.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: I want to understand the meaning of clause "The applicant(s) must hold a regular academic / research position in State Universities/ Colleges and private Academic Institution"?
answer: The term "Regular" in the context of SERB refers to the applicants who are appointed against the sanctioned post or in a tenure post but are likely to be renewed after the end of the tenure. | [Note: Research Associates, Ad-hoc faculties, Guest Faculty, Visiting Scientist, consultant, Project Fellows and Faculty members whose contract is renewed every year are not eligible] (In cases where it is not covered in any of the above, SERB has the right to determine the eligibility)

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Working day: 90 days attendance should include host institute working days attendance only or 90 days working in host institute during institutes working days, summer vacation, winter vacation, public holidays, Saturdays and Sundays?
answer: 90 days working in host institute includes, working days, summer vacation, winter vacation, public holidays, Saturdays and Sundays, provided host institute allows to work and issue attendance certificate by the end of the year.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Is there any limit on how old institute is affiliated for Eg.10 year, 20 year or so?
answer: Age of the institute will not be considered, as long as it is affiliated by UGC / AICTE / MCI or other competent organizations of Government of India / State Governments.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: What is the maximum distance between parent and host institute?
answer: Distance is not fixed, you need to justify the reasons for selection of institute whatso ever the distance, which will be evaluated by the committee. PI are advised to find the expertise/mentor nearer to their parent institute. Preference may be given to the candidates proposing host institute nearer to parent institute.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: How many candidates can a mentor can guide?
answer: A mentor can forward any number of applications, but only one candidate will be allowed to work with a mentor depending up on the merit of the proposal.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: How many applications can an institute forward?
answer: There are no fixed numbers.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Is the mentor and applicant subject areas should match exactly?
answer: The basic concept of this project itself is to execute the project in collaborative mode where the expertise of the mentor should be useful in executing the project work of the applicant. Accordingly, the expertise of mentor and applicant should fulfil the requirements of the proposed project work.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Can I get age relaxation, over and above the relaxation given in the program for filing the application?
answer: The upper age limit for the award is 45 years at the time of the submission of application. Age relaxation of 5 (five) years will be given to candidates belonging to SC/ST/OBC/Physically Challenged & Women candidates.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Is 90 days attendance compulsory requirement to get the fellowship money sanctioned? Can project be granted without the fellowship component?
answer: The basic concept of this project itself is to execute the project in collaborative mode where the applicant should work with the mentor and get trained at higher level. For which the minimum attendance period of 90 days is mandatory and hence the proposals without fellowship component will not be considered.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: If the applicant goes to the host institution less than 90 days/year and does not get the scholarship money of ₹60,000/year whether he/she will be eligible to get the project money?
answer: It is mandatory to full fill the minimum 90 days research work per year in the host institution.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: I have completed my M.Tech. and continuing my Ph.D. Can I apply for TARE project?
answer: No as per revised eligibility guidelines, only candidates holding Ph.D. degree in Science / Engineering or MS / MD in Medicine are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Can my Ph.D. supervisor be a mentor for TARE project?
answer: No, however candidates are allowed to work with a different mentor from the same institute where a Ph.D. degree was awarded.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Is only researcher having ongoing project with DST / SERB not eligible for apply or any ongoing projects?
answer: Researchers having any funded projects are not eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Can I apply from any other Central institutes other than mentioned in the TARE scheme? Eg.Centre for Materials for Electronics Technology (C-MET), Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology?
answer: You can apply for any Central institutions having relevant R&D infrastructure.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Whether applications from the regions where very limited Central institutes are available will be given with privilege or not?
answer: Selection for TARE scheme will be purely competitive mode based on the scientific merit of the proposal.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Any clauses that bound for publication of research work findings in conferences / journals?
answer: No, but PI are expected to bring out joint publications with the mentor from the results emanated out of this project and is mandatory to acknowledge SERB funding for the research work.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Can I use the money to hire a project fellow? Can the fellow be paid 50/50 by both institutions?
answer: No, the TARE awardee is expected to do research on his / her own.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: If I succeed in getting the TARE grant, can I apply for, say, an extramural grant later?
answer: Applicant should not hold any ongoing research projects or any fellowship at the time of submission of application. You are not eligible to avail of any other project from DST/SERB until you complete the TARE project.

scheme_name: Technology Development Fund (TDF) Scheme
question: What is Technology Development Fund (TDF) scheme?
answer: Technology Development Fund (TDF) has been established to promote self-reliance in Defence Technology as a part of the 'Make in India' initiative. It is a programme of the Ministry of Defence.

scheme_name: Technology Development Fund (TDF) Scheme
question: Which department has launched this scheme?
answer: Ministry of Defence has launched this scheme.

scheme_name: Technology Development Fund (TDF) Scheme
question: How is MSME defined for the purpose of the TDF Program ?
answer: MSME is defined as per the MSMED Act 2006 for the purpose of the Technology Development Fund Scheme.

scheme_name: Technology Development Fund (TDF) Scheme
question: Is this Scheme specific to any sector ?
answer: Yes (Defence and Aerospace).

scheme_name: Technology Development Fund (TDF) Scheme
question: Can an organisation apply in multiple TDF Projects simultaneously at the same time ?
answer: Yes.

scheme_name: Technology Development Fund (TDF) Scheme
question: What is the nature of the proposals to be supported under TDF Scheme ?
answer: A) Significant up-gradation/improvements/ further developments in the existing products/process/application etc. | b) Technology readiness level up-gradation from TRL3 onwards to realization of products as per Tri-Services requirements. | c) Development of futuristic technologies/innovative products which can be useful for the defence applications. | d) Import substitution of components whose technologies does not exist with the Indian industry.

scheme_name: Technology Development Fund (TDF) Scheme

scheme_name: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes
question: Is this specific pool of concessional finance exclusively intended for entrepreneurs belonging to the Scheduled Castes, or are other social categories also eligible?
answer: Entrepreneurs belonging only to the Scheduled Castes are eligible for assistance under this fund. Entrepreneurs from Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, or the General category are not eligible.

scheme_name: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes
question: Once financial assistance has been sanctioned and disbursed to my company, is there a mandatory requirement regarding the continuity of the Scheduled Caste shareholding structure?
answer: Yes, the aggregate shareholding of Scheduled Caste shareholders must be maintained at a minimum of 51% of the total shareholding of the company throughout the entire period the assistance remains in the company.

scheme_name: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes
question: What are the special ownership and managerial requirements for a company to be officially designated and considered as being owned by a Scheduled Caste woman entrepreneur?
answer: The Scheduled Caste woman entrepreneur should hold at least 51% of the shareholding in the company. Additionally, she must also serve as the Managing Director of the Company.

scheme_name: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes
question: If I have partners who are not from the target population, what is the minimum aggregate shareholding requirement that Scheduled Caste promoters must collectively maintain in the company?
answer: The aggregate shareholding of Scheduled Caste shareholders must be at least 51% of the total shareholding of the company. This group must also maintain management control of the company.

scheme_name: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes
question: What criteria apply if I have a technology-oriented innovative project that is currently receiving support from various recognized national incubation centers?
answer: The innovative project must be supported by incubation centers at Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), National Institutes of Technology (NITs), Premier Business Schools, or Universities. The project needs to show good potential for commercialization and must be at the implementation stage.

scheme_name: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes
question: What are the eligible business sectors and mandatory nature of the project being set up to qualify for financing under this scheme?
answer: The projects or units must be set up in the manufacturing, services, and allied sectors, including start-ups. It is mandatory that the project ensures the creation of assets out of the funds deployed in the unit.

scheme_name: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes
question: If I am a disabled entrepreneur seeking financial assistance, which specific government guidelines will be utilized to determine my official qualification status as disabled?
answer: In the case of disabled entrepreneurs, the qualification guidelines issued by the Department of Divyang Welfare will be followed to determine if they qualify as disabled for the purpose of the fund.

scheme_name: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes
question: Can a newly incorporated Private or Public Limited Company, which succeeded a Proprietary Firm or Limited Liability Partnership, qualify for funding?
answer: Yes, a new company can be eligible if it is a successor entity of a Proprietary Firm, Partnership Firm, One Person Company (OPC), or Limited Liability Partnership. The predecessor entity must have had a sound business model, be in operation for over 6 or 12 months, and have had at least 51% Scheduled Caste shareholding with management control.

scheme_name: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes
question: For companies seeking assistance up to ₹50,00,000/-, what is the mandatory minimum period for which the Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs must have maintained 51% shareholding with management control?
answer: For assistance up to ₹50,00,000/-, the company must have had at least 51% shareholding by Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs with management control for the past 6 months.

scheme_name: Vice Chancellor Internship Scheme
question: What is the duration of the internship?
answer: Summer internships are 8 weeks long with 15-20 flexible hours per week. Regular internships during the academic session are 8-10 hours per week, with a maximum duration of six months.

scheme_name: Vice Chancellor Internship Scheme
question: How many interns are selected per session?
answer: The total proposed number of interns is 200, subject to periodic review and approval.

scheme_name: Vice Chancellor Internship Scheme
question: What are the working hours for interns?
answer: Summer internships: 15-20 hours per week. Regular internships: 8-10 hours per week.

scheme_name: Vice Chancellor Internship Scheme
question: Is this internship considered employment?
answer: No, this internship is not employment nor an assurance of employment with the university.

scheme_name: Vice Chancellor Internship Scheme
question: What happens if I perform unsatisfactorily during the internship?
answer: Unsatisfactory performance may lead to discontinuation of the internship.

scheme_name: Vice Chancellor Internship Scheme
question: Can I terminate the internship early?
answer: Yes, interns can terminate the internship with prior notice.

scheme_name: Vice Chancellor Internship Scheme
question: Will the university provide accommodation?
answer: No, interns need to make their own accommodation arrangements.

scheme_name: Vice Chancellor Internship Scheme
question: What is the selection process?
answer: Based on assessment and interaction with the selection committee, comprising members nominated by the Vice-Chancellor.

scheme_name: Vice Chancellor Internship Scheme
question: Where will the selected interns be placed?
answer: In various departments/centers/institutes, including the Vice Chancellor's Office, Central Reference Library, Examination Branch, etc.

scheme_name: Vice Chancellor Internship Scheme
question: What kind of tasks will I be doing?
answer: Tasks include data collection, document streamlining, content creation, research, and community engagement.

scheme_name: Vice Chancellor Internship Scheme
question: Can I apply if I have already done an internship under VCIS?
answer: No, a student can avail of VCIS only once during their course of study at the University of Delhi.

scheme_name: Vikaas-Day Care Scheme For Person with Disability Children
question: What is Vikaas Day care scheme?
answer: Vikaas scheme aims at setting up Vikaas Centres for welfare of PwDs.

scheme_name: Vikaas-Day Care Scheme For Person with Disability Children
question: Which department has launched this scheme?
answer: Vikaas Day Care Scheme was launched by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.

scheme_name: Vikaas-Day Care Scheme For Person with Disability Children
question: What are the main benefits of this scheme?
answer: Vikaas Centre/Registered Organization(RO) should provide facilities to the PwD like day care,staffing, infrastructure,assessment and evaluation etc.

scheme_name: Vikaas-Day Care Scheme For Person with Disability Children
question: From where the PwD can get the facilities?
answer: PwD can avail the benefits from Vikaas Centre or Registered Organisation.

scheme_name: Vikaas-Day Care Scheme For Person with Disability Children
question: What is the main purpose of the scheme?
answer: This is a day care scheme, primarily for enhancing interpersonal and vocational skills of the children.

scheme_name: Vikaas-Day Care Scheme For Person with Disability Children
question: How this scheme is also beneficial to the family of the PwD?
answer: This scheme also helps in supporting family members of the PwDs to get some time during the day to fulfil other responsibilities.

scheme_name: Vikaas-Day Care Scheme For Person with Disability Children
question: Who will be covered under this scheme?

scheme_name: Vikaas-Day Care Scheme For Person with Disability Children
question: What is the enrolment process of the of PwD at the Vikaas Centre?

scheme_name: Vikaas-Day Care Scheme For Person with Disability Children
question: What are the documents required for the enrolment?
answer: - Enrolment form. | - Birth certificate or Date of Birth proof of the PwD. | - Disability certificate. | - BPL certificate or Income certificate of Parents or Guardian issued by competent authority as authorized by the concerned State/ Union Territory (for LIG or BPL family). | - ID proof of parent or guardian. | - Residence (Local) proof (Mandatory in case of LIG parent or guardian for parents of PwD availing transport facility). | - Declaration proof of the guardianship if PwD 18 years of age and parents are not the guardians.

scheme_name: Vikaas-Day Care Scheme For Person with Disability Children
question: May the beneficiary also get the benefits of other scheme?
answer: PwD should not be simultaneously enrolled under Samarth or Gharaunda scheme.

scheme_name: Vocational Education and Training Loan Scheme

answer: The candidate should attain a minimum age of 18 years upon completion of the course. The upper age limit is up to 50 years.

scheme_name: Vocational Education and Training Loan Scheme
question: What are the expenses to be considered for Vocational Education and Training Course?

scheme_name: Vocational Education and Training Loan Scheme
question: In how much time will the loan have to be repaid?
answer: The loan will have to be repaid for up to 7 years.

scheme_name: Vocational Education and Training Loan Scheme
question: What is rate of interest of the loan?
answer: NSKFDC shall charge interest at 1% per annum from the channeling agency, which, in turn, shall charge 4% per annum from the beneficiaries. In the case of women, an interest rebate of 0.5% shall be provided.

scheme_name: Vocational Education and Training Loan Scheme
question: What is the course eligiblity?
answer: Vocational Education & Training courses of duration of minimum 6 months and upto 2 years run or supported by Ministry/Department/Organization of the Government or a Company/Society/Organization supported by a National Skill Development Corporation or State Skills/Mission/State Skill Corporations.

scheme_name: Vocational Education and Training Loan Scheme
question: What is the eligiblity criteria?
answer: The person should be from the target group of NSKFDC. | The person should have secured admission in a course run or supported by a Ministry/Deptt./Organization of the Government or a Company/Society/Organization supported by National Skill Development Corporation or State Skill Missions/State Skill Corporations, preferably leading to a Certificate/Diploma/Degree etc. Issued by a Government Organization or an Organization recognized/authorized by the Government to do so.

scheme_name: Vanchit Ikai Samooh Aur Vargon Ko Aarthik Sahayata Yojana
question: Q 1. Are SHGs That Are Availing Subsidy Under Any Other Scheme Eligible Under This Scheme?

scheme_name: Vanchit Ikai Samooh Aur Vargon Ko Aarthik Sahayata Yojana
question: Q 2. Are All SHGs Eligible For Interest Subvention Under VISVAS Scheme?

scheme_name: Vanchit Ikai Samooh Aur Vargon Ko Aarthik Sahayata Yojana
question: Q 3. What Are The Key Features Under The VISVAS Scheme?
answer: Ans. All SC/OBC individuals and Self Help Groups with annual family income up to Rs. 3.00 Lakh will be eligible for interest subvention @ 5% on loans up to Rs lakhs.

scheme_name: Vanchit Ikai Samooh Aur Vargon Ko Aarthik Sahayata Yojana
question: Q 4. What Does VISVAS In The Scheme Stand For?

scheme_name: Vanchit Ikai Samooh Aur Vargon Ko Aarthik Sahayata Yojana
question: What is the Maximum Loan Limit for SHGs?

scheme_name: Vanchit Ikai Samooh Aur Vargon Ko Aarthik Sahayata Yojana

scheme_name: Vanchit Ikai Samooh Aur Vargon Ko Aarthik Sahayata Yojana
question: What is the Maximum Subvention Amount for this scheme?

scheme_name: Vanchit Ikai Samooh Aur Vargon Ko Aarthik Sahayata Yojana
question: What shall be the Mode Of Payment Of the Subvention?
answer: The Mode of payment of the Subvention shall be Through Direct Transfer of Subvention Amount into operating account of SHG or Individual.

scheme_name: Virasat Loan Scheme of NMDFC
question: What is the Virasat Scheme, and who can apply for it?
answer: The Virasat Scheme supports artisans and craftspersons from minority communities by providing credit for working capital and fixed capital requirements, such as purchasing tools, machinery, and raw materials.

scheme_name: Virasat Loan Scheme of NMDFC
question: What is the maximum loan amount and interest rate under this scheme?
answer: Under both Credit Lines, artisans can avail up to Rs. 10.00 lakh. | Under Credit Line-1, interest rates are 5% for male beneficiaries and 4% for female beneficiaries. | Under Credit Line-2, interest rates are 6% for male beneficiaries and 5% for female beneficiaries.

scheme_name: Virasat Loan Scheme of NMDFC
question: What is the repayment period and moratorium?
answer: A six-month moratorium is allowed, followed by repayment over a period of five years.

scheme_name: Virasat Loan Scheme of NMDFC
question: What documents or proof of skill are required to apply?
answer: Applicants must provide proof of artisan status, such as an Artisan ID Card issued by the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts/Handlooms), certificate from local craft societies, or evidence of traditional occupation.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: What was the rationale behind initiation of the scheme?
answer: In addition to enhancement of the number of PhDs in Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM) and IT/IT Enabled Services (IT/ITES) sectors in the country the scheme aims to: | - Give thrust to R&D, create an innovative ecosystem and enhance India's competitiveness in these knowledge intensive sectors. | - Thrust on significantly increasing the number of PhDs in the country to enable India to compete globally in the coming decades, to develop an ecosystem of research, development and IP creation in these knowledge intensive sectors.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: How many PhD candidates will the scheme support?
answer: The scheme aims to support 1000 full-time PhD candidates.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: Which institutions are eligible to participate in the scheme?
answer: Please refer to https://phd.dic.gov.in/eligibility for eligibility.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: What are the eligibility criteria for PhD candidates?
answer: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme is an institutional scheme wherein eligible institutions submit proposals requesting Full-time PhD seats against an active call for proposal by Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme, DIC, MeitY. | - The call for proposal for Full-time PhD seats is notified by PhD Cell, DIC; MeitY through the web portal https://phd.dic.gov.in/ | - Proposals for allotment of Full-time PhD seats are to be submitted by eligible institutions only. Suitable number of seats would be allotted to institutions for further enrollment of PDF fellows on these seats following the scheme guidelines. | - The institutions with PhD seats, allotted under the scheme, would conduct their admission process for enrolment of candidates on those seats. | - The support will be for additional PhD candidates taken up by an institution. No support would be provided for current levels of enrolment in the PhD programme at the institutions. Transfer from other scholarship schemes would not be permitted. | - Candidates already availing financial support from other government schemes are not eligible.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: Can a candidate apply for this scheme if they have already started their PhD?
answer: No, the scheme applies only to new PhD scholars enrolled after the PhD seats are allocated to the eligible institutions.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: How are institutions allotted seats?
answer: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme is an institutional scheme wherein eligible institutions submit proposals requesting Full-time PhD seats against an active call for proposal by Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme, DIC, MeitY. | - The call for proposal for Full-time PhD seats is notified by PhD Cell, DIC; MeitY through the web portal https://phd.dic.gov.in/ | - Proposals for allotment of Full-time PhD seats are to be submitted by eligible institutions only. Suitable number of seats would be allotted to institutions for further enrollment of PDF fellows on these seats following the scheme guidelines and evaluation of the submitted proposals.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: What is the procedure for joining the PhD Scheme?
answer: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme is an institutional scheme where seats are allocated to eligible institutions for enrolment during particular academic year. The candidates, interested to join the scheme, need to contact respective institutions for admission formalities.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: What financial support is available for full-time PhD candidates?
answer: - Fellowship | - ₹38,750/- per month (1st & 2nd year) | - ₹43,750/- per month (3rd, 4th & 5th year) | - Reimbursement of Rent (RoR) | - Institutional Overheads of ₹25,000 per year per Full-time PhD candidate. | - Research contingency grant of ₹1,20,000 per year per Full-time PhD candidate. | - Support up to ₹1.5 lakh for attending International Conferences. | - One-time support of ₹10.5 lakh for 250 selected PhD candidates for a 6-month visit to labs abroad.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: How will the funds be disbursed?
answer: - Fellowships and RoR will be transferred directly to candidates' bank accounts | - Institutional Overheads and Research Contingency Grants will be sent to the respective institutions.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: What is meant by Reimbursement of Rent (RoR)?
answer: This component is linked with the fellowship of PhD Candidate. The rate of RoR is 24%, 16% & 8% (of fellowship) for X, Y & Z class cities/towns respectively. The classification of the cities is as per the notification issued by the Ministry of Finance for HRA. | RoR the support is applicable to only those PhD candidates who are not availing hostel facility by the institution.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: What happens if a candidate drops out from the scheme?
answer: The institution has to immediately inform the PhD Cell, DIC and obtain an acknowledgement from PhD Cell. If not reported on time, the institution will be responsible for recovering any excess funds paid to the candidate.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: Can an institution transfer its PhD seats to another year if not filled?
answer: No, unfilled seats will be reallocated to the general pool and assigned to other institutions.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: Can the fellowship be extended beyond five years?
answer: No, the maximum duration of support is five years or until PhD completion, whichever is earlier.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: Is there any funding for laboratory equipment under the research contingency grant?
answer: Yes, institutions can apply for funding for research equipment under Research Contingency Grant, but civil construction/expansion costs are not covered.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: What is included under support for International Conference?
answer: This covers the travel and other expenses of a PhD candidate for attending an International conference, where the research paper has been accepted for oral (not poster) presentation. There is a list of renowned International Conferences related to the areas of ESDM and IT/ITES where the candidate can visit (https://phd.dic.gov.in/about/ListOfInternationalConferences.pdf)

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: Who can submit proposals for allotment of PDF seats?
answer: Only eligible institutions can submit proposals for allotment of PDF seats. Individual applicants cannot directly apply to PhD Cell, DIC, MeitY.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: What is the educational qualification required?
answer: The applicant must have obtained a PhD degree from a recognized University with first class (in terms of grades) in all preceding levels and a good academic record.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: Is there a time limit after PhD completion to apply?
answer: The PhD must have been completed within the last 5 years as of the last date of application submission to the institution.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: What is the maximum age limit for applicants?
answer: The upper age limit is 40 years on the date of application submission to the institution.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: Can the fellowship be availed in the same institution where the applicant earned their PhD?
answer: No. Applicants should not have completed their PhD from the same institution where the fellowship is to be undertaken.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: Will preference be given to any specific applicants?
answer: Yes. Preference will be given to applicants with active industry linkages and research proposals targeting industry-specific problems.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: Where can the fellowship be undertaken?
answer: The fellowship can be undertaken only in India at recognized and eligible academic or R&D institutions.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: What is the duration of the fellowship?
answer: It is awarded for one year initially, with the possibility of extension based on performance review.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: Can fellows hold another fellowship simultaneously?
answer: No. The PDF is a full-time assignment and fellows cannot receive any other fellowship from Government or Non-Government sources during its tenure.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: Can the fellowship be transferred to another institution?
answer: No. The fellowship is non-transferable and must be carried out at the same institution where the seat is allocated.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: How is Post-doctoral Fellowship (PDF) awarded?
answer: Proposals for allotment of PDF seats are to be submitted by eligible institutions only. Suitable no. of seats would be allotted to institutions for further enrollment of PDF fellows on these seats following the scheme guidelines.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: What is the main objective of the scheme?
answer: The objective is to increase the number of PhDs in ESDM and IT/ITES, encourage R&D, strengthen the innovation ecosystem, and enhance India's global competitiveness in these sectors.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: How many Part-Time PhD candidates will be supported under the scheme?
answer: A total of 150 part-time PhDs will be supported over 5 years.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: Are candidates already availing other government fellowships eligible?
answer: No, candidates availing any fellowship/scholarship from Central or State government schemes are not eligible.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: How are Part-Time PhD seats allocated to institutions?
answer: - The call for proposal for Part-time PhD seats is notified by PhD Cell, DIC; MeitY through the web portal https://phd.dic.gov.in/ | - Proposals for allotment of Part-time PhD seats are to be submitted by eligible institutions only. Suitable number of seats are allotted to institutions for further enrollment of Part-time PhD fellows on these seats following the scheme guidelines.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: Which institutions are eligible to participate in the scheme?
answer: Please refer to https://phd.dic.gov.in/eligibility for eligibility of institutions.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: What financial support do Part-Time PhD candidates receive?
answer: They receive a one-time incentive of ₹3,00,000 upon successful completion of their PhD degree and submission of completion documents to PhD Cell, DIC.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: Is the incentive given during the course of study?
answer: No, the incentive is disbursed only after successful completion of the PhD.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: Who disburses the incentive amount?
answer: The PhD Cell at Digital India Corporation (DIC), MeitY, disburses the incentive.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: On what grounds can support be terminated?
answer: Support can be terminated due to lack of progress, violation/non-compliance of scheme guidelines, or any other reason deemed appropriate by the PhD Cell, DIC.

scheme_name: Vocational Training in Tribal Areas
question: What is the objective of the scheme?
answer: Scheduled Tribes are the most marginalized section of the society, therefore to assist their socio-economic development; there is an imperative need to provide more employment avenues and income generation opportunities. It is aimed at upgrading the skills of the tribal youths in various traditional/modern vocations depending upon their educational qualification, present economic trends and the market potential, which would enable them to gain suitable employment or enable them to become self-employed.

scheme_name: Vocational Training in Tribal Areas
question: Which is the implementing agency of this scheme?
answer: Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India

scheme_name: Vocational Training in Tribal Areas
question: Is it a Central Sector Scheme?
answer: Yes, this is a Central Sector Scheme.

scheme_name: Vocational Training in Tribal Areas
question: What is the benefit given under the scheme?
answer: Under the scheme of Vocational Training, grants will be provided for organizing vocational trainings in recognized institutes or in Vocational Training Centres (VTCs) subject to terms and conditions revised from time to time of the scheme.

scheme_name: Vocational Training in Tribal Areas
question: Which are the agencies eligible for grants?
answer: (i) State Governments and UT Administrations; (ii) Institutions or Organisations set up by Government as autonomous bodies, either under a statue, or as a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860; (iii) Educational and other institutions (iv) A Public Trust registered under any law for the time being in force. (v) Any Private Recognized Institution, registered and conducting such vocational courses for at least three years. (vi) Any industry or an association of industries like ASSOCHAM, CII, FICCI, etc. (vii) Voluntary Organization (VO)/Non-Government Organisations (NGOs)

scheme_name: Vocational Training in Tribal Areas
question: What is the eligibility condition for a Public Trust?
answer: A Public Trust registered under any law for the time being in force. The trust must have been registered for at least three years.

scheme_name: Vocational Training in Tribal Areas
question: Who are the target beneficiaries under the scheme?
answer: The scheme will be implemented for the benefit of the Scheduled Tribes as well as PTGs and can be taken up anywhere in the country but priority will be given to remote tribal areas, areas inhabited by particularly vulnerable tribes and areas affected by extremist activities.

scheme_name: Vocational Training in Tribal Areas
question: Which type of institutions will get preference under the scheme?
answer: Preference will be given to those institutions which guarantee placement/employment after completion of training

scheme_name: Vocational Training in Tribal Areas
question: Is there any reservation for tribal girl candidates?
answer: Yes, as far as possible, minimum 33% seats will be reserved for tribal girl candidates.

scheme_name: Vocational Training in Tribal Areas
question: What are the two ways the funding under this scheme?
answer: (i) By setting up and running VTCs mainly in remote areas/rural areas deficient in facilities, (ii) To support vocational training in existing recognized institutes in other areas

scheme_name: Vocational Training in Tribal Areas
question: How to apply under the scheme?
answer: State/UT Governments and State owned autonomous institutions shall apply in prescribed application Format-I, whereas VOs/NGOs/private institutions shall apply in Format-II. Further, the State/UT Government/State owned institutions shall apply directly to the Ministry, whereas application of VOs/NGOs/private institutions shall be routed through "State Level Committee for Voluntary Efforts" as constituted under the scheme of Grant-in-aid to Voluntary Organizations.

scheme_name: Women Helpline
question: What is Women Helpline?
answer: Women Helpline under Sambal component of Mission Shakti intends to provide toll-free 24x7 emergency and non-emergency response to women affected by violence and other distress. It facilitates referral services, linking them with appropriate authorities such as the police, One Stop Centre, and hospitals. Additionally, it provides information about government schemes and programs for women across the country through a single uniform number.

scheme_name: Women Helpline
question: Who can call the Women Helpline?
answer: Any woman in distress or facing difficult circumstances, or someone calling on her behalf, can contact the Women Helpline for assistance.

scheme_name: Women Helpline
question: How can I contact the Women Helpline?
answer: The Women Helpline can be contacted through a single universal toll-free number across the country, which is 181. Individuals can call this number for assistance, information, or support.

scheme_name: Women Helpline
question: What services does the Women Helpline provide?
answer: The Women Helpline provides a range of services including emergency assistance through ERSS, information on government schemes, non-emergency assistance through OSCs and other institutions for legal support, psycho-social counselling, and empowerment initiatives.

scheme_name: Women Helpline
question: Can I remain anonymous when contacting the Women Helpline?
answer: Yes, you can choose to remain anonymous when contacting the Women Helpline. However, providing some basic information may help the call operators better assist you, especially in emergency situations.

scheme_name: Women Helpline
question: Are the services provided by the Women Helpline confidential?
answer: Yes, the services provided by the Women Helpline are confidential. Your privacy is respected, and information shared during the call is kept confidential unless there is a need to involve authorities for your safety and well-being.

scheme_name: Women Helpline
question: How is the Women Helpline integrated with other helplines and institutions?

scheme_name: Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers
question: Is there a specific format or template for applicants to use when completing the application, and what does this format entail?
answer: Yes, applicants are required to use the prescribed format for the application. This format outlines the necessary fields and details that applicants need to provide when submitting their application.

scheme_name: Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers
question: What measures are taken to maintain fairness and integrity in the application and subsidy process, and how does the Coffee Board address attempts to influence this process?
answer: The Coffee Board enforces strict measures to maintain the integrity of the application and subsidy process. It rejects applications from individuals who attempt to influence the process through offers, rewards, gifts, or coercion, whether directly or indirectly. Additionally, legal action is initiated against those who wilfully furnish incorrect information, engage in misrepresentation, or suppress information to obtain subsidy benefits.

scheme_name: Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers
question: Is there room for flexibility in the terms and conditions of this scheme, and under what circumstances might they be amended?
answer: Yes, the Coffee Board retains the authority to amend or modify the terms and conditions of the scheme as it deems necessary for the efficient execution of the scheme and the fulfillment of its objectives. Any changes made are intended to ensure that the scheme operates effectively.

scheme_name: Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers
question: Could you elucidate further on the handling of funds for this scheme and how it impacts the allocation of educational incentives?
answer: The availability of funds during a particular year plays a crucial role in determining the release of eligible amounts to the applicants. The scheme operates within the constraints of the funds allocated for that year.

scheme_name: Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers
question: Can you specify the documentation required when applying for these educational incentives, and how does each document contribute to the application process?
answer: Applicants need to provide a set of documents, including the duly filled application form with attached recent photographs, a self-attested Identity card (Student identity card and Aadhaar), a self-attested marks sheet of the previous class/year, a self-attested copy of the SC/ST caste certificate issued by a competent state government authority, a certificate from the owners or authorized individuals of the plantation/curing works in which the parent(s) are employed, and a certificate from the Principal of the college where the student is currently enrolled during the academic year.

scheme_name: Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers
question: What is the procedure for interested applicants to avail of these incentives, and could you outline the necessary steps?
answer: To avail of the incentives, interested and eligible applicants should follow a three-step process. First, they need to take a printout of the prescribed application form. Then, they should fill in all mandatory fields, paste a passport-sized photograph, and attach copies of the required documents, self-attesting them if necessary. Finally, they should submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to the Coffee Board.

scheme_name: Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers
question: Are there specific courses or fields of study under Professional courses that receive Financial Assistance, and if so, what is the extent of this support?
answer: Yes, Professional courses such as Medical Sciences, Engineering, Agriculture, Pharmacy, Nursing, and other equivalent professional degree courses are covered under this scheme. Students pursuing these courses receive Financial Assistance of ₹7,500 per student.

scheme_name: Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers
question: Could you elaborate on the Financial Assistance provided for Post-Graduation in traditional courses and how it benefits students?
answer: Post-Graduation students in traditional courses are eligible for Financial Assistance amounting to ₹7,500 per student, which aids in funding their higher education pursuits.

scheme_name: Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers
question: What amount of Financial Assistance is allocated for students pursuing Graduation in traditional courses, and how does this support their education?
answer: Students pursuing Graduation in traditional courses, including Arts, Science, and Commerce, receive Financial Assistance of ₹3,750 per student. This financial support aids them in their academic endeavors.

scheme_name: Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers
question: How does the Incentive Award work, and what are the additional sums provided for boys and girls?
answer: Students eligible for the Educational Stipend are also considered for the Incentive Award based on their academic merit. Boys receive an additional ₹1,000, while girls receive an additional ₹1,500 on top of the Educational Stipend.

scheme_name: Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers
question: Could you provide more information about the recognized educational institutions that are eligible for this scheme?
answer: The scheme stipulates that the educational institution where the student is enrolled must be recognized by either the Central or State Governments, ensuring that the educational standards are in accordance with the established norms.

scheme_name: Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers
question: Are there any exclusions in terms of occupation when considering eligibility for these educational benefits?
answer: Yes, certain occupational categories such as Clerks, Drivers, Supervisors, and Estate/Curing Works Managers are not entitled to the educational benefits offered by this scheme.

scheme_name: Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers
question: What criteria determine the eligibility of children for this scheme, and how many children of SC/ST labourers can benefit from it?
answer: To be eligible for this scheme, the children must be the offspring of SC/ST labourers engaged in coffee plantations and Licensed Coffee Curing Works. The first two surviving children of these labourers are eligible, with additional support extended to twins or multiple births if they meet individual merit requirements.

scheme_name: Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers
question: Can you elaborate on the primary objective of the "Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers" scheme and the specific educational support it provides to children of SC/ST labourers?
answer: The primary aim of the "Welfare Measures for Children of Labourers" scheme is to provide comprehensive educational support to the children of Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe (SC/ST) labourers employed in coffee plantations and Licensed Coffee Curing Works. This support includes educational stipends, incentives for academic excellence, and financial assistance for higher education, thereby enhancing the educational prospects of these children.
